report.title: Tide Rolls Into Baton Rouge: Alabama Takes On Death Valley
report.byline: Mary-Kathryn 'MK' Strickland · Alabama Insider · Week 10
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Roll Tide, and I mean that as a greeting. Mostly. I'm Mary-Kathryn Strickland, but everyone from the Quad to the press box calls me MK. I rode for the Tide equestrian team, I read blitz pickups the way some girls read Southern Living, and I can quote a legendary coaching maxim for every situation, perfectly, usually at dinner. My family has asked me to stop. I will not stop. I travel with this Alabama team and I live with it, and every week you'll get the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines with a little Tuscaloosa swagger. When we win, you'll hear "Roll Tide" in seventeen different tones, each more satisfied than the last. When we lose, I'll say "We will not speak of it," and I will not speak of it.

The School in 60 Seconds
Alabama claims 18 national championships, 13 of them wire-service titles from the poll era. Paul "Bear" Bryant won six from 1958 to 1982, and Nick Saban won six more between 2007 and 2023. The Tide's Heisman winners are Mark Ingram II (2009), Derrick Henry (2015), DeVonta Smith (2020) and Bryce Young (2021). Alabama has 30 SEC championships, an NCAA-record 79 bowl appearances and 46 bowl wins, also a record, plus a record 16 straight 10-win seasons from 2008 through 2023. Bryant-Denny Stadium seats 101,821 and opened in 1929. Coach Bryant has a maxim for this, and I'll save it for dinner.

The Coach and the Scheme
Kalen DeBoer was hired Jan. 12, 2024, and his first two Tide teams went 9-4 and 11-4.

We've played 8 games, and we're putting up 38.2 points a game while giving up 21.2.

Players to Know
QB Keelon Russell: 148 of 221, 2,057 yards, 15 touchdowns, 5 interceptions.
RB Daniel Hill: 332 yards on 71 carries, 4 touchdowns.
WR Lotzeir Brooks: 29 catches, 488 yards, 1 touchdown.
LB Yhonzae Pierre: 3.5 sacks, the team lead.
LB Caleb Woodson: a team-high 63 tackles.

The Conference Picture
Alabama is 6-2 overall and 4-2 in league play. ESPN's standings have Alabama 3rd in the SEC.
The season so far: W 48-10 vs East Carolina Pirates (Sept. 5), W 45-17 at Kentucky Wildcats (Sept. 12), W 50-36 vs Florida State Seminoles (Sept. 19), W 49-18 vs South Carolina Gamecocks (Sept. 26), W 56-23 at Mississippi State Bulldogs (Oct. 3), L 17-20 vs Georgia Bulldogs (Oct. 10), L 10-26 at Tennessee Volunteers (Oct. 17), W 31-20 vs Texas A&M Aggies (Oct. 24).

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides
We travel to No. 15 LSU (6-2, 3-2 SEC) on Saturday, Nov. 7, at 3:30 p.m. ET, at Tiger Stadium (LA), Baton Rouge, Louisiana, on ABC. We come in ranked No. 9.
Last time out. We beat the Texas A&M Aggies 31-20 at home on Oct. 24. Keelon Russell went 19 of 30 for 311 yards, with 3 touchdowns, Daniel Hill ran 9 times for 36 yards and Rico Scott caught 6 balls for 156 yards.
LSU beat the Auburn Tigers 38-17 on the road on Oct. 24. Sam Leavitt went 32 of 45 for 388 yards, with 3 touchdowns; Dilin Jones ran 21 times for 91 yards and 1 touchdown; Jackson Harris caught 9 balls for 178 yards and 2 touchdowns.
Players to watch. LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt is 180 of 256 for 2,173 yards, with 17 touchdowns and 8 interceptions. Dilin Jones leads their ground game with 657 yards on 149 carries and 6 scores. Jackson Harris is their top target: 36 catches for 634 yards. On defense, linebacker TJ Dottery has 58 tackles and defensive end Princewill Umanmielen has 8.5 sacks.
The series. CFBD has 10 regular-season meetings with LSU from 2016 through 2025. We won 5 of them, and LSU won the last one 20-9 in 2025.
Availability. Nothing official on injuries yet for Alabama vs. LSU. When Alabama or LSU puts out a real report, you'll hear it from me, not a rumor.

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
We roll into Baton Rouge on a Saturday when LSU's Mike's Kids Club Tailgate fills the Fan Zone outside the PMAC, which means the next generation of Tiger fans will be screaming at us, too.

report.title: Hogs on the Plains: Arkansas Takes Its Fight to Jordan-Hare
report.byline: Bubba Fayette-Dorsey · Arkansas Insider · Week 10
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Woooo, Pig, here comes the data! I'm Bubba Fayette-Dorsey, and I'm your Arkansas insider. I'm a grade-school science teacher from up in the Ozarks, and I call the Hogs before every stat, even the bad ones. On the podcast, my segment is called Hog Call: I call the Hogs, then I read the stat. My rules are simple. I keep it clean and kind, I celebrate Arkansas players as people, I respect every opponent, and I never invent a stat, a quote or a fact. If I can't source it, no Arkansas fan hears it from me.

The School in 60 Seconds
Home is Razorback Stadium in Fayetteville, built in 1938 with a listed capacity of 80,000. The playing surface is Frank Broyles Field, the band is the Best in Sight and Sound, and the fight song is "Arkansas Fight." The program claims a national title from 1964. The last five seasons went 9-4, 7-6, 4-8, 7-6 and 2-10, from 2021 through 2025. And if you visit, ask somebody about Calling the Hogs. It's the tradition I'd show you first.

The Coach and the Scheme
Ryan Silverfield became the 35th head coach in Arkansas history, and CollegeFootballData dates the hire to Nov. 30, 2025. He coached Memphis against Missouri in 2023.

The 8-game numbers: 19.6 points per game scored, 27.6 allowed.

Players to Know
QB KJ Jackson: 151 of 249, 1,673 yards, 7 touchdowns, 5 interceptions.
RB Sutton Smith: 217 yards on 63 carries, 1 touchdown.
WR Chris Marshall: 43 catches, 633 yards, 2 touchdowns.
DL Quincy Rhodes Jr.: 3 sacks, the team lead.
LB Ja'Quavion Smith: a team-high 53 tackles.

The Conference Picture

The season so far: W 31-14 vs North Alabama Lions (Sept. 5), L 10-43 at Utah Utes (Sept. 12), L 17-45 vs Georgia Bulldogs (Sept. 19), W 34-6 vs Tulsa Golden Hurricane (Sept. 26), L 7-34 at Texas A&M Aggies (Oct. 3), L 17-24 vs Tennessee Volunteers (Oct. 10), W 31-21 at Vanderbilt Commodores (Oct. 17), L 10-34 vs Missouri Tigers (Oct. 31).

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides
We travel to Auburn (4-4, 2-4 SEC) on Saturday, Nov. 7, at 12:45 p.m. ET, at Jordan-Hare Stadium, Auburn, Alabama, on SEC Network.
Last time out. We lost to the Missouri Tigers 34-10 at home on Oct. 31. KJ Jackson went 20 of 34 for 229 yards, Cam Settles ran 12 times for 38 yards and Antonio Jordan caught 7 balls for 106 yards.
Auburn lost to the Ole Miss Rebels 45-15 on the road on Oct. 31. Byrum Brown went 25 of 38 for 195 yards, with 1 touchdown; Jeremiah Cobb ran 7 times for 35 yards; Chas Nimrod caught 4 balls for 62 yards and 1 touchdown.
Players to watch. Auburn quarterback Byrum Brown is 159 of 247 for 1,560 yards, with 9 touchdowns and 7 interceptions. Byrum Brown leads their ground game with 484 yards on 139 carries and 7 scores. Keshaun Singleton is their top target: 39 catches for 433 yards. On defense, linebacker Elijah Melendez has 63 tackles and linebacker Elijah Melendez has 4 sacks.
The series. CFBD has 10 regular-season meetings with Auburn from 2016 through 2025. We won 7 of them, and we won the last one 33-24 in 2025.
Availability. No official availability report for Arkansas or Auburn was in the public data I checked, so nobody gets ruled in or out here.
From the preview booth. I shared the mic this week with Lacey Bellamy, Auburn's insider. Here's what I said:
"Woo Pig Sooie. We are here. We are hungry. We are 3-5 and we do not care."
And the last word from Lacey: "Our crowd is going to be standing for the veterans. Then it will be loud all day."

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
We walk into Jordan-Hare on Auburn's Military Appreciation day, with the home crowd dressed in navy, and a road crowd like that is exactly what this team needs to play angry.

report.text:

When we win, I roll an imaginary oak in imaginary toilet paper and shriek "War Eagle!" When we lose, I sip my lemonade with great dignity and say "We'll be back" to absolutely everybody. report.title: Cats Crash Homecoming: Kentucky Takes On Rocky Top
report.byline: Rhett Abernathy-Coyle · Kentucky Insider · Week 10
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Pedigree tells. Good evening, friends, I'm Rhett Abernathy-Coyle. I grew up on a horse farm out past Keeneland, mucking stalls before school and watching yearlings run in the morning mist. I learned early that you can tell a great deal about a horse from its bloodlines, and I grade football players the same way a Derby breeder grades a foal. I travel with the Wildcats and I live with the Wildcats, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, with a Southern gentleman's flourish. When we win, you'll hear my best Derby announcer: "And down the stretch they come!" When we lose, I'll say, "Even the best horses stumble," and adjust my hat. Now, pull up a chair, and let's talk bloodlines.

The School in 60 Seconds
The Wildcats represent the University of Kentucky in the SEC. Home is Kroger Field in Lexington, opened in 1973 and listed at 61,000 seats. The last five seasons: a fine 10-3 in 2021, then 7-6, 7-6, 4-8 and 5-7.

The Coach and the Scheme
Will Stein is our first-year head coach; CFBD dates his hire to Dec. 1, 2025.

The 8-game numbers: 32.9 points per game scored, 24.8 allowed.

report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Hotty Toddy, and hand me the footnotes. Good evening, gentle readers. I am Langston Fairbanks, a man of seersucker and iced tea, a student of literature who has read every word Mr. Faulkner wrote and every snap the Rebels have played this season, often on the same afternoon in the Grove. I travel with this Ole Miss team and I live with it, and every week I will bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines. Be warned: my takes tend to run three paragraphs. I can't help it. Football, like a good novel, deserves a proper beginning, middle and end. But I always land on a hard number. When we win, I recite a celebratory monologue under the nearest chandelier. When we lose, I murmur, "The past is never dead," and sip my iced tea in silence.

The School in 60 Seconds
The Rebels represent the University of Mississippi, which everyone calls Ole Miss, and play in the SEC. The program was founded in 1893 and has won six SEC titles: 1947, 1954, 1955, 1960, 1962 and 1963. Ole Miss has been recognized as national champion three times by major selectors. Home is Vaught-Hemingway Stadium on campus, opened in 1915 and listed at 64,038 seats. And the recent chapters read like an epic: 10-3, 8-5, 11-2, 10-3, and last year a 13-2 season that AP describes as a playoff team. Since 2023, the Rebels are 25-1 at home.

The Coach and the Scheme

report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
(banjo: plink-a-plink-plink.) Cue the banjo. Howdy, Big Orange Country, I'm Earl Haskew, but everybody on Cumberland Avenue calls me Rocky Top. I was a long snapper for the Vols, which means I spent four years looking at the world upside down and backward, and honestly it gave me a great perspective on defensive fronts. I travel with this team and live with this team, and before every stat I play a little banjo intro. Sometimes the banjo's out of tune on purpose. You'll know when. Every week you'll get the players, the matchups, the history and a few checkerboard metaphors from a fella who loves the end zones at Neyland more than his own front porch. When we win, I play "Rocky Top" until somebody stops me, and nobody ever does. When we lose, I play it slow and sad. Pull up a rocking chair.

The School in 60 Seconds
(plink.) Tennessee started playing football in 1891. The Vols claim six national titles, including two from the wire-service polls in 1951 and 1998, and 16 conference championships. We rank fifth all-time in bowl appearances, 55 of them, with four Sugar Bowls, three Cotton Bowls, two Orange Bowls, a Fiesta and a Peach among the wins. Neyland Stadium is the cathedral, and the Vols have won 485 games there, the most any program has won in its current home. Capacity is listed at 101,915 by one source and 102,455 by CFBD, so I'll just say "a whole lot of orange" and show you both. Josh Heupel's teams have gone 11-2, 9-4, 10-3 and 8-5 since 2022.

Heupel was hired Jan. 27, 2021.

report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Good afternoon, class! Oh, sorry. Old habits. Welcome, Illini Nation. I'm Margery Vandermolen, your Illinois insider, and I explain football the way your best-loved teacher explained long division: patiently, cheerfully and with a lot of charts. I'm a prairie-state numbers whiz. I've crunched the numbers on just about everything, and the numbers always say the same thing: orange. You'll get corn jokes from me. You'll get chart jokes. Sometimes you'll get a corn chart, which is both. And every Saturday morning I'll ask you the same question: "Orange you glad it's Saturday?" When something wonderful happens on the field, there's only one thing to say: "Oskee-wow-wow!" Each week I'll give you the players, the coaches and the matchup, explained clearly enough that Grandma and the grandkids can both follow along.

The School in 60 Seconds
Here's your history lesson, and yes, it will be on the test. Illinois is a founding member of the Big Ten and claims five national championships: 1914, 1919, 1923, 1927 and 1951. The 1923 title team opened Memorial Stadium and introduced the world to Harold "Red" Grange, the Galloping Ghost. On Oct. 18, 1924, at the stadium's dedication game, Grange scored four touchdowns against Michigan in the first 12 minutes. He ran for a fifth and threw for a sixth in a 39-14 win. ESPN once chose the legendary No. 77 as the greatest player in college football history. The stadium honors University of Illinois students who died in World War I. Illinois also claims 15 Big Ten titles. High fives all around.

The Coach and the Scheme
Bret Bielema was named the 26th head coach in Illinois history on Dec. 19, 2020. He's an Illinois native. One of his early wins was a nine-overtime victory at Penn State in 2021, the longest game in college football history.

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Well hello, Hoosier Nation, and welcome! I'm Mallory Penhallow, former Miss Monroe County runner-up, and these days I run a 40-tab efficiency model on everything this football team does. I travel with the team, I live with the numbers, and yes, the clicker is rhinestone. My pageant answer to every question is the same: "It's the explosives, people." Each week I give one opponent my honorary Miss Congeniality sash. It goes to whoever I roast the hardest, and I always keep it clean. When we win, you get the full pageant wave. When we lose, it's "grace in defeat," and then I quietly open tab 41.

The School in 60 Seconds
Before Curt Cignetti showed up, Indiana had the most losses of any program in college football, 713 of them over 130-plus years. It had won three bowl games in its whole history, and the last one came in 1991. Then 2025 happened. The Hoosiers went 16-0 and beat Miami 27-21 at Hard Rock Stadium on Jan. 19, 2026, to win their first national championship. The last team to win 16 games without a loss was Yale in 1894. Quarterback Fernando Mendoza won the Heisman, and he scored the deciding touchdown himself on a 12-yard run on fourth-and-4. Cignetti's quote still sounds like an acceptance speech to me: "We won the national championship at Indiana University. It can be done."

The Coach and the Scheme

The School in 60 Seconds

report.title: Gold in the Cold: Minnesota Hosts UCLA

report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Well, hello there. I'm Torvald Engebretsen, Tor to my friends, and I'm your Minnesota insider. I grew up in Minneapolis ice-fishing with my grandpa, and I know the history of every rivalry trophy this program plays for. Minnesota has more trophies than I have winter coats, and I have a lot of winter coats.

I'm dry, I'm earnest and I'm polite, but get me started on rivalry lore and I'm unstoppable. Here's my promise: every number in this report has a source. If I don't know something about Minnesota, I'll tell you so. I celebrate our players as young people first, I respect every opponent, even the ones from south of the border, and I thank God for crisp autumn Saturdays. Cold enough for ya? Good.

The School in 60 Seconds
Minnesota started playing football in 1882 and has been in the Big Ten since the league began in 1896 as the Western Conference. The Golden Gophers claim seven national championships. Four of them, in 1936, 1940, 1941 and 1960, came from the major wire-service polls. Since 2009, home has been Huntington Bank Stadium in Minneapolis. CFBD lists 50,850 seats.

The last five seasons have been sturdy: 9-4, 9-4, 6-7, 8-5 and 8-5. Four winning seasons in five years. My grandpa would call that a good catch.

The Coach and the Scheme
P.J. Fleck has led Minnesota since 2017. CFBD lists his Minnesota hire date as Jan. 6, 2017. He coached Western Michigan from 2013 to 2016. He played receiver at Northern Illinois and spent time with the San Francisco 49ers. He was a receivers coach at Northern Illinois, Rutgers and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. In 2019 he led the Gophers to one of their best seasons in half a century.

Through 8 games this season, Minnesota is scoring 25.2 points per game and allowing 20.5.

Players to Know

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides
We host No. 5 UCLA (8-0, 5-0 Big Ten) on Saturday, Nov. 7, at noon ET, at Huntington Bank Stadium, Minneapolis, Minnesota, on Fox.
Last time out. We lost to the Indiana Hoosiers 23-16 (OT) on the road on Oct. 31. Drake Lindsey went 20 of 37 for 120 yards, with 1 touchdown, TJ Thomas ran 6 times for 54 yards and Javon Tracy caught 7 balls for 40 yards.
UCLA beat the Nevada Wolf Pack 27-0 at home on Oct. 31. Ty Dieffenbach went 16 of 30 for 178 yards, with 1 touchdown; Wayne Knight ran 11 times for 53 yards; Jalen Saint Paul caught 3 balls for 52 yards.
Players to watch. UCLA quarterback Nico Iamaleava is 72 of 116 for 982 yards, with 4 touchdowns and 4 interceptions. Wayne Knight leads their ground game with 680 yards on 110 carries and 12 scores. Semaj Morgan is their top target: 36 catches for 415 yards. On defense, linebacker Jalen Woods has 62 tackles and linebacker Sammy Omosigho has 5.5 sacks.
The series. CFBD has one regular-season meeting with UCLA from 2016 through 2025, and UCLA won the last one 21-17 in 2024.

From the preview booth. I shared the mic this week with Kenzie Rhee, UCLA's insider. Here's what I said:
"Cut to the scoreboard in 2024. Minnesota 21, UCLA 17. I remember that one. I remember it the way I remember a walleye that was this big. Every year it gets a little bigger."
"Thank you. I practice it on the ice."
"That is the first honest thing you have said all day. Nothing to lose is the best way to play. We are 5-3, we have a home crowd, and we have Maverick Baranowski with 60 tackles waiting for Knight at the hole like a pike under the ice."
And the last word from Kenzie: "Final scene. Knight runs for a touchdown, the defense holds in the fourth quarter, and UCLA flies home 9-0 with snow on its shoes."

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Hi, hi, hi, Wildcat family, welcome! I'm Inez Paloverde, your Arizona insider, and I am a desert-sunrise optimist. I talk fast, I love hard, and I will defend this team to the last saguaro. I love the desert and I want you to love it too, so be warned: there will be cactus metaphors. A good defense is a lot like a cactus. It's beautiful from a distance, and you do not want to touch it. The School in 60 Seconds

Here's my promise. I'm bubbly, but I don't fake the finishes. Every number here has a source, and when I do the math myself, I'll tell you. The School in 60 Seconds
Baylor plays in the Big 12. After 64 seasons at off-campus Floyd Casey Stadium, the Bears moved into on-campus McLane Stadium in 2014. CFBD lists 45,140 seats. Talk about a glow-up.

Joe Klanderman, the first-year defensive coordinator, is the interim head coach for the rest of the season. He won four national titles at North Dakota State and led the defense at Kansas State before coming to Waco. New project manager, same blueprints.

Through 8 games this season, Baylor is scoring 30.6 points per game and allowing 15.2.

Iowa State beat the Oklahoma State Cowboys 51-49 at home on Oct. 31. Jaylen Raynor went 18 of 28 for 309 yards, with 3 touchdowns; Aiden Flora ran 29 times for 221 yards and 2 touchdowns; Jamal Polite Jr. caught 6 balls for 171 yards and 1 touchdown.

"You also allowed 49 points. In my business we call that a house with a beautiful front door and no back wall. And the week before that, you went to Arizona and scored 3 points. Three. I have seen more points on a throw pillow."
"Nobody in Waco has had to tackle anybody. Our three losses came by one point to Auburn, 17-16, by eleven to TCU and by one at Kansas, 25-24. We have not been blown out once. You lost to Arizona by thirty-six."

report.title: Clones Crash Homecoming: Iowa State Visits Waco
report.byline: Twyla Hemmingsen · Iowa State Insider · Week 10
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Good evening, Cyclone Nation, and here's your Saturday forecast! I'm Twyla Hemmingsen, your Iowa State insider, coming to you live from the Ames weather center. Okay, it's my kitchen, but it has a very nice map on the wall. I'm high-energy, a little nerdy and joyful about it, and I talk about football the way the TV meteorologist talks about a cold front: pressure systems, wind shifts, and a big red blob moving across the screen. Every week I'll bring you the players, the coaches and the matchup, plus a full radar sweep of the opponent. Expect conditions to change quickly. When things are going our way, you'll hear "Forecast: loud, with gusts." When it's really rolling: "Cyclone warning in effect." Umbrellas optional, joy mandatory.

The School in 60 Seconds
Our home is Jack Trice Stadium in Ames, which holds 61,500. It's named for Jack Trice, Iowa State's first Black athlete. The stadium got his name in 1997, and it is still the only major college football stadium named for a Black man. Every Cyclone fan should know his story. On the field, Iowa State went 8-4 last season. Then came the biggest offseason storm in the country. Coach Matt Campbell left for Penn State and took three-year starting QB Rocco Becht with him. More than 50 Cyclones entered the transfer portal, including 16 starters. That's a full barometric reset.

The Coach and the Scheme
Jimmy Rogers was named Iowa State's 34th head coach on Dec. 5, 2025, coming from Washington State on a six-year contract. Before that he went 27-3 and won an FCS national title at South Dakota State, and he brought in more than 45 transfers to rebuild this roster.

We've played 8 games, and we're putting up 29.0 points a game while giving up 27.2.

Players to Know
QB Jaylen Raynor: 111 of 186, 1,416 yards, 10 touchdowns, 5 interceptions.
RB Aiden Flora: 937 yards on 131 carries, 8 touchdowns.
WR Jamal Polite Jr.: 14 catches, 286 yards, 2 touchdowns.
DE Isaac Terrell: 3 sacks, the team lead.
LB Sullivan Schlimgen: a team-high 79 tackles.

The Conference Picture
Iowa State is 4-4 overall and 2-3 in league play. ESPN's standings have Iowa State 8th in the Big 12.
The season so far: W 38-10 vs Southeast Missouri State Redhawks (Sept. 5), L 13-16 at Iowa Hawkeyes (Sept. 12), W 55-7 vs Bowling Green Falcons (Sept. 19), L 17-31 vs Utah Utes (Sept. 26), W 45-42 vs West Virginia Mountaineers (Oct. 3), L 10-24 at BYU Cougars (Oct. 9), L 3-39 at Arizona Wildcats (Oct. 24), W 51-49 vs Oklahoma State Cowboys (Oct. 31).

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides
We travel to Baylor (5-3, 3-2 Big 12) on Saturday, Nov. 7, at noon ET, at McLane Stadium, Waco, Texas.
Last time out. We beat the Oklahoma State Cowboys 51-49 at home on Oct. 31. Jaylen Raynor went 18 of 28 for 309 yards, with 3 touchdowns, Aiden Flora ran 29 times for 221 yards and 2 touchdowns and Jamal Polite Jr. caught 6 balls for 171 yards and 1 touchdown.
Baylor beat the UCF Knights 41-9 on the road on Oct. 30. DJ Lagway went 16 of 25 for 319 yards, with 4 touchdowns; Ryelan Morris ran 11 times for 82 yards; Gavin Freeman caught 5 balls for 114 yards and 1 touchdown.
Players to watch. Baylor quarterback DJ Lagway is 129 of 242 for 1,671 yards, with 13 touchdowns and 4 interceptions. Dawson Pendergrass leads their ground game with 338 yards on 95 carries and 2 scores. Gavin Freeman is their top target: 63 catches for 792 yards. On defense, linebacker Travion Barnes has 57 tackles and defensive end Garrick Ponder has 4 sacks.
The series. CFBD has 9 regular-season meetings with Baylor from 2016 through 2025. We won 4 of them, and Baylor won the last one 43-21 in 2024.
Availability. Nothing official on injuries yet for Iowa State vs. Baylor. When Iowa State or Baylor puts out a real report, you'll hear it from me, not a rumor.
From the preview booth. I shared the mic this week with Maggie Whitlock, Baylor's insider. Here's what I said:
"Arizona was a weather event. Every storm has a calm spot. We came out of it and scored 51."
"Freeman is very good. Sixty-three catches, 792 yards. I will grant you that the way a forecaster grants you a sunny afternoon, with an asterisk. But Flora has 937 rushing yards and 8 touchdowns, and nobody in Waco has had to tackle him yet."
"And in 2024 we beat you 43-21. Forty-three. That is not a weather event, that is climate."
And the last word from Maggie: "That is how you know it is good design. Homecoming, Twyla. Wear something warm and something green."

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
We walk into Baylor's Homecoming at McLane Stadium, and Cyclone fans in early can hit the Waco Downtown Farmers Market on East Bridge Street on Saturday.

report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Hi, everybody. I'm Fitz Calloway, your Kansas insider. I'm a lifelong Lawrence native and a hoops-first guy who converted to football analytics out of spite. I travel and live with this team, and I convert every football stat into basketball points. A touchdown is two and a half three-pointers. I refuse to stop.

Here's my promise. I'm self-deprecating, but I'm not sloppy. Every number in this report has a source, and when I do the math myself, I'll say so. If I don't know something about Kansas, I'll admit it. I celebrate our players as people first, I respect every opponent, and I thank God for this town, this team and this stubborn hope. I'm only here because of spite and the stats. Okay, also love. Rock Chalk.

The School in 60 Seconds
Kansas football began in 1890, which makes it one of the oldest programs in the country. Home is David Booth Kansas Memorial Stadium, which opened in 1921 and is one of the oldest college football stadiums anywhere. Until 2014 it had a running track around the field. CFBD lists 47,000 seats.

The last five seasons: 2-10 in 2021, then 6-7, a joyful 9-4 in 2023, and 5-7 twice. That 9-4 season is a memory I cherish.

The Coach and the Scheme
Lance Leipold has been head coach since 2021. CFBD lists his Kansas hire date as April 30, 2021. At Wisconsin-Whitewater from 2007 to 2014, he won six Division III national championships. He reached 100 wins faster than any coach in NCAA history, in his 106th game. Then he coached Buffalo from 2015 to 2020.

We've played 8 games, and we're putting up 29.1 points a game while giving up 23.8.

From the preview booth. I shared the mic this week with Knox Brevard-Stiles, UCF's insider. Here's what I said:
"Rock Chalk. Wait, it's FOOTBALL season?"
"In basketball we'd still be undefeated."
"I watched the end of that one. Somebody told me it was on."
And the last word from Knox: "It's good in anything, Fitz."

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)

report.title: Purple in the Flint Hills: Kansas State Hosts Oklahoma State
report.byline: Hattie Brandvold · Kansas State Insider · Week 10
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Well, howdy, Wildcat family. I'm Hattie Brandvold. I have an agronomy degree, a purple denim jacket, a wheat-sheaf brooch and a field notebook with real Flint Hills dirt on it. Every drive gets named after a crop. A three-and-out is a dry sorghum patch. A long, patient march is winter wheat. And a touchdown? That's a bumper harvest, and you will hear me holler it. When we win, I do the Wabash Cannonball in my chair, tidy and joyful. When we lose, I whisper my most treasured words, "You can't rush a harvest," and I plant a tiny basil seed right there on set. Easygoing as a prairie Sunday, until I hand you the one fact that ends the argument.

The School in 60 Seconds
Kansas State football is the story of the biggest turnaround in the sport. When Bill Snyder took over in 1989, the program was in the middle of a 27-game winless streak. He turned it into a national contender that went to 11 straight bowl games and had six 11-win seasons in a seven-year stretch. Snyder won two Big 12 championships, one in 2003 with Darren Sproles and one in 2012. He went into the College Football Hall of Fame while still coaching, in December 2015. The Wildcats play at Bill Snyder Family Stadium in Manhattan, and the rivalry with Kansas is the Sunflower Showdown, played for the Governor's Cup. Now that's a crop that keeps coming back every spring.

The Coach and the Scheme
Collin Klein was named the 36th head coach in school history on Dec. 4, 2025. You may remember him as the quarterback: he was a 2012 Heisman Trophy finalist and won the Johnny Unitas Award that year, when K-State won the Big 12. He is the first K-State alum to be head coach since Ellis Rainsberger in 1975-77. Before this job he coached nine years in Manhattan, including two as offensive coordinator (2022-23) that went 19-8 with a Big 12 title, then ran the offense at Texas A&M.

The 8-game numbers: 31.8 points per game scored, 21.9 allowed.

Players to Know

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides
We host Oklahoma State (5-3, 3-2 Big 12) on Saturday, Nov. 7, at 1:00 p.m. ET, at Bill Snyder Family Stadium, Manhattan, Kansas, on TNT, HBO Max.
Last time out. We lost to the Colorado Buffaloes 27-24 (OT) on the road on Oct. 31. Blake Barnett went 18 of 28 for 224 yards, with 3 touchdowns, Rodney Fields Jr. ran 12 times for 65 yards and Josh Manning caught 6 balls for 73 yards and 1 touchdown.
Oklahoma State lost to the Iowa State Cyclones 51-49 on the road on Oct. 31. Drew Mestemaker went 27 of 42 for 323 yards, with 5 touchdowns; Caleb Hawkins ran 25 times for 194 yards and 2 touchdowns; Justin Bowick caught 7 balls for 124 yards and 2 touchdowns.
Players to watch. Oklahoma State quarterback Drew Mestemaker is 184 of 281 for 2,649 yards, with 25 touchdowns and 7 interceptions. Caleb Hawkins leads their ground game with 906 yards on 167 carries and 4 scores. Justin Bowick is their top target: 41 catches for 731 yards. On defense, linebacker Ethan Wesloski has 76 tackles and linebacker Ethan Wesloski has 4 sacks.
The series. CFBD has 10 regular-season meetings with Oklahoma State from 2016 through 2025. We won 6 of them, and Oklahoma State won the last one 14-6 in 2025.
Availability. ESPN had no injury data for this game when I checked, so I'm not guessing about anybody's health on either side, Kansas State or Oklahoma State.
From the preview booth. I shared the mic this week with Dusty Lockridge, Oklahoma State's insider. Here's what I said:
"A stampede runs out of grass. We give up 21.9 points a game. You give up 27.1. And you lost 49-51 at Iowa State last week."
"I remember 14-6. Last year. And 42-20 the year before."
And the last word from Dusty: "Rodeo timing. You let the bull think he's winning, then you ride him for eight."

report.title: Frogs Under the Desert Lights: TCU Visits Tucson
report.byline: Ryder Galloway · TCU Insider · Week 10
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Well, howdy, Frog fans, and welcome! I'm Ryder Galloway, your TCU insider. I'm a Stockyards cowboy who became a finance guy, so I wear boots with a quarter-zip and I explain defenses as cattle drives. You've got your point riders, your flank riders and your drag riders, and when everyone holds their spot, nobody gets loose. I travel with this TCU team, and I live with it. Fair warning: if something goes wrong, anything at all, I will probably blame Dallas. Flat tire? Dallas. Missed field goal? Dallas. When we win, it's "Yeehaw!" and my hat goes flying. When we lose, I mutter about Dallas some more. And the best sound in football is me hollering "Yeehaw, that's a turnover!" Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, Fort Worth style.

The School in 60 Seconds
TCU has a national title on the wall. The 1938 Horned Frogs went 11-0, beat Carnegie Tech 15-7 in the Sugar Bowl and won the national championship. Quarterback Davey O'Brien won the Heisman Trophy that year. The 2010 team went 13-0 and won the Rose Bowl, and in 2022 Sonny Dykes led TCU all the way to the College Football Playoff national championship game. Home is Amon G. Carter Stadium in Fort Worth, listed at 46,000. Not one bit of that history happened in Dallas. And the rivalry with Baylor has a name now, the Revivalry, and we just won it in Waco. Ten more minutes on that and I'd be throwing my hat again.

The Coach and the Scheme

The School in 60 Seconds

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Charge On, Knights! I'm Knox Brevard-Stiles, your UCF insider. I grew up in Orlando, I'm a theme-park ride engineer, and I swear the stands really move. I measure crowd noise with a ride-safety gauge, and I wear a knight's helmet after big wins. Please keep your hands and feet inside the stadium at all times.

The School in 60 Seconds
UCF first fielded a varsity team in 1979 as an NCAA Division III program and reached Division I-A, now the FBS, in 1996. That made UCF the first program in NCAA history to play in all four divisions of college football. As a Division I-AA program, the Knights made the 1990 and 1993 playoffs. Today they play in the Big 12.

Home is the Acrisure Bounce House on UCF's main campus east of Orlando. Wikipedia lists 45,906 seats and CFBD lists 44,206. CFBD says it opened in 2007. The first game there was a 35-32 loss to No. 6 Texas on Sept. 15, 2007, and UCF led 24-23 early in the fourth quarter. Ride Check: the stands held up just fine that day.

The last five seasons: 9-4, 9-5, 6-7, 4-8 and 5-7.

The Coach and the Scheme
Scott Frost is back for a second run in Orlando. He coached UCF in 2016 and 2017, and his 2017 team went 13-0. Then he coached Nebraska from 2018 to 2022. CFBD lists his return as Dec. 7, 2024. As a player, he led Nebraska to the 1997 national championship. He has coached Heisman winner Marcus Mariota and Heisman candidate McKenzie Milton.

report.title: Eagles at Home: Boston College Hosts Florida State on Military Appreciation Day

report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
All rise, Eagles fans. I'm Siobhan Dunleavy, your Boston College insider, grad student and former debate champion. I argue every play like it's a moot-court case, and I always appoint myself the judge, which my co-hosts find wicked unfair. When we win, I bang my toy gavel and announce, "Objection overruled, we WON." When we lose, I file an appeal with the Court of Iced Coffee. The court has never ruled in my favor, and I keep filing anyway. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, argued on the merits. "Objection: sustained."

The School in 60 Seconds
Boston College plays at Alumni Stadium in Chestnut Hill, listed at 44,500.

The Coach and the Scheme
Bill O'Brien was named Boston College's 37th head coach on Feb. 9, 2024. His résumé is a long exhibit list. At Penn State in 2012 and 2013 he went 15-9 and won the Bear Bryant and Maxwell Club coach of the year awards in 2012. With the Houston Texans he went 52-48 and won four AFC South titles.

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides
We host Florida State (3-5, 1-4 ACC) on Saturday, Nov. 7, at noon ET, at Alumni Stadium (Chestnut Hill, MA), Chestnut Hill, Massachusetts, on ACC Network.
Last time out. We lost to the Duke Blue Devils 47-2 on the road on Oct. 31. Mason McKenzie went 9 of 17 for 87 yards, Bo MacCormack III ran 9 times for 24 yards and Jackson Wade caught 1 balls for 36 yards.
Florida State lost to the Clemson Tigers 36-24 at home on Oct. 31. Ashton Daniels went 21 of 33 for 350 yards, with 2 touchdowns; Quintrevion Wisner ran 13 times for 43 yards; Micahi Danzy caught 4 balls for 108 yards and 1 touchdown.
Players to watch. Florida State quarterback Ashton Daniels is 127 of 214 for 1,968 yards, with 14 touchdowns and 11 interceptions. The series. CFBD has 8 regular-season meetings with Florida State from 2016 through 2025. We won 4 of them, and Florida State won the last one 28-13 in 2024.

From the preview booth. I shared the mic this week with Gianna Ravello, Florida State's insider. Here's what I said:
"History is what you reach for when your present is 3-5. Let me introduce a counterargument. You are 3-5."

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Well, hey there, y'all! I'm Dixie-Lynn Pruitt, your Clemson insider. I was a flag captain in the Tiger Band, and I read defensive fronts like choreography. Step, slide, swim move, sack. I've named every one of them. My orange rain boots are named Darlene.

Here's my promise. I'm all Upstate grit, and I don't dress up the facts. Every number in this Clemson report has a source. If I don't know something about Clemson, I'll say so plainly. I celebrate our players as young men first, I respect every opponent, and I thank the good Lord for Saturdays in the Upstate. Orange you glad I said it?

The School in 60 Seconds
The Tigers won national championships in 2016 and 2018, beating Alabama both times. Clemson made six straight College Football Playoff appearances from 2015 to 2021 and has 27 conference championships. More than 100 All-Americans and over 250 NFL players came through here.

Home is Memorial Stadium, which CFBD lists at 81,500 seats. The last five seasons: 10-3, 11-3, 9-4, 10-4 and 7-6.

report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Good evening. I'm Harrison Wexley-Moore IV, your Duke insider. I'm pre-law, pre-med and, frankly, pre-everything. Did I mention I also passed that exam? I did. Whichever one you're thinking of.

Here's my academic honor code for this column. Every fact has a citation, like any good thesis. If I don't know something about Duke, I'll mark it "incomplete" rather than invent an answer. Durham, class is in session.

The School in 60 Seconds
Duke plays in the ACC and has won 18 conference championships: eight in the ACC and ten in the Southern Conference. The program counts 53 All-Americans, ten ACC Players of the Year and three Pro Football Hall of Famers. Home is Wallace Wade Stadium in Durham, which CFBD lists as built in 1929 with 40,004 seats.

For decades the university de-emphasized football, starting around the mid-1960s. Then came a renaissance under David Cutcliffe from 2008 to 2021, including Duke's first Coastal Division title in 2013, clinched with a win over North Carolina. The last five seasons show the progress: 3-9 in 2021, then 9-4, 8-5, 9-4 and 9-5. Four straight winning seasons. I've written longer papers on less.

The Coach and the Scheme
Manny Diaz is our head coach. CFBD records his hire date as Dec. 7, 2023. He was head coach at Miami from 2019 to 2021 and defensive coordinator and linebackers coach at Penn State in 2022 and 2023. He's also coached at Mississippi State, Louisiana Tech, Texas, Middle Tennessee, NC State and Florida State. That's a doctoral program in defense.

Through 8 games this season, Duke is scoring 32.0 points per game and allowing 14.2.

Players to Know

Players to watch. NC State quarterback CJ Bailey is 156 of 244 for 1,955 yards, with 13 touchdowns and 4 interceptions. Jayden Scott leads their ground game with 358 yards on 62 carries and 4 scores. Keenan Jackson is their top target: 30 catches for 456 yards. On defense, linebacker Popo Aguirre has 76 tackles and linebacker Elijah Satchell has 4 sacks.

From the preview booth. I shared the mic this week with Rutherford "Ruff" Pegram, NC State's insider. Here's what I said:
"I have tolerated your brisket for six years. As a courtesy. A gentleman never refuses food from a neighbor, even one wearing that much red."
"That is the single most NC State thing I have ever heard. You could not beat us, so you named a running back after us."
"Most years? We won 45-33 last year. We won 29-19 the year before that. We won 24-3 in 2023. Three. You scored three points, Ruff. I have seen more points on the scoreboard at a tennis match."
And the last word from Ruff: "Afterward, you eat my brisket and say thank you, win or lose. It is Military Appreciation day. We can all be decent for one afternoon."

report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Motion to reconsider: denied! I'm Gianna Ravello, and I'm your Florida State insider. I'm a Capitol lobbyist type who networks recruits and reads coverage like legislation. Fair warning: I turn every take into a bill on the floor. On the podcast, that segment is called Floor Debate. My rules are simple. I keep it clean and kind, I celebrate Florida State players as people, I respect every opponent, and I never invent a stat, a quote or a fact. If I can't source it, no Florida State fan hears it from me.

The School in 60 Seconds
Home is Doak Campbell Stadium in Tallahassee, built in 1950 with a listed capacity of 67,277. The playing surface is Bobby Bowden Field, and the band is the Marching Chiefs. The program claims national titles from 1993, 1999 and 2013. The last five seasons went 5-7, 10-3, 13-1, 2-10 and 5-7, from 2021 through 2025. And if you visit, ask somebody about Osceola and Renegade. It's the tradition I'd show you first.

The Coach and the Scheme
Florida State fired Mike Norvell on Sunday, Nov. 1, the day after the 36-24 home loss to Clemson. Rick Stockstill, who was head coach at Middle Tennessee for 18 seasons, is the interim head coach, and offensive coordinator Tim Harris Jr. calls the plays. Norvell went 41-39 here, and his best team went 13-0 and won the ACC in 2023. We thank Coach Norvell for every Saturday he gave this program.

report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Hey there, Pack! I'm Rutherford Pegram, but everybody calls me Ruff, and I'm your NC State insider. I'm a Wake County native and an engineer, and I grill at the same Carter-Finley lot every home game. I explain schemes with grill thermometers. A defense running at 225 degrees? That's low and slow. An offense at 450? That's a sear.

Here's my promise. I'm loud, I'm warm and I'm gloriously dramatic, but I don't cook the numbers. Every stat here has a source. If I don't know something about NC State, I'll tell you the thermometer's still reading. I celebrate our players as people first, I respect every opponent, and I thank God for good friends, good food and good football. I howl once per segment, no more, no less. Wolfpack, howl!

The School in 60 Seconds
NC State plays in the ACC and was a founding member in 1953, after years in the Southern Conference. The Wolfpack has won seven conference championships and played in 34 bowl games, winning 17. Since 1966, home has been Carter-Finley Stadium, the largest college football stadium in North Carolina. CFBD lists it at 58,000 seats. In 2010 the school brought back a live mascot, a Tamaskan dog named Tuffy. Good boy.

The last five seasons have been steady heat: 9-3, 8-5, 9-4, 6-7 and 8-5. Four winning seasons in five years. The grill stays lit in Raleigh.

The Coach and the Scheme
Dave Doeren led NC State starting in 2013. CFBD records his hire date as Dec. 1, 2012. Before Raleigh he was head coach at Northern Illinois in 2011 and 2012. The school relieved Doeren of his duties after the loss at Stanford, and running backs coach and special teams coordinator Todd Goebbel will serve as interim head coach for the rest of the season. We thank Coach Doeren for every Saturday he gave this program.

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

Last time out. We beat the California Golden Bears 31-10 at home on Oct. 31. CJ Bailey went 13 of 25 for 192 yards, with 2 touchdowns, Davion Gause ran 19 times for 104 yards and 1 touchdown and Chance Robinson caught 4 balls for 76 yards and 1 touchdown.
Duke beat the Boston College Eagles 47-2 at home on Oct. 31. Walker Eget went 11 of 18 for 201 yards, with 1 touchdown; Nate Sheppard ran 20 times for 97 yards and 5 touchdowns; Jeremiah Hasley caught 3 balls for 55 yards and 1 touchdown.
Players to watch. Duke quarterback Walker Eget is 133 of 215 for 1,641 yards, with 9 touchdowns and 3 interceptions. Nate Sheppard leads their ground game with 972 yards on 173 carries and 14 scores. Jonah Burton is their top target: 22 catches for 308 yards. On defense, linebacker Nick Morris Jr. has 45 tackles and defensive end Kevin O'Connor has 4.5 sacks.
The series. CFBD has 4 regular-season meetings with Duke from 2016 through 2025. We won 3 of them, and we won the last one 45-33 in 2025.

From the preview booth. I shared the mic this week with Harrison Wexley-Moore IV, Duke's insider. Here's what I said:
"And a gentleman says thank you. Here is your thank you. NC State has a running back named Duke. Jayden Scott. Wears number 1. Everybody calls him Duke. So on Saturday, there will be exactly one Duke on that field worth watching, and he is ours."
"We did not name him. We just took the name. Like we take your lunch most years."
"Fair. But you went to Georgia Tech and lost 28-25. You lost to North Carolina 24-20. You beat Virginia 19-16 and needed every bit of it. On the road, your private club turns into a tent."
And the last word from Harrison: "For one afternoon. Then I go back to being right."

report.title: Golden Hurricane in the Big Easy: Tulsa Visits Tulane
report.byline: Wiley Pettibone · Tulsa Insider · Week 10
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Howdy, friends. I'm Wiley Pettibone, your Tulsa insider. I studied petroleum geology, so I see football as a drilling operation. A good drive is a gusher. A bad one is a dry well.

Here's my promise. I'm all-in on the Golden Hurricane, but I don't strike oil where there isn't any. Every number I give you is sourced. If I don't know something about Tulsa, I'll say the survey's still out.

The School in 60 Seconds
Tulsa plays its home games at Skelly Field at H. A. Chapman Stadium, which CFBD lists as built in 1930 with 30,000 seats. The Golden Hurricane has played in the American Conference since 2014 after previously competing in Conference USA. Here's a fact I love: Tulsa has the smallest undergraduate enrollment of any FBS school. Small well, deep reserves.

The last five seasons have been mostly dry: 7-6 in 2021, 5-7, 4-8, 3-9 and 4-8 in 2025. I smell oil.

The Coach and the Scheme
Tre Lamb is our head coach. Wikipedia says he took the job in December 2024, and CFBD records Dec. 8, 2024. He coached East Tennessee State in 2024 and Gardner-Webb from 2020 to 2023, with earlier assistant jobs at Tennessee Tech and Mercer. He was born in 1989, which makes him one of the younger bosses in the business.

We've played 8 games, and we're putting up 29.8 points a game while giving up 24.4.

Players to Know
QB Baylor Hayes: 122 of 195, 1,343 yards, 10 touchdowns, 2 interceptions.
RB Damari Alston: 429 yards on 103 carries, 6 touchdowns.
WR Oran Singleton Jr.: 43 catches, 535 yards, 4 touchdowns.
DL Kyran Duhon: 6 sacks, the team lead.
LB Chris Thompson Jr.: a team-high 81 tackles.

The Conference Picture
Tulsa is 4-4 overall and 1-3 in league play. ESPN's standings have Tulsa 10th in the American.
The season so far: W 24-10 vs Oklahoma State Cowboys (Sept. 5), W 23-17 at Sam Houston Bearkats (Sept. 12), W 42-0 vs East Texas A&M Lions (Sept. 19), L 6-34 at Arkansas Razorbacks (Sept. 26), L 44-45 (OT) vs North Texas Mean Green (Oct. 1), L 26-34 at Navy Midshipmen (Oct. 10), W 38-17 at Rice Owls (Oct. 17), L 35-38 vs Army Black Knights (Oct. 23).

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides
We travel to Tulane (4-4, 2-2 American) on Saturday, Nov. 7, at noon ET, at Yulman Stadium, New Orleans, Louisiana, on ESPNU.
Last time out. We lost to the Army Black Knights 38-35 at home on Oct. 23. Baylor Hayes went 23 of 34 for 262 yards, with 2 touchdowns, Trequan Jones ran 5 times for 66 yards and 1 touchdown and Jimmy Calloway caught 10 balls for 88 yards and 1 touchdown.
Tulane beat the Charlotte 49ers 38-31 (OT) on the road on Oct. 30. Trace Johnson went 28 of 36 for 284 yards, with 1 touchdown; Johnnie Daniels ran 13 times for 99 yards and 2 touchdowns; Zycarl Lewis Jr. caught 3 balls for 55 yards.
Players to watch. Tulane quarterback Kadin Semonza is 64 of 119 for 804 yards, with 4 touchdowns and 2 interceptions. Johnnie Daniels leads their ground game with 493 yards on 79 carries and 6 scores. Destyn Hill is their top target: 32 catches for 390 yards. On defense, linebacker Dickson Agu has 78 tackles and linebacker Makai Williams has 4 sacks.
The series. CFBD has 9 regular-season meetings with Tulane from 2016 through 2025. We won 4 of them, and we won the last one 31-14 in 2025.
Availability. No official availability report for Tulsa or Tulane was in the public data I checked, so nobody gets ruled in or out here.
From the preview booth. I shared the mic this week with Twan Ducros-Labat, Tulane's insider. Here's what I said:
"We have been resting. There is a difference. Two weeks off, fresh legs, and Oran Singleton Jr. with 535 receiving yards running past your secondary like a pipeline leak. Fast, messy, and expensive to clean up."
"In Tulsa it is the highest one there is."
"Your offense scores 22.5 a game. That is not a horn section. That is a kazoo."
And the last word from Twan: "Then the band plays louder. That is what we do. When the other team scores, we play louder. When we score, we play louder still. By the end of the day you will not be able to hear yourself think."

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
We head to New Orleans on the same Saturday as Beignet Fest at City Park's Festival Grounds, with Amanda Shaw and the Imagination Movers playing, so Hurricane fans have a full day.

report.title: Roadrunners in Boca: UTSA Takes On FAU on Thursday Night
report.byline: Marisol Ybarra · UTSA Insider · Week 10
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Birds up! ¡Hola, y'all! I'm Marisol Ybarra, born and raised in San Antonio, and I have a confession: I collect Fiesta medals. Hundreds of them. They fill a whole wall of my living room, and every great Roadrunner play earns a brand-new medal. I travel with this UTSA team and I live with it, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, with Tex-Mex warmth and Fiesta energy. I read an offense the way I read a parade route: every float has to be on time, every band in step. When we win, I yell "Birds up!" and crack a cascarón full of confetti over the nearest head. When we lose, I tell you, "The parade will come back around." It always does in San Antonio.

The School in 60 Seconds
The Roadrunners represent the University of Texas at San Antonio and compete in the American Conference. Home is the Alamodome, which seats 65,000 but is normally set up for about 35,000 for UTSA games; CFBD lists 36,582. Jeff Traylor has coached the team since 2020. And the medal wall from these years is full: 12-2 in 2021, 11-3 in 2022, 9-4, 7-6 and 7-6. This program has built something special in a short time.

The Coach and the Scheme
Coach Traylor was hired Dec. 9, 2019, per CFBD.

The 8-game numbers: 33.5 points per game scored, 26.0 allowed.

Players to Know
QB Owen McCown: 169 of 243, 1,751 yards, 10 touchdowns, 4 interceptions.

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides
We travel to Florida Atlantic (5-3, 2-2 American) on Thursday, Nov. 5, at 7:30 p.m. ET, at Flagler Credit Union Stadium, Boca Raton, Florida, on ESPN.
Last time out. We beat the Tulane Green Wave 42-19 on the road on Oct. 24. Owen McCown went 16 of 23 for 173 yards, Will Henderson III ran 15 times for 102 yards and 1 touchdown and David Amador II caught 5 balls for 47 yards.
Florida Atlantic lost to the North Texas Mean Green 48-41 on the road on Oct. 29. Caden Veltkamp went 37 of 56 for 452 yards, with 5 touchdowns; Leonard Farrow ran 14 times for 47 yards; Easton Messer caught 16 balls for 189 yards and 3 touchdowns.
Players to watch. Florida Atlantic quarterback Caden Veltkamp is 227 of 316 for 2,536 yards, with 23 touchdowns and 5 interceptions. Ethan Ervin leads their ground game with 369 yards on 91 carries and 2 scores. Easton Messer is their top target: 74 catches for 898 yards. On defense, linebacker Joseph Sipp Jr. has 57 tackles and linebacker Joseph Sipp Jr. has 2 sacks.
The series. CFBD has 4 regular-season meetings with Florida Atlantic from 2016 through 2025. We won 2 of them, and Florida Atlantic won the last one 38-24 in 2024.
Availability. The public injury data for Florida Atlantic and UTSA is empty this week, so I'm sticking to who has actually been on the field.
From the preview booth. I shared the mic this week with Kaia Brightwater, Florida Atlantic's insider. Here's what I said:
"Mija, I love a big offense. I married one. But UTSA is 4-0 in the American. We beat Tulane 42-19 on their own field. Owen McCown does not panic. He reads the field like a parade route. Left at the Alamo, right at the river, and he never drops the float."
"Brandon Tucker has 56 tackles. Owen Pewee has four sacks. And we have Will Henderson III, who ran for 102 yards at Tulane and has 664 on the year. When we get the lead, Kaia, we hand the ball to Will and you watch your offense sit on the bench eating jam."
"And you guys swim. Beautifully. Right up until the fourth quarter, when you notice the tide went out."
And the last word from Kaia: "Tonight. breaks your heart."

report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Good evening from the hangar. I mean the press box. I'm Lt. Col. Marissa Okonkwo-Hale, retired, your Air Force insider. I spent my career as an instructor pilot, and now I fly through option reads at Mach speed. I travel and live with this team, and everyone I work with gets a call sign. My editor is "Red Pen."

Pre-flight checklist for this column. Every number is sourced, like a verified flight plan. If I don't know something about Air Force, I'll report it as unknown instead of guessing. I celebrate these cadets as people and future officers first, I respect every opponent, and I give thanks to God for the privilege of serving alongside them. Call sign: correct.

The School in 60 Seconds
Air Force represents the U.S. Air Force Academy and plays home games at Falcon Stadium, north of Colorado Springs. CFBD lists it as built in 1962 with 46,692 seats, at an elevation of about 2,025 meters. The Falcons have been in the Mountain West since the league was founded in 1999. The three service academies compete for the Commander-in-Chief's Trophy each year.

The last five seasons: 10-3, 10-3, 9-4, then 5-7 and 4-8. We're climbing back to cruising altitude.

The Coach and the Scheme
Troy Calhoun has led the program since 2007, and CFBD records his hire date as Dec. 22, 2006. Twenty seasons in the cockpit is a rare thing in this sport.

The series. CFBD has 7 regular-season meetings with Army from 2016 through 2025. We won 3 of them, and we won the last one 20-17 in 2025.

From the preview booth. I shared the mic this week with Capt. (Ret.) Thaddeus Rourke, Army's insider. Here's what I said:
"Forty years of telling the same story."
"We beat Navy 14-9. We beat UNLV 41-31. We won in overtime at Nevada. This team finds a way."

report.title: Rainbow Warriors in El Paso: Hawai'i Returns to the Sun Bowl
report.byline: Kainoa Akana-Baird · Hawai'i Insider · Week 10
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Aloha, Rainbow Warriors fans! I'm Kainoa Akana-Baird, your Hawai'i insider. When I'm not on the show, I teach big-wave surfing on O'ahu. And when I'm on the show, I do time-zone math, because when your team flies farther than anybody in college football, somebody has to keep the clocks straight. When we win, I say "Shoots!" and throw a shaka. When we lose, I shrug: "Island time. We'll catch the next wave." Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, with aloha. "Island time, but on schedule."

The School in 60 Seconds
Home for us is the Clarence T.C. Ching Athletics Complex, listed at 15,194. Last season was a big wave. Hawai'i went 9-4, opened the season by beating Stanford, and won the Hawai'i Bowl over Cal after coming back from 21 points down, tying the biggest comeback in program history. It was our first bowl bid since 2021.

The Coach and the Scheme
Timmy Chang was named Hawai'i's 25th head coach on Jan. 22, 2022. Before that, he was a Hawai'i legend. As our quarterback from 2000 to 2004, he set the NCAA career records for passing yards (17,072) and total offense, and he won a program-record 29 games as a starter. He was also a two-time Hawai'i Bowl Most Outstanding Player and a finalist for the Johnny Unitas Award as a senior. Before all that he was a record-setting quarterback at Honolulu's Saint Louis School. Local boy. He coached at Nevada, Jackson State, Emory & Henry and SMU before coming home. In 2025 he was the AFCA Region 5 Coach of the Year.

Through 8 games this season, Hawai'i is scoring 20.8 points per game and allowing 24.5.

My granddaddy could spot a blitz before the snap and carve a perfect duck in the same afternoon. I'm still working on the duck.

I don't hurry, and I don't holler (much). I treat every week like a hike: steady climbing, honest footing, then a view at the top. That means real numbers, plain talk, and a fair word for every visitor. If I don't know something about App State, I'll tell you, and then I'll go find out. Some programs get a stadium. The School in 60 Seconds
Appalachian State is in Boone, North Carolina, and has played FBS football in the Sun Belt since 2014. Before that, the Mountaineers were an FCS power from 1978 to 2013. report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Hi, friends. I'm Mercy Holderby, your Marshall insider. I'm a Huntington native and a nurse, and I'm the daughter of two Marshall grads. I grew up hearing the story of this program's rebirth at our kitchen table. Some families hand down recipes. Mine handed down a chant.

You'll get two things from me every week. First, heart. I love these young men, win or lose, and I'll always talk about them as people first. Second, toughness. I'll tell you the truth about what the numbers say, even when it stings, and I'll never invent a fact to make us feel better. If I don't know, I'll say so. And yes, I'll be the loudest "We Are" in any room. In Huntington, those words mean more than a cheer.

The School in 60 Seconds
Marshall plays in the Sun Belt Conference East Division at the FBS level. Home is Joan C. Edwards Stadium, which opened in 1991 with a 24-23 win over New Hampshire in front of 33,116 fans. The record crowd is 41,382, set against West Virginia on Sept. 10, 2010. Capacity is listed two ways: Wikipedia says 38,227 and CFBD says 38,016. It's one of two Division I stadiums named for a woman, and through the 2024 season Marshall was 192-45 there.

Marshall's first organized game against another college was a 15-0 win over Shelton College on Nov. 24, 1903. The last five seasons: 7-6, 9-4, 6-7, 10-3 and 5-7.

The Coach and the Scheme

I travel with this Old Dominion team and I live with it, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines with a royal-court flourish and an honest heart. To the top! Hey, y'all, I'm Delphine Broussard, but please call me Dee. The last five seasons have been a roller coaster: 3-9 in 2021, 7-6 in 2022, 3-9, then a hard 1-11 in 2024 and a hard-earned 7-6 bounce back in 2025. Every week you'll get the players, the matchups, the history and the hope, because I believe we are always one play away from greatness. I can FEEL it. The School in 60 Seconds

The program moved up to Division I-A, now FBS, in 1994 and plays in the Sun Belt. Our home is Malone Stadium in Monroe, listed at 27,617 seats and opened in 1978. Here's the hard truth, said with love: our only FBS bowl game was the 2012 Independence Bowl in Shreveport, a 45-14 loss to Ohio, and the drought since then is the longest in FBS. THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Greetings, Zips fans, and welcome! I'm Hollister Grubbs, but everybody calls me Zip. I'm a polymer-science grad from the Rubber City, and I measure football the only scientific way: in tire tread depth. Deep, grippy tread means a team that holds the road on third down. Bald tires mean a team sliding all over the place. I travel with this team and I live with this team, usually with a clipboard of formulas. When we win, I bounce like a superball: BOING! When we lose, I say, "Some tread wear today," and start scribbling equations to figure out why. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, vulcanized for durability. "That's some sticky tread."

The School in 60 Seconds
Akron plays at InfoCision Stadium, listed at 30,000, in a city that put the world on rubber tires. Our big rivalry is the Wagon Wheel game against Kent State. The trophy dates to 1946, and Kent State won the first nine games for it. Kent State won the 2025 meeting 42-35. Before that, we won the 2023 and 2024 meetings, 31-27 and 38-17.

The Coach and the Scheme

THE FANATIC EDITION

Howdy, Cardinals fans! I'm Gus Ponder, your Ball State insider. By day I produce community radio here in Muncie. By night I chart Ball State special teams on a whiteboard in my garage. When we win, I wear my celebratory cat tie and tell a joke so bad it's good. When we lose, I sigh, "Sounds like a Monday," and pull up the punt chart. The School in 60 Seconds

The Coach and the Scheme

Before that, he spent six seasons as an assistant at Northern Illinois and helped win MAC titles in 2012 and 2018. His stated plan: run the ball on offense, be physical on defense, be good on special teams, and don't beat yourself.

Hey, Falcons fans! I'm Darcy Fenwick, your Bowling Green insider. I played goalie for the club hockey team, and I still watch everything like I'm in the crease. Defending the throw? Greetings from the Pioneer Valley, friends. I'm Abner Kettleworth, your Massachusetts insider. I was an organic farmer in the Five College area until I started grinding game tape, and now I travel and live with this team. I still bring kale chips on the bus. Nobody eats them.

Fair warning: I make a Revolutionary War pun for every scheme. One if by run, two if by air. I'm also a stickler for the truth, which seems fitting for a Minuteman. Every number I give you carries a source. If I don't know something about Massachusetts, I'll tell you I'm still waiting on Paul Revere's report. I celebrate our players as people first, I respect every opponent, and I thank God for every chilly autumn Friday. Shot heard 'round the film room.

The School in 60 Seconds
UMass began playing football in 1879. The Minutemen reached three FCS national championship games and won the title in 1998. They've played home games at Warren McGuirk Alumni Stadium since 1965, and CFBD lists its capacity at 17,000. UMass began moving up to FBS in 2011 and was an associate MAC member until leaving after the 2015 season. After years as an independent, the school announced in February 2024 that it would rejoin the MAC. CFBD lists UMass as a MAC member this season.

The last five seasons were a long winter at Valley Forge: 1-11, 1-11, 3-9, 2-10 and 0-12 in 2025.

The Coach and the Scheme
Joe Harasymiak leads the regiment. CFBD records his hire date as Dec. 4, 2024. In December 2015 he became the youngest head coach in Division I football when Maine hired him. He went 20-15 there in three seasons, and his 2018 team won the CAA and reached the FCS semifinals. He later was co-defensive coordinator and safeties coach at Minnesota, then defensive coordinator at Rutgers from 2022 to 2024.

report.title: Bobcats Under the Tuesday Lights: Ohio Visits Akron
report.byline: Penny Trautman · Ohio Insider · Week 10
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Brick by brick, friends. I'm Penny Trautman, and I live in Athens, Ohio, where the streets are brick, the hills are green, and the Bobcats run the football like they're laying Court Street, one sturdy block at a time. I'm a brick-street archivist by hobby (it's a real hobby; I have a binder), and I chart this run game the same way. I travel with this Ohio team and I live with it, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines with some hill-country wit and an unreasonable number of brick puns. When we win, I tap a brick for luck and grin. When we lose, I say "brick by brick" and start rebuilding by Monday. Welcome to the porch. One more thing: I'll always be honest with you, even when the mortar's cracked.

The School in 60 Seconds

Meet Your Insider
Hey, Owl Nation! I'm Ximena Holcombe-Reyes, your Kennesaw State insider. I'm a Marietta native with a computer science degree, and I've cheered this program since its very first season. I was there for version 1.0. I still have the T-shirt. It no longer fits. That's growth.

Here's my operating system. I'm a builder. I love that some programs have a hundred years of history while Kennesaw State gets to write ours right now, live, in front of us. I'm keeping the notes. Every number I share is sourced and debugged. Every opponent gets respect. When I don't know something, I'll log it as "unknown" instead of guessing. Bugs happen. We patch them, and we ship again. Let's go, Owls.

The School in 60 Seconds
Kennesaw State football began play in 2015 as an FCS member of the Big South Conference. In 2022 the Owls moved to the ASUN's new FCS football league, and after that season they began the transition to FBS ahead of joining Conference USA in 2024. Home is Fifth Third Stadium, just outside the Kennesaw city limits. The game feed lists it as Walens Family Field at Fifth Third Stadium, and CFBD lists it as built in 2010 with a capacity of 11,040. report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Well, praise the Lord and hand me the program! I'm Gideon Fairweather, your Liberty insider. I grew up in Lynchburg, and I'm a youth pastor who coaches middle-school football on the side. That means I've given a locker-room speech about perseverance to eleven 12-year-olds who were mostly worried about Gatorade flavors. I'm ready for anything.

You'll hear a big laugh from me, and a lot of encouragement. When I look at a roster, I see a hundred-some young men who are each somebody's son, and I'll write about them that way. I'll also tell you the truth. Every number here is sourced. If we play poorly, I'll say so gently. If I don't know something about Liberty, I'll admit it. Lynchburg on game day feels like a family reunion with a marching band. Our guys play hard, play fair, and you can see the joy on their faces.

The School in 60 Seconds
Liberty University is a private Christian university in Lynchburg, Virginia. Its football program announced the move from FCS to FBS in July 2017, became a provisional FBS member in 2018, and became a full member with bowl eligibility in 2019. report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Howdy from the Ozarks! I'm Clementine Bilyeu, your Missouri State insider. I'm a Springfield native and a float-trip guide, and I've been maroon since the day I was born. Mama swears my first word was "Bears." It was probably "boat," but I've chosen my story and I'm sticking with it.

I take a practical view of football, the same way I take a river. Read the current, respect the rocks, and keep everybody in the canoe. Missouri State is on a brand-new ride as an FBS program, and I'm thrilled to be your guide. I'll give you real numbers, honest takes, and kind words for every opponent. If I don't know something about Missouri State, I'll tell you, and then I'll paddle off and find out. Springfield is the heart of the Ozarks, and our Bears are taking the whole region along. Pack a snack. It's going to be a fun float.

The School in 60 Seconds
Missouri State University is in Springfield, Missouri, and its first football team took the field in 1909. Until 2005, the school was known as Southwest Missouri State. The Bears were a founding member of the Gateway Football Conference in 1985, which later became the Missouri Valley Football Conference.

Home is Plaster Sports Complex, which CFBD lists with a capacity of 17,337 and a 1941 construction year. The last five seasons: 8-4, 5-6, 4-7, 8-4 and 7-6.

The Coach and the Scheme

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
¡Buenas noches, Aggies! I'm Esperanza Lujan-Tafoya, your New Mexico State insider. I'm a Las Cruces native, a chile farmer's daughter and an ag-science grad. That means I can tell you the soil pH of the practice field and how much Scoville heat a fourth-down stop packs. (A lot. A fourth-down stop is Christmas-style, red and green.)

Everything gets a chile grade from me. A routine first down? Mild. A 40-yard run? Hatch hot. But I don't heat up the facts. Every number I give you is real and sourced. Every opponent gets respect. If I don't know something about New Mexico State, I'll say so, and then I'll go find out. In the Mesilla Valley, fall smells like roasting chile and fresh-cut grass. Our Aggies play with that same heat, and the Organ Mountains watch every snap.

The School in 60 Seconds
New Mexico State plays FBS football in Conference USA. The road here was winding. The Aggies were independent in 2013, a football-only Sun Belt member from 2014 to 2017, and independent again from 2018. They announced in November 2021 that they would join Conference USA in all sports starting in 2023. Home is Aggie Memorial Stadium in Las Cruces, which CFBD lists as built in 1978 with a capacity of 28,853.

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Evenin', folks. Pull up a stump. I'm Lemuel Coxwell, but everybody from here to the Trinity River calls me Lem, and I'm your Sam Houston insider. I'm a Walker County native and a high-school history teacher, and I collect Texas folklore the way some folks collect bottle caps. My students say I can turn a fire drill into a three-part saga. They're not wrong.

Here's how I'll tell it. I'll be patient, because seasons are long and young men grow. I'll be proud, because Huntsville is a small Texas town with a big Texas name, and our Bearkats play like they're carrying it. Most of all, I'll be honest. A good storyteller never needs to stretch the truth. Every number I give you will be real. If I don't know something about Sam Houston, I'll say so plain, then go dig through the archives.

The School in 60 Seconds
Sam Houston State fielded its first football team in 1912. Home is Elliott T. Bowers Stadium in Huntsville, which seats 14,000, and CFBD lists it as built in 1986. In 2021 the Bearkats left the Southland Conference for the WAC's FCS football league, and in November 2021 they accepted an invitation to join Conference USA at the FBS level starting in 2023-24.

The last five seasons tell a tale with some hills in it: 11-1 in 2021, 5-4 in 2022, 3-9 in 2023, 10-3 in 2024 and 2-10 in 2025. Every good story has a hard chapter before a good one.

The Coach and the Scheme
Phil Longo was named Sam Houston's 16th head coach on Dec. 18, 2024, so this is his second season. Wikipedia describes him as a practitioner of the air raid offense. He was previously offensive coordinator at Wisconsin, and before that offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach at North Carolina, Ole Miss and Sam Houston.

report.title: Rams at Canvas: Colorado State Hosts Boise State
report.byline: Ansel Rimrock · Colorado State Insider · Week 10
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Mountain air, thick defense. Hello, friends, I'm Ansel Rimrock. Most mornings you'll find me on a trail in the foothills west of town, and on fall Saturdays you'll find me with the Rams. I travel with this Colorado State team and I live with it, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines. I'm a calm guy, but don't mistake calm for quiet: I'm competitive right down to my trail shoes. I think football is just a long trail run with blocking. You pace yourself, you climb, you don't panic on the switchbacks, and you finish strong. Fort Collins on a fall Saturday is green and gold from the foothills to the stadium. Visiting teams breathe a little harder up here, and our kids love it. Ram tough, trail ready.

The School in 60 Seconds
The Colorado State Rams compete in the Pac-12. Our big rivalries are with Colorado, Wyoming and Air Force. We've played at Canvas Stadium since 2017; before that, the Rams spent 49 seasons, 1968 to 2016, at Sonny Lubick Field at Hughes Stadium. CFBD lists Canvas at 36,500 seats. The last five seasons were a steep climb: 3-9, 3-9, 5-7, a nice 8-5 in 2024 and then 2-10 in 2025. Every trail has a hard stretch. We're climbing out of one.

The Coach and the Scheme
Jim Mora was hired on Nov. 26, 2025, and this is his first season.

We've played 8 games, and we're putting up 35.5 points a game while giving up 42.4.

Players to Know
QB Hauss Hejny: 90 of 134, 1,138 yards, 14 touchdowns, 2 interceptions.

report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Wave the flag. Howdy, neighbors, I'm Hank Palouse. I drive a combine for a living out in the wheat country, and I haven't missed a game in Pullman since cassette tapes. And yes, I still have the tapes. A whole shoebox of them, labeled by year, in the cab of my pickup. I travel with the Cougars and I live with the Cougars, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, with a little dry Palouse humor and a lot of love for Ol' Crimson, the flag that shows up at every big game in the country. When we win, I wave Ol' Crimson right here in the studio. When we lose, I say "Cougs never quit," and then I tell you a 20-minute story about harvest. You've been warned.

The School in 60 Seconds
Washington State University is in Pullman, and the first Cougar football team took the field in 1894. We play in the Pac-12. Home is Gesa Field at Martin Stadium, with Gesa naming the playing surface. Martin Stadium opened in 1972, and the ground there dates back to 1892, when it was called Soldier Field. CFBD lists 32,952 seats. The last five seasons were 7-6, 7-6, 5-7, 8-5 and 7-6. Steady folks out here, like the wheat: some years are a bumper crop, some years you pray for rain, but you always plant again.

The Coach and the Scheme
Kirby Moore is in his first season, and CFBD dates his hire to Dec. 12, 2025.

We've played 9 games, and we're putting up 19.0 points a game while giving up 27.4.

Players to Know
QB Caden Pinnick: 110 of 178, 952 yards, 3 touchdowns, 5 interceptions.
RB Kirby Vorhees: 292 yards on 66 carries, 4 touchdowns.
WR Branden Ganashamoorthy: 34 catches, 459 yards, 3 touchdowns.
DT Jirah Leaupepetele: 2.5 sacks, the team lead.
LB Keith Brown: a team-high 71 tackles.

The Conference Picture
Washington State is 1-8 overall and 0-5 in league play. ESPN's standings have Washington State 8th in the Pac-12.
The season so far: L 10-24 at Washington Huskies (Sept. 6), L 7-34 at Kansas State Wildcats (Sept. 12), W 48-7 vs Duquesne Dukes (Sept. 19), L 24-34 vs Arizona Wildcats (Sept. 26), L 6-26 vs Fresno State Bulldogs (Oct. 3), L 16-17 at Utah State Aggies (Oct. 9), L 30-48 at Oregon State Beavers (Oct. 17), L 10-31 vs Boise State Broncos (Oct. 24), L 20-26 at San Diego State Aztecs (Oct. 31).

This Week: Bye Week
No game for Washington State this week. We're off from Tuesday, Nov. 3, through Saturday, Nov. 7, so the rest of this Washington State report is about where we stand and what's next.
Last time out. We lost to the San Diego State Aztecs 26-20 on the road on Oct. 31. Owen Eshelman went 30 of 42 for 299 yards. He also ran 16 times for 34 yards and 2 touchdowns. Daniel Blood caught 8 balls for 105 yards.
Up next. We play the Colorado State Rams at home on Saturday, Nov. 14, 10:30 p.m. ET, at Martin Stadium in Pullman.
Cougs, rest up and refocus. Colorado State is next, and Pullman wants a big finish.

report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
I would posit! I'm Declan Moriarty-Chen, and I'm your Notre Dame insider. I'm a sweater-vested grad-student type who can recite the Irish schedule back to the leather-helmet era and the CFP selection protocol by heart. On the podcast, my segment is called The Thesis Defense, where I argue one Notre Dame proposition and defend it. My rules are simple. I keep it clean and kind, I celebrate Notre Dame players as people, I respect every opponent, and I never invent a stat, a quote or a fact. If I can't source it, no Notre Dame fan hears it from me.

The School in 60 Seconds
Home is Notre Dame Stadium in Notre Dame, Ind., built in 1930 with a listed capacity of 80,795. The mascot is the Notre Dame Leprechaun, the fight song is the "Notre Dame Victory March," and the band is the Band of the Fighting Irish. The program claims national titles from 1924, 1929, 1930, 1943, 1946, 1947, 1949, 1966, 1973, 1977 and 1988. The last five seasons went 11-2, 9-4, 10-3, 14-2 and 10-2, from 2021 through 2025. And if you visit, ask somebody about "Touchdown Jesus." It's the tradition I'd show you first.

The Coach and the Scheme
Marcus Freeman leads the Fighting Irish, and CollegeFootballData dates the hire to Dec. 3, 2021.

The 8-game numbers: 40.4 points per game scored, 13.4 allowed.

Players to Know
QB CJ Carr: 148 of 222, 1,849 yards, 18 touchdowns, 1 interception.

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides
We host No. 1 Miami (8-0, 6-0 ACC) on Saturday, Nov. 7, at 7:30 p.m. ET, at Notre Dame Stadium, Notre Dame, Indiana, on NBC. We come in ranked No. 4.
Miami beat the North Carolina Tar Heels 38-35 on the road on Oct. 31. Darian Mensah went 22 of 29 for 274 yards, with 3 touchdowns; Javian Mallory ran 12 times for 51 yards; Malachi Toney caught 7 balls for 75 yards and 2 touchdowns.
Players to watch. Miami quarterback Darian Mensah is 188 of 233 for 2,425 yards, with 25 touchdowns and 1 interception. The series. CFBD has 3 regular-season meetings with Miami from 2016 through 2025. We won 3 of them, and we won the last one 27-24 in 2025.

From the preview booth. I shared the mic this week with Javi "The Breeze" Castillo, Miami's insider. Here's what I said:
"You beat us last year. 27-24. In Miami. This is our house."

report.title: Huskies at the Rent: UConn Hosts North Carolina
