UL Monroe Warhawks vs Arkansas State Red Wolves prediction for Saturday, November 7: Arkansas State is calling this one USA 250 Day, and it is also Heroes Day, Ag Day and Paragould Day, with the ROTC Hall of Heroes, an in-game commissioning ceremony and the 30th anniversary of the Ring of Honor. Darla Pickens says it is the busiest Saturday in Jonesboro since she can remember.

Remy Thibodeaux drove up from Monroe with a cooler of boudin and a grudge he has carried for a decade.

"One," he said, holding up a finger as he walked into Darla's tailgate. "One time we beat y'all in ten years. And it was last year. Twenty-eight to sixteen."

Darla runs a family farm outside town, and she explains football the way she explains soybeans: you plant, you wait, you harvest. "And nine times," she said, "we beat you."

That part is true. Arkansas State won 9 of the 10 meetings from 2016 through 2025. Some of them were wild. The Red Wolves won 67-50 in 2017 and 48-41 in 2019. Remy remembers both. He wishes he did not.

This fall has been hard for the Warhawks. UL Monroe is 1-7. It lost 13-62 at Mississippi State, 35-52 at South Alabama and 0-24 to Louisiana Tech. It scores 20.2 points a game and gives up 37.0. Remy does not hide from it. He just points to the one bright spot.

"We won at Troy," he said. "Twenty-one to fourteen. On the road. Aidan Armenta threw 2 touchdowns."

Darla gave him that one. Armenta has 1,323 yards and 10 touchdowns, with only 3 interceptions. Marcellus Jackson caught an 83-yard score last week against Southern Miss. Noah Flemmings has 75 tackles, and Kevontay Wells has 3 sacks. Remy calls Flemmings the bayou bouncer, because nobody gets past him without paying.

Arkansas State is 4-4, and Darla says the record does not tell the whole story. The Red Wolves lost 20-23 at Louisiana and 49-56 to South Alabama, and either of those could have gone the other way. Since then, they won 23-13 at Southern Miss and 38-32 over Georgia State. They have also had a week off to rest.

Trey Owens is the reason Darla sleeps well. He has 1,940 yards and 11 touchdowns. He threw for 418 against South Alabama and 309 against Georgia State. Jaylen Bonelli caught 7 balls for 150 yards in that last one. Joe Drew has 74 tackles from the safety spot. Solomon Baggett leads the team on the ground with 306 yards.

"Our defense gives up some," Darla admitted. "But your defense gives up more."

Remy had boudin in his mouth and could not argue.

Here is how it shakes out. Arkansas State comes out rested and loud, Owens finds Bonelli early, and the Red Wolves go up two scores before the first quarter ends. Armenta keeps UL Monroe in it for a while with some long throws, and Flemmings makes a dozen tackles, because he always does. But the Warhawks cannot slow Owens for four quarters. Arkansas State pulls away in the second half, and Darla's grill stays busy until dark.

The best part of the day happens before kickoff. The ROTC Hall of Heroes welcomes new names, and young officers take their oath right on the field in the commissioning ceremony. Darla has watched that ceremony for years, and she still tears up every time. Remy takes his hat off and stands for every word.

"That part," he said, "I can cheer for."

Then kickoff comes, and he goes right back to hollering for the Warhawks.

If the game gets out of hand, Darla says there is always the NEAVAL Art Show and Sale at the Harlan Henry Center that morning. Remy says he will go if they have a painting of the 2025 game.

My call: Arkansas State Red Wolves 37, UL Monroe Warhawks 19.

Delaware vs Kennesaw State prediction, spread and over/under for Saturday: I have Kennesaw State Owls +2.5 and Under 55.5, with Kennesaw State Owls 27, Delaware Blue Hens 26 as my final. Kickoff is 3:00 PM ET in Kennesaw, it is Homecoming and the Mental Health Awareness game at Fifth Third Stadium, and Taste of Kennesaw fills downtown with food and live music all day.

Pete Marchetti waves a Blue Hens towel like a semaphore flag. "Nick Minicucci threw for 414 at Western Kentucky. Sean Wilson caught 9 for 183. We've won two in a row."

Tasha Greer, an Owls lifer, is not impressed. "Pete, we just won 44-28 at Middle Tennessee. Rickie Collins went 16 for 19. And Ugonna Nwoha has 5 sacks."

Here is why I take the points. Kennesaw State is 2-6, but three of those losses were by a field goal or less: 14-17 at Arkansas State, 26-27 to Jacksonville State and 21-24 at Missouri State. The Owls finally broke through last week. Delaware is 4-4, and it gives up 27.5 a game. The Blue Hens lost 30-33 at Middle Tennessee, the same team the Owls just beat by 16. Delaware has also rotated quarterbacks: Minicucci, Braden Streeter, EJ Archield Jr. and Tyler Bell have each led in throws. My 27-26 is a one-point Owls win at home. DraftKings opened Delaware −3, and it is down to 2.5.

The risk is Minicucci. He has 14 touchdown throws and only 4 interceptions, and he threw 9 touchdowns in the last two games. Kennesaw State scores just 23.0 a game.

On the over/under, DraftKings opened at 51.5 and it has jumped to 55.5. I think that went too far. Kennesaw State scored 9 at Tennessee, 14 at Arkansas State and 6 against Liberty. The Owls give up 25.4 a game. My 27 and 26 make 53, two and a half under 55.5.

The room likes the home team. The Formula has Delaware 27-26 and takes Kennesaw State +2.5 with the Under. Next Man Up has Kennesaw State 29-26, takes the Owls +2.5, and likes the Under. In The Trenches takes Kennesaw State +2.5 as well, and it reads sides only with no score this week. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick. Letdown Watch has no score this week.

The Formula: "One point. I flipped a coin and the coin agreed with the column."

Next Man Up: "Homecoming crowd. Three points. I'll take my chances."

Tasha is spending the morning at Taste of Kennesaw before heading to the stadium. Pete says he will eat whatever she eats, as long as nobody makes him wear black and gold.

Delaware Blue Hens vs Kennesaw State Owls prediction for Saturday, November 7: it is Homecoming at Kennesaw State and the Mental Health Awareness game, Taste of Kennesaw takes over downtown from 11 in the morning until 6 at night, and Tasha Greer has a full plan for the day.

Pete Marchetti flew down from Wilmington and did not bring a plan. He brought a towel.

"Blue Hens!" he hollered at the tailgate, swinging the towel over his head. "Two in a row! Four hundred fourteen yards at Western Kentucky!"

Tasha is a nurse, and she has seen louder men calmed down by quieter words. "Pete," she said, "you're 4-4."

Pete stopped swinging. She was right. Delaware opened by beating Merrimack 42-7, then lost 26-35 at Vanderbilt and beat Coastal Carolina 22-14. After that it fell apart for a stretch: 3-42 at Virginia, 14-30 to Liberty, 30-33 at Middle Tennessee. Then the Blue Hens woke up. They beat Missouri State 61-38 and won 35-21 at Western Kentucky.

Nick Minicucci is the reason. He has 1,477 yards and 14 touchdowns with only 4 interceptions. He threw 5 touchdowns against Missouri State and 4 more at Western Kentucky, where he went 32 for 38 for 414 yards. Sean Wilson caught 9 balls for 183 yards in that one, and he has 591 on the year. Blake Matthews has 4.5 sacks. Gavin Moul has 53 tackles.

"He is a different quarterback now," Pete said. "You'll see."

Tasha has watched her own team fight through a long fall. Kennesaw State is 2-6, and almost all of it has been heartbreak. The Owls lost 14-17 at Arkansas State, 26-27 to Jacksonville State and 21-24 at Missouri State. Every one of those came down to the last few minutes. Tasha says she aged a year in October.

But last week was different. Kennesaw State went to Middle Tennessee and won 44-28. Rickie Collins went 16 for 19 with 3 touchdowns. Boogie Woods III ran for 2 more scores. Dylan Gary caught 2 balls, and both went for touchdowns. Tasha watched it twice.

"Middle Tennessee beat you," she reminded Pete. "Thirty-three to thirty. We beat them by 16."

Pete thought about that for a while. Football does not work that way, he said. Tasha said she knows, but it felt good to say.

The Owls have pieces. Collins has 1,632 yards through the air. Woods has 358 rushing yards and 6 touchdowns. Javon Rogers has 397 receiving yards. Ugonna Nwoha has 5 sacks up front, and Tywon Christopher has 62 tackles. Tasha thinks Nwoha is the key. If he gets to Minicucci early, the Blue Hens cannot get comfortable.

Homecoming also matters to her for another reason. This is the Mental Health Awareness game, and Tasha has spent her career in hospitals. She talks about checking on friends the way some people talk about stretching before a run. Pete got quiet when she said it. Then he said that was the best thing anybody had said at a tailgate all year, and he meant it. Tasha told him the best part of Homecoming is seeing who shows up for each other, win or lose, and that a towel-waving Blue Hens fan counts too.

Here is how it shakes out. Delaware moves the ball, because Minicucci is playing as well as anybody in this conference right now. Wilson gets loose once. But the home crowd is huge, Nwoha gets home a couple of times, and Woods grinds out the tough yards in the fourth quarter. It comes down to the last drive, like everything does with this Owls team. This time it goes their way.

After the game, if there is anything left at Taste of Kennesaw, Tasha wants a funnel cake and some live music. Pete says the towel comes too.

My call: Kennesaw State Owls 27, Delaware Blue Hens 26.

display.fanatic_story:
Alabama Crimson Tide vs LSU Tigers prediction for Saturday, November 7: the Fan Zone outside the PMAC is full of kids for the Mike's Kids Club Tailgate, with food, games and STEM activities, and Remy-Jean Fontenot has a pot of jambalaya going big enough to feed every one of them.

Hollis Dunaway walked into her tailgate in crimson from head to toe.

"Roll Tide," he said, like a man saying good morning.

"Geaux Tigers," Remy-Jean said, like a woman saying get out. Then she handed him a bowl, because that is how it works down here.

Hollis is a retired band director from Tuscaloosa, and he hears football like music: tempo, rhythm, a big finish. Remy-Jean is a Baton Rouge lawyer, and she argues football like a closing statement. They have been doing this for years.

"Eight of the last ten," Hollis said. "We won 20-9 last year. We won 42-13 the year before that."

"And we won 46-41 in 2019," Remy-Jean said. "And 32-31 in 2022. In overtime. I was there. You were there. You cried."

Hollis did not deny it.

This year, both teams are 6-2, and both of them can score. Alabama puts up 38.2 points a game. LSU puts up 40.1. The difference is defense. LSU gives up 16.0 a game, the fewest in this matchup by a lot. Alabama gives up 21.2.

"Keelon Russell," Hollis said, counting it out on his fingers like a downbeat. "Two thousand fifty-seven yards. Fifteen touchdowns. Five interceptions. He threw for 365 against South Carolina and 311 against Texas A&M."

The Tide have only stumbled twice. They lost 17-20 to Georgia and 10-26 at Tennessee. Lotzeir Brooks has 488 receiving yards. Rico Scott caught 6 balls for 156 yards against the Aggies. Caleb Woodson has 63 tackles, and Yhonzae Pierre has 3.5 sacks.

Remy-Jean let him finish. Then she began her closing.

"Sam Leavitt," she said. "Two thousand one hundred seventy-three yards. Seventeen touchdowns. He went 32 for 45 for 388 yards at Auburn. Jackson Harris caught 9 for 178 that day. Dilin Jones has 657 rushing yards. And Princewill Umanmielen has 8.5 sacks."

"Eight and a half," Hollis said quietly.

"Eight and a half," she repeated, like a verdict.

LSU's two losses came on the road: 24-32 at Ole Miss and 34-35 in overtime at Kentucky. At home, the Tigers have been a wall. They beat Clemson 51-10, Texas A&M 35-6 and Mississippi State 31-0. Remy-Jean says Tiger Stadium does that to people.

Hollis says Alabama has been to Tiger Stadium before.

Here is how it shakes out. Russell comes out sharp, Brooks gets behind the defense once, and the Tide quiet the crowd for a few minutes. But Leavitt answers, Jones runs hard, and Umanmielen gets home at the worst possible moment for Alabama. It is a shootout into the fourth quarter, the kind both of them will talk about for years. Alabama has the ball late with a chance, and Hollis is on his feet. LSU makes one more stop.

Hollis will say the band was better. Remy-Jean will say that is not how scoring works.

Before any of that, she is taking her nieces to the Mike's Kids Club Tailgate in the Fan Zone. There is a meal package for kids, and there are STEM tables where you can build things and break things. Hollis says that sounds like an Alabama practice. Remy-Jean says he can come along if he keeps the crimson zipped under a jacket.

He agrees, mostly because the jambalaya is that good. By the time they reach the PMAC, he has helped two kids build a paper bridge and lost an argument with a little girl about who has the better mascot. Remy-Jean says that is the only argument he will lose all day. Hollis says the day is young.

My call: LSU Tigers 31, Alabama Crimson Tide 27.

Cincinnati Bearcats vs Houston Cougars prediction for Saturday, November 7: Houston is hosting its 13th Annual AfriFest across town at The KBC Houston Event Center, with music, food and culture from 11 in the morning until 7 at night, and Marisol Treviño has already told everybody she is going.

Gus Bellweather flew down from Cincinnati with a Bearcats hoodie and a list.

"Five of the last six," he said, unfolding the list at Marisol's tailgate. "Thirty-four to nothing in 2024. Twenty-four to fourteen in 2023. Thirty-five to twenty in 2021. Shall I go on?"

Marisol is a Houston engineer, and she builds her arguments the way she builds bridges: load first, then style. "You can go on," she said. "Or you can look at what happened last Saturday."

Gus folded the list back up.

Last Saturday, Cincinnati lost 25-49 to Utah at home. Cole Tabb ran for 131 yards and a touchdown, but the defense could not stop anything. That has been the story of the Bearcats' fall. They are 5-3, they score 34.1 points a game and they give up 29.2. They lost 7-34 at Arizona and 42-45 at West Virginia. They also beat Kansas State 31-26 and Texas Tech 37-24, so they are dangerous on any given day.

"Cole Tabb," Gus said, recovering. "Seven hundred fifty-two yards. Ten touchdowns. JC French IV has 13 touchdown throws and 3 interceptions. We do not give the ball away."

That is true, and Marisol knows it. French is careful, and JV Gibson has 461 receiving yards. Jonathan Thompson has 63 tackles, and Patrick Bauer has 3.5 sacks.

Houston is 6-2, and Marisol thinks it is the best Cougars team she has seen in years. Conner Weigman has 2,053 yards, 20 touchdowns and just 2 interceptions. He threw 5 touchdowns in a 35-32 win over Oklahoma State and 4 more in a 35-16 win at Kansas State. Amare Thomas has 620 receiving yards. Makhi Hughes has 516 rushing yards. The defense gives up 21.0 points a game, and Kentrell Webb has 46 tackles from the back of it.

"You lost at Utah too," Gus said.

"Thirteen to twenty-one," Marisol said. "And then we had two weeks to think about it."

Houston has not played since Oct 24, so the Cougars come in rested. Marisol thinks a rested Weigman is the most dangerous player on the field. Gus says Tabb has fresher legs than anybody, because he runs so fast nobody touches him. Marisol says that is not how legs work.

Here is how it shakes out. Tabb breaks a long one early, and for a quarter Gus looks like a man about to add another entry to his list. But Houston settles in. Weigman starts finding Thomas on third downs, Hughes grinds out the tough yards, and the Cougars build a lead before halftime. Cincinnati keeps scoring, because it always does, but the defense cannot get off the field. Houston pulls away in the fourth quarter.

Gus will fly home with his list a little shorter. Marisol says she will mail him a new one. He says he will frame it next to the old one, because a Bearcats fan never throws away proof of the good years. She tells him the good years are a lot like Houston weather in November: pleasant while they last, and gone before you notice.

In the morning, she is taking him to AfriFest. The Nigerian American Multicultural Council hosts it every year, and Marisol says it is the best food in Houston for one day. Gus says he will try everything once. Marisol says he should start with the jollof rice and work from there.

My call: Houston Cougars 37, Cincinnati Bearcats 24.

Merrimack vs Wake Forest prediction for Saturday: there is no line posted yet on this game. ESPN has no spread and no over/under up as of early Tuesday, so I have no side and no over/under call on it. What I do have is a final score, Wake Forest Demon Deacons 41, Merrimack Warriors 10, and the reasons behind it. Kickoff is 3:30 PM ET in Winston-Salem, and it is Homecoming, with Deacon fans asked to wear gold for the Gold Rush game.

Eloise Brightman-Rowe has the gold blazer out already. "No line? Fine. I don't need a market to tell me what a 51-7 win over Virginia looks like."

That is the first thing to know. Wake Forest is 7-1, No. 14, and it has won five in a row since a 20-33 loss to Miami on September 18. display.fanatic_story:
Merrimack Warriors vs Wake Forest Demon Deacons prediction for Saturday, November 7: it is Homecoming in Winston-Salem, the Quad is getting its annual paper decorating, and Eloise Brightman-Rowe has a gold blazer pressed and a roll of toilet paper on her keychain for the occasion.

"Gold Rush game," she says. "Everybody wears gold. If you show up in anything else, I will hand you a rebuttal and a scarf."

She means it. Wake Forest is asking every fan to wear gold, and the football program is again partnering with Brenner Children's Hospital to raise money and awareness for childhood cancer. There is a Golden Deacs lunch, Party So Dear, a Festival on the Quad, the Alumni Tailgate and a pile of class reunions, so half the people in the stands will be catching up with somebody they lived down the hall from twenty years ago. Over in Ardmore, the art walk puts 100 artists on front lawns from 11 a.m., which Eloise calls the warm-up act.

Kickoff is 3:30 p.m. ET. This is the first meeting ever between the Demon Deacons and the Warriors, and that is the part Eloise keeps circling back to.

"We don't know them," she says. "They don't know us. That is how upsets get written. I have read those essays. I have graded those essays."

Here is the honest picture. Wake Forest is 7-1, ranked No. 14, and 5-1 against the conference. The only loss came on September 18, 20-33 to Miami. Since then the Deacs have won five in a row, and they have not been close lately. They beat Stanford 57-3. They won 38-14 at NC State. They went to California and won 41-7. Last Saturday they beat Virginia 51-7. Across eight games they score 39.1 a game and allow 17.9.

"That last month reads like a closing argument," Eloise says. "And the closing argument is: sit down."

The offense runs through Gio Lopez. He has 2,176 yards, 18 touchdown throws and 1 interception, and that last figure is the one Eloise taps on the table. Carlos Hernandez has 57 catches for 856 yards and 5 touchdowns. Ty Clark III has 376 rushing yards and 7 touchdowns. On defense, Langston Hardy has 5.5 sacks and Vincent Firenze leads the team with 52 tackles.

"Firenze tackles like he read the syllabus," Eloise says. "Everybody else on that field is cramming."

Now Merrimack, because the Warriors deserve a fair hearing, and Eloise was on the debate team, so she knows how to give one. Merrimack comes down from Massachusetts at 4-5, but it is playing its best football right now. The Warriors have won two in a row, 24-17 over New Hampshire and 19-14 over Wagner, and three of their last five, with a 17-10 win over New Haven before that. They also won 23-14 at Maine in September. Matthias Latham is the workhorse, 121 carries for 623 yards. AJ Hairston Jr has thrown for 1,362 yards with 7 touchdowns and 6 interceptions. Austin Palmer has 25 catches for 417 yards, and Danny Simms has 57 tackles, more than anybody on Wake's roster.

"Fifty-seven tackles," Eloise says. "That's a man who has had to make a lot of tackles. I respect that. I also know why."

The tough part for Merrimack is the road. The Warriors opened with a 7-34 home loss to Rhode Island, and on the road they lost 7-42 at Delaware, 20-45 at Tarleton State, 24-41 at Yale and 21-27 at Dartmouth. They score 18.0 a game and give up 27.1. The Delaware game is the closest thing to a measuring stick, and that one got away early.

There is also history on Wake's side, just not with Merrimack. The Deacs have won their last 20 games against FCS opponents, going back to 2000.

"Twenty in a row," Eloise says. "I was in grade school for the first one. I have opinions about all of them."

So how does it play out? The building is gold and loud early, and Wake goes right at it. Lopez gets the ball to Hernandez on the outside, and Clark finishes a drive or two in close. Merrimack tries to keep it on the ground with Latham, shorten the afternoon and keep Lopez on the sideline, and for a quarter that works well enough to make the visitors' section happy. Hairston hits Palmer for a big gain at some point, because good teams give up one of those. But Hardy gets home, the Deacs' defense that held Stanford, California and Virginia to single digits does it again, and by the fourth quarter the reunion classes are taking pictures instead of watching.

Eloise rolls the Quad that night with the Class of 2016. Merrimack goes home with a first trip to Winston-Salem and a story to tell, and with Monmouth and Sacred Heart still ahead, the Warriors have plenty to play for.

"Roll the Quad!" she says. "Then be nice to the visitors. They drove a long way."

My call: Wake Forest Demon Deacons 41, Merrimack Warriors 10.

Oregon Ducks vs Ohio State Buckeyes prediction for Saturday, November 7: Ohio State has called this one Scarlet the Shoe, every fan in the Horseshoe is asked to wear scarlet, and Bud Kowalczyk has been laying out sweaters on his tailgate table since dawn.

Ingrid Halvorsen showed up in green. Of course she did.

"You know what today is," Bud said.

"I know what today is," Ingrid said. "It is the day my Ducks come into your house and remind you about USC."

Bud winced. He is a retired steelworker from Youngstown, and he explains football like a mill shift: you show up, you work, you go home tired. He did not enjoy last Saturday. Ohio State lost 18-30 at USC, and Luke Fahey led the Buckeyes in throws that day instead of Julian Sayin. Bud does not want to talk about why. Ingrid did not ask.

"We are 6-2," he said. "We give up 15.5 points a game. We lost by a point at Texas and we lost at USC. That is it."

That is it. Ohio State beat Illinois 42-19, Iowa 31-14, Maryland 45-16 and Indiana 19-15. Sayin has 2,007 yards, 19 touchdowns and 4 interceptions. Jeremiah Smith has 62 catches for 1,067 yards and 13 touchdowns. Bo Jackson has 637 rushing yards. Earl Little Jr. has 43 tackles, and Kenyatta Jackson Jr. has 3 sacks. The Buckeyes score 36.6 points a game.

"Jeremiah Smith," Bud said, "is the best player in America. Write that down."

Ingrid wrote nothing down. She is a software designer from Portland, and she thinks about football like a product launch: the version you ship matters more than the version you planned.

Oregon has shipped a few versions this year. Dante Moore led the Ducks in throws early, including 378 yards against Boise State. Dylan Raiola took over and threw for 289 in a 41-27 win at USC. Brock Thomas led them in throws against Nebraska. Now Raiola is back, and last week he went 22 for 31 for 336 yards and 3 touchdowns in a 34-26 win over Northwestern. Dakorien Moore caught 7 balls for 128 yards and 2 scores in that one.

"We beat USC by 14," Ingrid said. "You lost to USC by 12. Math."

Bud said football does not work that way. Ingrid said it worked fine for her.

Oregon is 5-3, and the losses have been close and frustrating: 31-39 at Oklahoma State, 15-17 to UCLA, 10-21 at Illinois. Jordon Davison has 439 rushing yards and 7 touchdowns. Matayo Uiagalelei has 6.5 sacks, and Koi Perich has 53 tackles. The Ducks give up 21.4 points a game.

Here is how it shakes out. Oregon comes out fast, Uiagalelei gets into the backfield early, and for a few minutes the Horseshoe is very quiet. But Ohio State settles in. Smith makes a catch that nobody else in the country makes, Bo Jackson pounds away in the third quarter, and the Buckeyes' defense keeps Raiola from finding Moore deep. Oregon scores enough to keep Ingrid hopeful into the fourth quarter. Ohio State pulls away late.

Bud will celebrate the way he always does, by hugging people he does not know. Ingrid will say the next meeting is in Eugene, and she will mean it as a warning.

Before kickoff, Bud holds out a scarlet sweater. Ingrid looks at it for a long time. She agrees to wear it for exactly one photo, for Scarlet the Shoe, and then the green comes right back on. Bud frames the photo anyway. He says it will hang in his garage next to his old ticket stubs, the ones he never lets anybody touch. Ingrid says she will send him a green frame for it. Bud says he would sooner wear the sweater to Eugene. She says that can be arranged.

My call: Ohio State Buckeyes 31, Oregon Ducks 21.

Penn State has not played a game on Montlake in more than a century, and the Huskies picked Homecoming to welcome them back. Luann Kessler wants the record shown that her team is the guest who brought a casserole.

"Two and a half points is the price of a Creamery cone," Luann says. "I'll take the cone and the points."

Vangie Tollefsrud, who rowed past this stadium at dawn more times than she can count, does not blink. "Luann, it rains on the visitors first. That's just science."

Why Penn State with the points: the Nittany Lions score 29.0 a game and give up 18.6, which is the better split of the two. Rocco Becht has thrown for 1,839 yards with 13 touchdowns against 5 interceptions, and Sowell has 34 catches for 510 yards. The run game showed up last week when Wallace went 22 carries for 135 yards in the 31-17 win over Purdue. Washington has Demond Williams Jr., who has 1,495 yards and 9 touchdowns through the air, but Elijah Brown has taken most of the throws the last three games, and he went 19 of 30 for 136 yards in the 17-10 win at Nebraska. That is a short-field offense, and a field goal game inside 2.5 is exactly where the dog lives.

On the over/under, DraftKings opened at 44.5 and it sits there now. We're on the Over 44.5. The Huskies score 26.5 and allow 21.1. Lawson caught 12 balls for 155 yards last game and has 44 for 638 on the year, so Washington has a chain-mover when Brown needs one. Penn State's defense is good, with Rojas at 5 sacks and 57 tackles, but 24 and 23 gets you there with a little room to spare.

The room splits on the side. The Formula likes Penn State +2.5 and has it Penn State 25-23. Next Man Up lands on Washington −2.5 without backing it hard and has it Washington 26-22. In The Trenches likes Penn State +2.5. The Formula likes the Over. Next Man Up likes the Over too. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick. Letdown Watch has no score this week.

The last meeting went Penn State 35-6 in 2024 in State College. This one is in Seattle, and the Huskies have won two straight since.

Vangie gets the last word before kickoff. "Bring a rain shell, Luann. And bring the points, you'll need them."

"I brought both," Luann says.

Penn State Nittany Lions vs Washington Huskies prediction for Saturday, November 7: Penn State is coming to Husky Stadium for the first time in 105 years, and Washington made sure the welcome party is Homecoming. Vangie Tollefsrud says she has been waiting for this since she was a freshman on the water at dawn, and Luann Kessler says she has been waiting since 1921, which is not true but she said it with a straight face.

Here's the deal. The last time Penn State played on Montlake was the final game of the 1921 season. It was the seventh game ever played at Husky Stadium. This time the Huskies are calling it the Purple Reign Game, and it opens with the Blanket Parade, when former Washington letterwinners stand along the field to welcome the team back out. Kickoff is 3:30 p.m. ET.

"A blanket parade," Luann says. "That's sweet. In Happy Valley we just call that November."

Vangie sets down her third coffee of the morning. "Luann, the blankets are for you. We're polite people. We figured you'd be cold."

The Nittany Lions brought company. Penn State's alumni group booked its first-ever Sailgate, a cruise on Lake Washington aboard the Spirit of Seattle with the Pep Band trumpets, the cheerleaders and the Nittany Lion himself, and it sold out. Washington parents are coming in too, since it doubles as UW Family Weekend, complete with a family section and a scarf.

"Penn State fans on a boat on my lake," Vangie says. "I rowed that lake in the rain for four years. You people get a buffet."

"We get a buffet and a trumpet section," Luann says. "Try to keep up."

Now the football, because these two came to argue.

Luann goes first. Rocco Becht has thrown for 1,839 yards with 13 touchdowns and 5 interceptions. Chase Sowell is the go-to guy with 34 catches for 510 yards. Carson Hansen leads the ground game with 374 yards, but the back everybody in State College is talking about this week is Cam Wallace, who ran 22 times for 135 yards in the 31-17 win over Purdue. And then there's Tony Rojas, the linebacker who leads the team in sacks with 5 and tackles with 57. Penn State scores 29.0 a game and gives up 18.6.

"Linebacker U," Luann says. "Rojas is the Peachy Paterno of linebackers. Sweet on the outside, and then he takes your quarterback home."

Vangie takes the floor. Demond Williams Jr. has thrown for 1,495 yards and 9 touchdowns, but Elijah Brown has been the guy taking most of the throws in the last three games, including 19 of 30 for 136 yards in the 17-10 win at Nebraska. Chris Lawson made that day happen with 12 catches for 155 yards, and he has 44 catches for 638 yards this season. Alex McLaughlin leads the defense with 56 tackles, and Jacob Manu has 2.5 sacks. Washington scores 26.5 a game and allows 21.1.

"Lawson against Nebraska was a coxswain calling the stroke," Vangie says. "Every catch right on the beat."

"Seventeen to ten," Luann says. "Very rhythmic. Very low."

"We won in Lincoln in November," Vangie says. "Nobody scores in Lincoln in November. You lost 18-21 at Michigan."

Luann does not respond to that. She looks out the window at the drizzle like it owes her money.

Both teams have been through it. Penn State dropped four straight in the middle of the season, including 20-24 to Wisconsin, 23-31 to USC and that 18-21 loss in Ann Arbor, before getting right against Purdue. Washington lost three in a row too, to Minnesota, at USC and to Iowa, then won at Purdue and at Nebraska.

"We have both been to the dark place," Luann says.

"Ours has better coffee," Vangie says.

There's one more thing Luann wants on the record. The last time these two met, in 2024, Penn State won 35-6.

"That was in State College," Vangie says. "Rain doesn't count when it's yours."

Here's how it plays out on Montlake. The Blanket Parade gets the place loud early, and the Washington defense, led by McLaughlin, keeps the Penn State run game honest in the first half. Becht and Sowell find a rhythm before halftime, and Wallace grinds out the hard yards. Brown looks for Lawson every time Washington needs a first down, and Rojas makes the Husky backfield miserable at least twice. Nobody gets away. It comes down to one last Washington drive and a kick that splits the uprights while the rain gets heavier.

Vangie leaps out of her seat and nearly spills her coffee. Luann says Linebacker U doesn't cry, then cries a little, then buys a Washington scarf anyway because it's cold.

My call: Washington Huskies 24, Penn State Nittany Lions 23.

display.fanatic_story:
Charlotte 49ers vs UAB Blazers prediction for Saturday, November 7: Protective Stadium turns into Kids Takeover, the Blazers wear gray jerseys with 99 children's names on the back, and Ozella Birchfield has already ironed her gray sweater twice. Priya Halloran drove down from uptown Charlotte with a spreadsheet, a thermos and the calm face of a woman who has watched her team go 1-7.

Here's the deal. Saturday is the 10th annual Children's Harbor Game. Since the first one in 2017, UAB players have swapped their own names off the backs of their jerseys for the names of kids facing serious medical challenges, and each child gets the jersey worn in their honor after the game. More than 400 tickets and parking tickets were bought for the families. Fans are asked to wear gray. The Blazers are 8-1 in these games.

"I'm going to cry before kickoff," Ozella says. "Then I'm going to yell. In that order. Every year."

Priya nods. "That's a beautiful tradition. I'm still wearing teal. I'll clap in teal."

There's also a display in Blazer Village this week called "Derail the Niners." Priya has seen it.

"Derail," she says. "Clever jab. We already derailed ourselves in September. You can't derail a train that's in the shop."

"Forged, not given," Ozella says. "Birmingham was a train town before it was anything. We know what a derailment looks like."

Kickoff is 3:30 p.m. ET, and before that the Blazer Walk brings the team through Uptown with the Marching Blazers. UAB is 4-0 at Protective this season, which Ozella will tell you about whether you ask or not.

Now the football.

Priya goes first, and she goes first because she has the better story to tell, even at 1-7. Charlotte's season turned when Conner Harrell took over at quarterback. He has 831 yards with 5 touchdowns and just 2 interceptions, and in his three games the 49ers won 38-31 at Temple and took Tulane to overtime before losing 31-38. Henry Rutledge leads the ground game with 452 yards, and he ran 22 times for 121 yards against Tulane. Jaden Barnes has 48 catches for 462 yards. Gavin Willis leads the defense with 65 tackles.

"The first five games were a write-down," Priya says. "Since then we're a turnaround story. I'd hold."

Ozella takes the floor. Ryder Burton has thrown for 1,333 yards. Rod Robinson II has 450 rushing yards. CJ Smith is the big-play guy with 21 catches for 403 yards, which is a lot of yards for not many catches. Then there's the defense. Marlin Dean has 7.5 sacks, and Muaaz Byard leads the team with 76 tackles.

"Marlin Dean is a blast furnace," Ozella says. "You open the door, you get burned."

"Your team lost 10-30 at South Florida last week," Priya says.

"And we beat Navy 24-20 in September," Ozella says. "Furnaces have off days. The fire doesn't go out."

Charlotte scores 20.6 a game and gives up 40.2. UAB scores 21.6 and allows 25.2. Ozella keeps reading the 40.2 out loud like it's a hymn.

"I know that figure," Priya says. "I put it in red. It has been in red since September."

The recent history is even. Going back to 2017, they've split four meetings, two apiece. Charlotte won the last one, 29-27 in 2024, and Priya remembers the Thanksgiving weekend drive home like it was a victory lap at Charlotte Motor Speedway.

"Two and two," Ozella says. "Somebody breaks it Saturday."

"Somebody always does," Priya says.

Here's how it plays out under the Birmingham sky. The building is gray and loud early, and the Blazers come out flying in those jerseys. Robinson gets UAB rolling on the ground, and Smith catches a long one over the top that makes Ozella stand on her chair. Charlotte stays in it longer than anybody in Uptown wants, with Harrell finding Barnes on third downs and Rutledge running hard. But Dean gets home a couple of times in the second half, and Byard is everywhere. UAB pulls away in the fourth quarter, and the kids on the jerseys get the afternoon they deserve.

Ozella hugs a stranger in gray. Priya opens a spreadsheet tab called "Write-Downs," adds one more row, and then shuts the laptop and claps for the kids anyway, in teal.

My call: UAB Blazers 33, Charlotte 49ers 22.

Temple vs Navy prediction: our pick is Temple Owls +7.5, we're on the Under 53.5, and the final we're calling is Navy Midshipmen 30, Temple Owls 23. Kickoff is 3:30 PM ET Saturday in Annapolis, where the spread opened at Navy −7.5 and has not moved off it.

Navy is 2-6 and so is Temple, which makes this a game for people who love football and nobody else. Teddy Fiorella, who has never left North Philly without a gym bag, is fine with that. Cmdr. (Ret.) Annabel Merriweather is not.

"Seven and a half is a lot of hook for a team that just lost by 22 to Notre Dame," Teddy says.

"Notre Dame is not Temple, Theodore," Annabel says. "Adjust your heading."

Why Temple with the points: last year's game was decided by one point, 32-31, and the last nine meetings split five for Navy and four for Temple. These programs play close. Navy gives up 29.9 a game, and it lost 39-49 at home to North Texas and 34-38 at UTSA in back-to-back weeks. Temple has Ajani Sheppard, who has 1,245 yards with 8 touchdowns and only 3 interceptions, though all three came in the 9-17 loss at East Carolina. Keveun Mason has 564 rushing yards, so Temple can grind a little too. A team that can run the ball and shorten the game is how you stay inside a touchdown and a hook.

On the over/under, DraftKings opened at 52.5 and it is up a point to 53.5. We're on the Under 53.5. Navy's offense is Jackson Gutierrez running the ball, with 979 yards and 13 touchdowns on the ground. That keeps the clock moving. He also has 717 yards through the air, mostly on a handful of throws a game. Temple only scores 23.6 a game. Both teams want long drives, and long drives eat the second half.

The room splits both ways. The Formula lands on Temple +7.5 without backing it hard and has it Navy 30-24. Next Man Up lands on Navy −7.5 without backing it hard and has it Navy 30-21. In The Trenches has no side this week. The Formula lands on the Over without backing it hard. Next Man Up lands on the Under without backing it hard. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick. Letdown Watch has no score this week.

Curly Ordonez has 77 tackles for Temple, and he is going to see a lot of Gutierrez. Navy's Coleman Cauley has 63 tackles and MarcAnthony Parker has 4 sacks. Neither defense is going to shut the other down. That is why we think Navy wins by a touchdown and not by more.

"Ya gotta take a punch, Commander," Teddy says.

"Then keep your guard up, Theodore," Annabel says.

Temple Owls vs Navy Midshipmen prediction for Saturday, November 7: both teams walk into Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium at 2-6, and Teddy Fiorella says that makes it the most honest game in America. Cmdr. (Ret.) Annabel Merriweather says it makes it a game where somebody gets to stop the bleeding, and she has a chart showing which way the current runs.

Here's the deal. Kickoff in Annapolis is 3:30 p.m. ET. Before that, the Navy Football Brotherhood sets up its tailgate at Gate 5 and Taylor Avenue at noon, and the Naval Academy classes of 2011, 2016 and 2021 are back for their 15th, 10th and 5th reunions. This is also the season the stadium is marking the 100th anniversary of Navy's 1926 national championship team.

"Nineteen twenty-six," Teddy says. "In Philly we were busy inventing everything else."

"In Annapolis we were busy winning a national title, Theodore," Annabel says. "Note it in the log."

The stadium got new food this year too, including cream of crab soup and coffee from Travelin' Tom's in Annapolis. And in the southwest corner of the stadium, fans can take photos with a Blue Angel and a Marine Corps Harrier.

"Cream of crab soup," Teddy says. "Fancy. Where's the cheesesteak?"

"In Philadelphia," Annabel says. "Where you left it."

Teddy is wearing a Temple hoodie and running shoes. He jogged the steps at the stadium twice before anybody else showed up. Annabel watched him from the parking lot with a coffee and said nothing, which is the most frightening thing she can do.

Now the football.

Teddy goes first, because he is louder. Ajani Sheppard has 1,245 yards with 8 touchdowns and 3 interceptions, and yes, all three interceptions came in the 9-17 loss at East Carolina last week. Keveun Mason is the workhorse with 564 rushing yards. Colin Chase leads the receivers with 330 yards. And then there's Curly Ordonez, the linebacker, who leads the team with 77 tackles and 2 sacks.

"Ordonez is a Philly guy in spirit," Teddy says. "He'll hit you, then help you up, then hit you again."

Annabel takes the floor. Jackson Gutierrez runs the Navy offense, and he does it on the ground. He has 979 rushing yards and 13 rushing touchdowns, plus 717 yards through the air on very few throws. Jordan Collins, the tight end, has 212 receiving yards on just 6 catches. Coleman Cauley leads the defense with 63 tackles, and MarcAnthony Parker has 4 sacks.

"Gutierrez is a destroyer escort," Annabel says. "Low profile. Hard to stop. Keeps coming."

"Your team gave up 49 to North Texas," Teddy says.

"Steady as she goes," Annabel says. "And your team lost to Charlotte."

Teddy does sit-ups on the spot. Out of spite.

The numbers say these two belong together. Temple scores 23.6 a game and gives up 26.6. Navy scores 27.6 and gives up 29.9. Over the last nine meetings, Navy won five and Temple won four. Last year Navy won 32-31.

"One point," Teddy says. "One point, Commander."

"A point is a point," Annabel says. "Ask anyone who has docked a ship."

Both teams are coming off a bad week. Temple lost at East Carolina. Navy lost 13-35 to Notre Dame. Navy also dropped close ones at UTSA, 34-38, and at UAB, 20-24.

Here's how it plays out on the Severn. Navy keeps the ball for long, grinding drives, and Gutierrez carries it over and over. Temple answers with Mason on the ground and a couple of big throws from Sheppard to Chase. Ordonez makes a big stop in the third quarter that makes Teddy run up and down his row like it's the art museum steps. But Navy's running game wears on Temple in the fourth quarter, and Cauley gets the stop the Midshipmen need. It's a one-score game until late.

Annabel rings an imaginary ship's bell and says "Anchors aweigh." Teddy says you gotta take a punch, takes the punch, and asks where the cream of crab soup stand is.

My call: Navy Midshipmen 30, Temple Owls 23.

display.fanatic_story:
Marshall Thundering Herd vs Georgia Southern Eagles prediction for Saturday, November 7: it's Homecoming in Statesboro, it's Military Appreciation Day at Paulson Stadium, and Royce Ogeechee has been at the Bishop Alumni Center since before the coffee was ready. Mercy Holderby drove down from Huntington in a green sweater, green socks and, she swears, green earrings she was born wearing.

Here's the deal. Georgia Southern is rolling Homecoming and Military Appreciation Day into one, and the alumni tailgate at the Bishop Alumni Center runs from noon until 3 p.m. as a Salute to Service tailgate for active-duty service members, veterans and military families. Kickoff is 3:30 p.m. ET.

And this one has history. Saturday is the 11th all-time meeting between these two schools. They played six times from 1989 to 1996, back when both were two of the most famous programs in I-AA, and then picked it back up when Marshall joined the Sun Belt in 2022.

"I-AA," Royce says, and his eyes get wet. "The option. The buses. Beautiful Eagle Creek. Mercy, those were the days."

"Those were our days too, Royce," Mercy says. "Huntington remembers every one of those games."

"So does Statesboro," Royce says. "Every single snap."

Mercy lets that one sit. She's a nurse. She has patience, and she has a long memory.

The last three meetings were decided by a combined 11 points. Marshall won 38-33 in 2023. Georgia Southern won 24-23 in 2024 and 24-19 last year in Huntington.

"Five points, one point, five points," Royce says. "Y'all keep making me nervous."

"Good," Mercy says.

Now the football.

Royce goes first, because it's his house. Max Johnson has thrown for 1,924 yards with 11 touchdowns and only 2 interceptions. Against App State last week he went 36 of 47 for 327 yards in a 19-3 win. Alex Taylor is his go-to guy, with 34 catches for 435 yards, and he caught 10 against App. On defense, Anthony Bynum has 5 sacks, and Brandon Tyson leads the team with 39 tackles. Georgia Southern gives up 20.5 a game.

"Our defense held App to 3," Royce says. "Three. That's a peanut-sized number, and I know peanuts."

Mercy takes the floor. Marshall is 5-3, and the Herd won 36-23 at Old Dominion last week. Carlos Del Rio-Wilson has 1,107 passing yards, and Zion Turner has taken his share of snaps too. Judah Price leads the ground game with 319 yards and ran for 82 at Old Dominion. Xayvion Turner-Bradshaw has 372 receiving yards and 4 touchdowns. Caleb Clark-Glover leads the defense with 59 tackles, and Kelvon McBride has 3 sacks.

"We are 5-3," Mercy says. "Say it with me. Five and three."

"Y'all also lost 0-45 at Penn State," Royce says.

"September," Mercy says. "That was September. We are a November team."

Marshall scores 23.5 a game and gives up 29.8. Georgia Southern scores 23.8 and gives up 20.5. Mercy reads the Marshall defense figure, then closes her eyes like she's checking a pulse.

"It's going to be fine," she says. "It's always fine. We rebuild. That's what we do."

Royce takes his hat off for that one. Everybody in Statesboro knows what Marshall means when it says that.

Here's how it plays out in Statesboro. The Homecoming crowd is loud, and the veterans honored before kickoff get the biggest cheer of the day. Johnson gets the Eagles moving early with Taylor on short throws, and Georgia Southern punches in a couple of scores before halftime. Marshall stays in it with Price running hard and Turner-Bradshaw making a big catch down the sideline. But Bynum gets home on a third down in the third quarter, and the Eagles turn it into points. The Herd fights to the end, the way the Herd always does, but Georgia Southern pulls away late.

Royce cracks a bag of boiled peanuts and hugs a veteran at the tailgate. Mercy hums "We Are" all the way to the car, sniffles once, and promises Royce that Huntington will remember this.

My call: Georgia Southern Eagles 31, Marshall Thundering Herd 19.

Western Kentucky Hilltoppers vs Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders prediction for Saturday, November 7: it's Homecoming at Floyd Stadium, it's the Hall of Fame Game, and Opal Stonebriar brought two casseroles, one for her people and one for Thurman "Tops" Whitsitt, because she's going to feed you before she corrects you. Tops drove down from Bowling Green with a hot towel still slung over one shoulder from his last customer.

Here's the deal. This is Middle Tennessee's first November Homecoming since 2008, and the Blue Raiders are making a whole day of it. It's also Youth Sports Day and Blue Raider Kids Club Day, so kids walk in the Homecoming parade and form the high-five tunnel when the team runs out. Kickoff is 3:30 p.m. ET in Murfreesboro.

"A high-five tunnel," Tops says. "Very sweet. We'll wave on our way through."

"Thurman, the children will remember your manners," Opal says. "Mind them."

Floyd Stadium opened in 1933. It holds 27,303 people. The Blue Raiders are 55-29-2 all-time on Homecoming, and 21-9-2 in Homecoming games played in November. Opal has those figures written inside the lid of her casserole dish.

"I didn't need to know that," Tops says.

"Everybody needs to know that," Opal says.

But this is a rivalry, and Tops has his own figures. Western Kentucky leads the all-time series 39-35-1. The Hilltoppers have won 7 in a row and nine of the last ten. Last year was 42-26. In Murfreesboro, though, Middle Tennessee leads 21-17-1, which is the one fact Opal holds onto like a hymnal.

"Seven straight," Tops says, polishing an imaginary razor. "That's a lot of fresh haircuts, Opal."

"Aren't you sweet for counting," Opal says. "Now count to 21-17-1."

Now the football.

Tops goes first, unhurried, like he has all afternoon. Brock Glenn is the guy for Western Kentucky. He has 887 passing yards, and he leads the team in rushing with 451 yards and 5 touchdowns. Against Delaware he ran 17 times for 129 yards. Jonathan Stafford Jr. leads the receivers with 46 catches for 433 yards. On defense, Jaylen Lewis has 62 tackles and Westen Ard has 2.5 sacks.

"Glenn is a straight-razor quarterback," Tops says. "Smooth, quick, and you don't see him coming."

Opal takes the floor. Roman Gagliano has thrown for 1,587 yards with 12 touchdowns. Cam'ron Lacy is his go-to target, or as Opal calls him, "my boy," with 45 catches for 510 yards. Antonio Martin leads the ground game with 586 yards, and he ran for 106 against Kennesaw State. Korey Smith leads the defense with 73 tackles.

"Korey Smith is the deacon of that defense," Opal says. "He keeps everybody in their pew."

"You gave up 44 to Kennesaw State last week," Tops says.

"We did," Opal says, setting down the casserole spoon very carefully. "And you gave up 35 to Delaware. Hand me the rolls."

Both teams have had a tough fall. Western Kentucky is 3-5 and gives up 31.1 a game. Middle Tennessee is 4-4 and gives up 29.6. Both offenses can score. Both defenses have had rough weeks.

"So it's a shootout," Tops says.

"It's a homecoming," Opal says. "Different thing. More casseroles."

Here's how it plays out in Murfreesboro. The kids give the Blue Raiders a loud send-off through the high-five tunnel, and Middle Tennessee comes out swinging with Gagliano hitting Lacy early. Glenn answers with his legs, breaking a long run that makes Tops stand up in the visitors' section. It goes back and forth all afternoon. Martin grinds out tough yards in the fourth quarter, Korey Smith makes a stop on WKU's last real chance, and the Homecoming crowd gets to sing on the way out.

Opal hugs every Hall of Famer she can find. Tops sits quietly with his hot towel over his face for a full minute, then says, "Good game, Opal. Next year you're coming to my shop."

My call: Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders 28, Western Kentucky Hilltoppers 27.

UCF Knights vs Kansas Jayhawks prediction for Saturday, November 7: Knox Brevard-Stiles designs roller coasters in Orlando and has flown to Lawrence with a clipboard full of g-force charts, and Fitz Calloway, a Lawrence lifer, has just been told by his wife that the Jayhawks play football on Saturday.

"Rock Chalk," Fitz says. "Wait, it's FOOTBALL season?"

"It has been since September, Fitz," Knox says. "Your team is 3-5."

"In basketball we'd still be undefeated," Fitz says.

Here's the deal. Saturday is Kansas' Salute to Service game and its "Beak the Stigma" game, and it's the fifth home game of the season at David Booth Kansas Memorial Stadium. Kickoff is 3:45 p.m. ET. Kansas is 3-1 at home this year, and the last time the Jayhawks played there, they beat Baylor 25-24 on Homecoming on Oct. 24, coming back from 11 points down in the fourth quarter.

"Eleven points in the fourth quarter," Knox says. "That's a launch coaster. Zero to sixty."

"I watched the end of that one," Fitz says. "Somebody told me it was on."

Knox has his own coaster story. UCF beat BYU 39-31 in overtime on Oct. 24. Then the Knights went home against Baylor and lost 9-41. Up the lift hill, then straight down.

"That's not a ride," Fitz says. "That's a malfunction."

"It's a lesson in physics," Knox says. "What goes up comes down hard."

Fitz insists on giving Knox the full tour. He points out every concession stand, especially the one where he plans to spend most of the second quarter.

"You know there's a game going on during all this," Knox says.

"I've heard rumors," Fitz says. "Somebody said there's a scoreboard and everything."

"There is," Knox says. "And it counts by sevens, not twos."

Now the football.

Knox goes first, flipping through his clipboard. Keyone Jenkins has thrown for 1,181 yards and 11 touchdowns. Duke Watson leads the ground game with 597 yards. Josh Derry has 37 catches for 428 yards. UCF scores 29.8 a game. On defense, Tackett Curtis leads with 48 tackles and Isaiah Nixon has 2.5 sacks.

"Jenkins is a smooth operator," Knox says. "When he's on, it's a ten-car train with no wobble."

"Against Baylor he threw for 82 yards," Fitz says.

"Every coaster has a maintenance day," Knox says.

Fitz takes over, confused but loyal. Isaiah Marshall has 1,506 passing yards with 11 touchdowns. Cole Ballard threw for 285 at TCU last week, though Kansas lost 16-22. Dylan Edwards leads the backs with 573 yards. Nik McMillan has 466 receiving yards on just 25 catches, which Fitz says is like a guard who only shoots threes. Trey Lathan has 55 tackles. Leroy Harris III has 3.5 sacks.

"McMillan's a sharpshooter," Fitz says. "Catch, go, gone."

"That's a good ratio," Knox says. "I respect the engineering."

Kansas scores 29.1 a game and gives up 23.8. UCF gives up 25.2. Knox notes that these teams have met before. Kansas won 51-22 in 2023 and 27-20 last year.

"Two straight," Fitz says. "Is that good in football?"

"It's good in anything, Fitz," Knox sighs.

Here's how it plays out in Lawrence. The Salute to Service crowd fills the stands early, and Kansas comes out fast with Marshall finding McMillan deep. UCF answers, because Jenkins and Watson are too good to stay quiet. It's a back-and-forth game, a real wooden coaster, all rattle and noise. Edwards grinds out the clock in the fourth quarter, and Lathan makes the stop that ends UCF's last drive.

Knox folds up his clipboard and says it was a good ride. Fitz checks his phone to see when basketball starts.

My call: Kansas Jayhawks 29, UCF Knights 25.

display.fanatic_story:
Rice Owls vs North Texas Mean Green prediction for Saturday, November 7: Odalys Chen-Moreau, a Rice PhD student who carries a notebook full of footnotes, has driven up to Denton for Homecoming, and Grady Mayhew-Ochoa, a Denton jazz drummer, is tapping out a beat on the hood of her car before she has even parked.

"Is that a samba?" Odalys asks.

"It's the Mean Green fight tempo," Grady says. "Very fast. You'll see."

Here's the deal. This is the 80th annual Homecoming at North Texas. The Mean Green have held a Homecoming every season since 1946. This is just the third time Rice has been the Homecoming opponent. North Texas is 53-25-1 all-time on Homecoming and has won 7 of its last 9. Kickoff is 4:00 p.m. ET at DATCU Stadium.

"Eighty years," Odalys says. "Now that's a sample size I respect."

"You hear that?" Grady says. "She respects something."

Odalys reminds him that Rice has its own Homecoming crowd back in Houston, and that the Marching Owl Band would turn this whole parade into a skit. Grady says he would pay good money to see that, and he means it, and he would bring his own snare drum to join in.

Now the football.

Grady goes first, drumming on a cooler lid. Tayven Jackson has thrown for 2,577 yards with 22 touchdowns and only 5 interceptions. Last week he threw for 404 yards in a 48-41 win over Florida Atlantic. Jahiem White has run for 1,054 yards and 13 touchdowns, and he went for 193 against the Owls from Boca. Justin Stevenson has 50 catches for 781 yards and 8 touchdowns. North Texas scores 43.8 a game.

"That's bebop," Grady says. "Four hundred yards. A drum solo every drive."

"Correlation is not causation," Odalys says. "But I admit that's a lot of yards."

Odalys flips open her notebook. Jacurri Brown leads Rice with 669 rushing yards and has thrown for 478. But the headline is Gael Ochoa. At Florida Atlantic, Ochoa ran 12 times for 259 yards and 4 touchdowns. Rice lost that one 49-51, which Odalys describes as "statistically devastating." Jordan Clark leads the receivers with 257 yards. AJ Brown has 59 tackles, and Chibby Nwajuaku has 2 sacks.

"Twelve carries, 259 yards," Odalys says. "N is too small. But it's a very exciting N."

"That's a great solo," Grady says. "But can he play a full set?"

Here's the honest part. Rice is 1-7. North Texas is 6-2. The Mean Green give up 31.9 a game, so Rice can score. But the Owls give up 31.8, and North Texas has been scoring in bunches. Last year North Texas won 56-24, and the Mean Green are 7-1 against Rice since 2016.

"Seven and one," Grady says. "That's a pretty steady groove."

"Eight games," Odalys says. "Still small. I'm writing it down anyway."

Zakye Barker has 62 tackles for North Texas, and Davion Rhodes has 4 sacks. Grady says Barker plays like a bass player, never flashy, always there.

Here's how it plays out in Denton. The Homecoming crowd is loud early, and Jackson hits Stevenson for a long score in the first quarter. White adds two short touchdowns. Rice answers with Ochoa and Brown running hard, and the Owls hang around for a while. But North Texas just keeps pushing the tempo, and by the fourth quarter the Mean Green are playing in double time. Barker makes a stop on fourth down to end Rice's last real drive.

Odalys closes her notebook and admits the sample is getting bigger. Grady hands her a pair of drumsticks and tells her to count it off.

My call: North Texas Mean Green 42, Rice Owls 24.

"Bagpipes, barbecue and a parade," Champ says. "Y'all don't do anything halfway."

"Wait until you hear the Sound of the South," Marlo says. "That band will rattle your peaches."

Champ says he'll take the barbecue first and the bagpipes second. Marlo says that's the right order.

Now the football.

Champ goes first, standing up like he's still in the backfield. Louisiana Tech is 6-2. The Bulldogs score 32.6 a game and give up only 20.9. Blake Baker has thrown for 1,327 yards with 13 touchdowns and just 1 interception. Jalen Mickens leads the receivers with 43 catches for 618 yards. And then there's Alonzo Jackson Jr., who has 7 sacks and 57 tackles.

"Jackson is a wrecking ball," Champ says. "I'd have loved to block for a guy like that. Or better, not block against him."

"One interception all year?" Marlo asks.

"One," Champ says. "Baker takes care of the ball like I take care of my peach trees."

Last week the Bulldogs won 35-20 at South Alabama. Champ has the box score folded in his shirt pocket.

Marlo takes over, cracking a peanut. Troy is 4-4, but the Trojans just won 24-21 in overtime at James Madison with Tucker Kilcrease at quarterback. "Donnie Smith has as many sacks as your guy," Marlo says.

"He does," Champ admits. "That's a fair fight."

"And Troy is 3-1 at home," Marlo adds, and Champ nods along.

These two teams haven't met since 2016, so there is no fresh grudge. Champ says that's good, because he'd rather make friends over barbecue.

The queen is crowned at the break with Louisiana Tech in front. Troy fights back in the second half, Griffin running hard and Jones making stops, but Jackson Jr. comes up with a sack on Troy's final drive.

Marlo hands Champ the last of the boiled peanuts. Champ hands Marlo a jar of peach preserves. Both of them agree it was a good day in Troy.

Vanderbilt vs Mississippi State prediction, pick against the spread and over/under for Homecoming in Starkville: Mississippi State has spent the week of Nov. 1 through Nov. 8 telling everybody There's No Place Like State, and the Saturday payoff is a 4:15 PM ET kickoff at Davis Wade Stadium with the crowd asked to wear maroon. My side is Mississippi State Bulldogs −3, my call on points is Over 48.5, and my score is Mississippi State Bulldogs 32, Vanderbilt Commodores 23.

Pippa Ashcroft has the economist's case for the Commodores. "We're 3-5, but Junior Sherrill has 706 receiving yards, and Jared Curtis threw for 247 and two scores at Kentucky. We score 22.8 a game. Dogs that bark late can still get bit."

Wade Pettus answers from the feed-store notebook he keeps in his jacket. "Vandy is 0-5 in the league and gives up 30.2 a game. Ole Miss hung 52 on y'all. Homecoming crowd, maroon everywhere, and we have Fluff Bothwell with 563 rushing yards and Anthony Evans III with 666 receiving."

Here is why I lay the three. Both teams are sliding, but Vanderbilt's slide has more holes in it. The Commodores have lost five in a row, giving up 21, 38, 52, 31 and 34 along the way, and Curtis has 8 interceptions to go with his 8 touchdown throws. Mississippi State's offense has gone quiet over the last month, with 0 at LSU and 3 at Texas, and Kamario Taylor has not been the Bulldog with the most throws in any of the last three games. Still, the Bulldogs scored 62, 38, 41 and 31 when they had their footing in September, and this is the softest defense they have seen since then.

The risk is plain. If the quarterback spot stays unsettled, a 15-23 day like the one against Oklahoma is on the table, and Vanderbilt has enough throwing game to sneak out of town. DraftKings opened Mississippi State −3 and it has not moved.

On points, DraftKings opened 48.5 and held. Vanderbilt allows 30.2 and Mississippi State allows 28.1. The two meetings in this series since 2020 went 24-17 and 45-6. My 32 and 23 come to 55, well clear of 48.5.

The room is close to one voice. The Formula has Mississippi State 31-23, takes the Bulldogs −3 and likes the Over. Next Man Up has Mississippi State 33-23, takes the Bulldogs −3 and likes the Over. In The Trenches sees the trenches even and has no side, and it reads sides only with no score this week. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick. Letdown Watch has no score this week.

Pippa says she will sing the Commodores home on the drive up the Natchez Trace no matter what. Wade says the cowbells will drown her out before the second quarter.

display.fanatic_story:
Vanderbilt vs Mississippi State prediction for Homecoming in Starkville: the cowbells come out Saturday at Davis Wade Stadium at 4:15 PM ET, and the whole town has been told what to wear. Maroon. Head to toe, if you can manage it, because Mississippi State has spent Homecoming week reminding everybody that There's No Place Like State.

I asked two people who see this one from opposite porches to walk me through it.

Pippa Ashcroft studies economics in Nashville and hums country hooks under her breath when she is nervous. She was humming before I finished saying hello. Wade Pettus has a poultry-science degree from Mississippi State and keeps the Bulldogs' throwing game charted on feed-store receipts, folded into a stack in his shirt pocket.

"Y'all have the theme down," Pippa said. "No place like State. I'll give you that. It's the only place in the league where I can hear my own heartbeat over a cowbell."

Wade grinned. "That's the point. Homecoming week ran from the first of the month through the eighth. Friday night the Diamond Dawg Classic is out at Dudy Noble Field, with Will Clark and Rafael Palmeiro managing. Then the True Maroon Trek. Breakfast with Royalty had chicken biscuits. We do the week right."

"Chicken biscuits," Pippa said. "You would bring up chickens."

He shrugged. "Professional pride."

Here is where the two of them landed on football, and it is a matchup of two teams trying to remember how September felt.

Vanderbilt won its first three, then lost five in a row. The Commodores are 3-5 and 0-5 in league play, scoring 22.8 points a game and giving up 30.2. The losses read Auburn 15-21, Georgia 14-38, Ole Miss 17-52, Arkansas 21-31 and Kentucky 17-34.

"The Auburn game still hurts," Pippa said. "Six points. Then Georgia, then the Ole Miss game I won't talk about. But look at Jared Curtis at Kentucky. Twenty-seven of thirty-six for 247 and two touchdowns. He is figuring it out."

Curtis has 1,489 yards this year with 8 touchdowns and 8 interceptions, and that even split is the whole Vanderbilt story in one stat. Junior Sherrill is the reason the throwing game works at all, with 706 receiving yards and 4 touchdowns, and he had 8 catches for 78 at Kentucky. Sedrick Alexander leads the rushing with 274 yards and 5 scores. On defense, CJ Heard has 60 tackles and Nick Rinaldi has 3.5 sacks.

Wade pulled out a receipt. "Now mine. We were 4-0. Beat UL Monroe 62-13, won at Minnesota, won at South Carolina 41-34, beat Missouri 31-24. Kamario Taylor was throwing it all over the yard."

"And then?" Pippa asked, sweetly.

"And then Alabama, 23-56. LSU, 0-31. Oklahoma, 15-23. Texas, 3-31." He folded the receipt back up. "Rough month."

Mississippi State is 4-4, scoring 26.6 and allowing 28.1. Taylor has 1,460 yards, 17 touchdowns and only 4 interceptions, but Parker Puckett took the most throws at LSU and against Oklahoma, and AJ Swann did at Texas, going 12 of 15 for 97. Fluff Bothwell has 563 rushing yards, Anthony Evans III has 666 receiving yards, Tyler Lockhart has 48 tackles and Jaray Bledsoe has 3.5 sacks.

"So who is your quarterback Saturday?" Pippa asked.

"Whoever it is, he gets to throw against a defense that gave up 52 to Ole Miss," Wade said. "That changes the whole night. The last month we played four ranked-looking giants. Vanderbilt is a different kind of Saturday."

Pippa sang a verse of something about a dirt road and a broken heart. Then she said, "Your last two in this series were 24-17 and 45-6. I know. I looked it up so you wouldn't get to tell me."

"I was going to tell you anyway."

The way I see it, the game turns on whether Mississippi State's offense wakes up in front of its own people. Four straight weeks against Alabama, LSU, Oklahoma and Texas would flatten anybody. Vanderbilt's defense is the softest group the Bulldogs have faced since September, and a Homecoming crowd in maroon is going to be loud from the opening kick.

Vanderbilt can score enough to keep it honest. Curtis and Sherrill will make plays. But the Commodores have not stopped anybody in five weeks, and I don't see that changing in Starkville with the cowbells going.

Pippa said she would hum the Commodores home on the drive back up the Natchez Trace whatever happens. Wade said he would save her a chicken biscuit.

My call: Mississippi State Bulldogs 32, Vanderbilt Commodores 23.

Rutgers vs Wisconsin prediction, pick against the spread and over/under for Heroes Day at Camp Randall: Wisconsin opens its doors to veterans at 4:15 PM ET in Madison, and the Badgers are laying a big number to a Rutgers team that just played Michigan to a touchdown. My side is Rutgers Scarlet Knights +17.5, my call on points is Over 45.5, and my score is Wisconsin Badgers 33, Rutgers Scarlet Knights 18.

Vinny Scolari drove in from Exit 9 and grades trenches the way he grades boardwalk arm-wrestlers, by who blinks first. "Seventeen and a half? We just lost 21-28 to Michigan. We won 37-30 at Maryland. KJ Duff has 774 receiving yards and 9 touchdowns. Nobody blinks first here."

Lars 'Brat' Ellefson played fullback for the Badgers and still wears the cheese wedge to every home game. "Wisconsin gives up 17.1 a game. We went to Happy Valley and won 24-20. We beat USC 24-7. And we've won the last four of these, 31-17, 52-3, 24-13 and 42-7."

Both of them have a point, and that is why I want the points. Wisconsin's offense has been a sometime thing. The Badgers were shut out 0-30 at Iowa and scored 7 at UCLA, and Colton Joseph has thrown for 66, 58 and 90 yards in three of his last four games. He leads the team in both throwing yards at 1,346 and rushing at 371. That is a defense-first team that wins 24-20 and 24-7, not one that wins by three scores every week.

Rutgers has warts. The Scarlet Knights give up 32.6 a game and lost 15-47 to Indiana and 14-42 at Northwestern. But they score 27.8, Antwan Raymond has 733 rushing yards, and Duff can flip a game on one catch. Against Michigan, AJ Surace hit only 3 of 12 throws and they still had a chance late.

On points, my 33 and 18 add to 51, past 45.5. Wisconsin's scoring defense is the reason the Over is not easy, but Rutgers has allowed 28 or more in seven of its eight games, and the Badgers have hit 31 or more three times.

The room is in agreement on the side. The Formula has Wisconsin 32-19, takes Rutgers +17.5 and likes the Over. Next Man Up has Wisconsin 34-17, takes Rutgers +17.5 and likes the Over. In The Trenches takes Rutgers +17.5 and likes it, and it reads sides only with no score this week. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick. Letdown Watch has no score this week.

Vinny says Jersey guys do not need three touchdowns of cushion, just three hours of stubborn. Brat says the cheese wedge has seen worse.

display.fanatic_story:
Rutgers vs Wisconsin prediction for Heroes Day at Camp Randall: Saturday at 4:15 PM ET, Madison turns its home game into a salute to veterans, and Rutgers walks into the middle of it carrying a long trip and a short memory of last week.

Camp Randall carries that weight well. There is a free Salute to Veterans Tailgate at Camp Randall Memorial Park, with replica gear on loan from the Wisconsin Veterans Museum, and the new Camp Randall Veterans Memorial Plaza is open for people to walk through before kickoff.

I sat down with two guys who could not be more different if they tried.

Vinny Scolari is from off Exit 9 of the Turnpike. He grades blockers the way he grades arm-wrestling on the boardwalk, by watching who blinks. Lars Ellefson, who everybody calls Brat, played fullback for the Badgers and owns a foam cheese wedge older than some of the current roster.

"Heroes Day is a good day," Vinny said. "My uncle did twenty years. I'll be at the tailgate looking at the old helmets. Then I'll be in the stands looking at us get no respect."

Brat laughed. "You get respect. You just don't get wins in Madison. Four meetings, four Wisconsin wins. 31-17, 52-3, 24-13, 42-7."

"Fifty-two to three was 2021. Different guys."

That is true. This Rutgers team is 2-6, and it is a strange 2-6. The Scarlet Knights score 27.8 points a game and allow 32.6. They lost 21-37 to UMass, which hurts to type, and 21-28 at Boston College. Then they gave USC everything in a 35-42 loss, beat Howard 58-7, got run over 15-47 by Indiana, won 37-30 at Maryland, lost 14-42 at Northwestern and then played Michigan close in a 21-28 loss last Saturday.

"The Michigan game is the one," Vinny said. "AJ Surace went 3 for 12 and we still almost had it. Jourdin Houston caught one ball and took it 80 yards for a score. That's Jersey. One shot."

Dylan Lonergan leads the team with 1,066 throwing yards and 10 touchdowns, and Surace has taken the most throws in three of the last four games. Antwan Raymond is the workhorse with 733 rushing yards and 6 scores, and he ran for 85 against Michigan. KJ Duff is the guy you build the night around, with 774 receiving yards and 9 touchdowns. Sekou Kromah has 3 sacks and Chris Joines leads with 41 tackles.

Brat had his own list. "Wisconsin is 5-3. We give up 17.1 a game. We won 24-20 at Penn State. We beat USC 24-7. We beat Michigan State 31-3."

"And Iowa?" Vinny asked.

Brat looked at the cheese wedge for a while. "Zero to thirty. We don't discuss it."

The Badgers score 23.6 a game, which tells you everything about how they win. Colton Joseph is the whole offense. He has 1,346 throwing yards and 11 touchdowns, and he is also the leading rusher at 371 yards. Tyrell Henry is the top receiver at 397. The defense is the real show, with Cooper Catalano at 75 tackles and Sebastian Cheeks at 6 sacks.

"Here's my problem," Vinny said. "Joseph threw for 66 at UCLA and 58 against USC and 90 at Iowa. You can't throw it? We'll put nine guys in the box and make you."

"We beat USC throwing for 58," Brat said. "That's the Wisconsin way. Run it, hit you, run it again."

I asked them about the veterans plaza. Both of them got quiet. Brat said he walked through it on a weeknight and stayed longer than he planned. Vinny said his uncle would have liked the replica gear more than the football.

So here is how I see the game. Wisconsin's defense should win the day. Rutgers has allowed 28 or more in seven of eight games, and the Badgers at home on a big emotional Saturday will be ready. But the Wisconsin offense does not blow anyone out unless the other side hands it over. Raymond will move the chains some, Duff will get a couple of shots, and Rutgers will score enough to make the fourth quarter mean something.

Vinny promised to stay for the whole thing. Brat promised to lend him a cheese wedge if it gets cold.

My call: Wisconsin Badgers 33, Rutgers Scarlet Knights 18.

South Alabama vs Louisiana prediction, pick against the spread and over/under for Saturday at Cajun Field: Louisiana Salutes night in Lafayette kicks off at 5:00 PM ET, and the Ragin' Cajuns are laying more than a touchdown to a South Alabama team that has a habit of leaving this building happy. My side is South Alabama Jaguars +9.5, my call on points is Over 58.5, and my score is Louisiana Ragin' Cajuns 35, South Alabama Jaguars 26.

Azalea Fairhope-Grice builds Mardi Gras floats in Mobile and coached volleyball long enough to know a team that is about to crack. "We won 24-22 the last time we came to Lafayette, and 20-17 the time before. Nine and a half is a lot of float to push uphill."

Amélie 'Mimi' Fontenot keeps the books for half the dance halls in Acadiana and two-steps when she is right. "No. We won 31-22 last year, and this series since 2016 is 8 to 2 for us. Lunch Winfield has 470 rushing yards and 9 rushing touchdowns. You do not stop that man in our house."

Here is why I take the points. South Alabama scores 33.2 a game, and it has put up 52 on UL Monroe and 56 at Arkansas State. Keenan Phillips has 576 rushing yards and 6 touchdowns, and Jared Hollins has 1,195 throwing yards with only 4 interceptions. South Alabama vs Louisiana prediction for Louisiana Salutes night in Lafayette: the Ragin' Cajuns honor military members, veterans and first responders at Our Lady of Lourdes Stadium on Saturday, with a 5:00 PM ET kickoff, and South Alabama shows up as the one visitor in the league that seems to like it here.

The Jaguars have won their last two trips to Lafayette. They won 24-22 in 2024, and in 2022 they won 20-17 on a field goal at the very end. That is the part Mobile people bring up first. The part they bring up second, if you push, is that they are 2-5 all time at Cajun Field. Saturday is the 15th meeting between the two.

I got the two sides together on a phone call that ran long.

Azalea Fairhope-Grice builds Mardi Gras floats in Mobile and used to coach high school volleyball, which means she can spot a rotation breaking down from the cheap seats. Amélie Fontenot, Mimi to everyone, is an accountant in Lafayette who will tell you about zydeco whether you asked or not, and then she will show you the steps.

"I want to talk about 2022," Azalea said before I could ask anything.

"Of course you do," Mimi said. "One kick. Everybody in Mobile has it framed."

"We have two, actually. 2024 too. 24-22."

"And last year we won 31-22 and nobody in Mobile mentions it."

They are both right, and that is the fun of this one. Over the ten meetings from 2016 to 2025, Louisiana won eight and South Alabama won two. But the Jaguars' two came in the last four years, and both came in this building.

This South Alabama team is 4-4 and plays wide open. The Jaguars score 33.2 a game and allow 32.8. They beat Ohio 41-36, beat UL Monroe 52-35 and won a 56-49 shootout at Arkansas State. Then the month went sideways, with a 13-20 loss at Marshall and a 20-35 loss to Louisiana Tech last Saturday.

"The Marshall game was a volleyball match where nobody could serve," Azalea said. "Jared Hollins went 12 for 33. That is not him."

Hollins has 1,195 throwing yards with 9 touchdowns and 4 interceptions. Keenan Phillips is the lead back with 576 yards and 6 scores, Brendan Jenkins leads the receivers at 451 yards, and Cole Blaylock leads the defense with 46 tackles. Against Louisiana Tech, Anthony Eager caught 7 balls for 102 yards and 2 touchdowns, so there are weapons.

Mimi waited politely and then went to work. "Lunch Winfield."

That is the whole Louisiana argument in two words. Winfield has thrown for 1,452 yards and leads the team on the ground with 470 yards and 9 rushing touchdowns. The Cajuns are 5-3, scoring 30.1 a game and allowing just 21.2, with Jake St. Andre at 60 tackles.

"We lost by one at Louisiana Tech, 31-32," Mimi said. "We lost 31-35 at Southern Miss. Close ones. At home we beat Troy 33-6 and Arkansas State 23-20. Home is home."

"Home is also where you lost to us twice," Azalea said.

Mimi did a little two-step in her kitchen. I could hear it over the phone.

What about the salute? Both of them liked it. Azalea's father was a firefighter in Mobile, and she said a night that honors first responders hits her harder than any rivalry. Mimi said Lafayette does these nights right, with the crowd on its feet for every service member they bring onto the field.

Here is how I see the game. Louisiana's defense is the better group on the field, and Winfield is the best player in it. At home, with the crowd up for Louisiana Salutes, the Cajuns should take control by the third quarter. But South Alabama scores too much to go away. Phillips will find room, Hollins will hit enough shots, and the Jaguars will keep it a two-score game into the fourth.

Azalea says she has seen floats lose a wheel and still finish the parade. Mimi says she will be dancing on the way out either way.

My call: Louisiana Ragin' Cajuns 35, South Alabama Jaguars 26.
