display.fanatic_story:
Boise State vs Colorado State prediction for Saturday at Canvas Stadium: the Broncos bring a sea of blue to Fort Collins for a 6:00 PM ET kickoff, and the Rams get one more chance to prove their best night this season was not a fluke.

Boise State's schedule card for this road game says it in two words: Wear Blue. The Boise State alumni association is running a free Bronco Bash on South College Avenue before kickoff, from 3 to 5:30 PM ET, with music, game day swag and a drawing for a football signed by Coach Danielson for those who registered by Nov. 3. Colorado State, for its part, lists tailgating on the game page, and the parking office has event hours running all day out of the lots on West Pitkin Street.

I found two people to argue it out.

Thatcher Bluestem is from the Treasure Valley and has blue in every shade. Blue jacket, blue hat, blue socks. He says the blue turf is a lifestyle. Ansel Rimrock lives in Fort Collins and runs trails before work, which might explain why nothing seems to bother him.

"You know what I like about this trip?" Thatcher said. "We've been coming here forever and we've won almost every time. Eight of nine since 2016."

"The one we won was 31-30 in 2023," Ansel said. "I was there. I ran home."

"You ran home?"

"It was a good night. I had energy."

The series tilts hard to Boise, and last year's game was a 49-21 Broncos win. But this Colorado State team is a strange, fun mess. The Rams are 3-5 and score 35.5 points a game while allowing 42.4. They opened with a 35-13 win over Wyoming and a 58-24 win over Southern Utah. Then came four straight losses, including 45-59 at UTSA, 26-56 to Oregon State and 27-66 at Texas State. Then they turned around and beat San Diego State 56-49.

"That San Diego State game," Ansel said. "Hauss Hejny went 24 of 31 for 333 and 3 touchdowns. When he plays, we are a different team."

Hejny has 1,138 yards with 14 touchdowns and only 2 interceptions, and when he has taken the most throws the Rams have scored 35, 58, 56 and 14. Mel Brown leads the rushers with 454 yards, RJ Vick leads the receivers with 425, and Oumar Diomande is all over the field with 76 tackles.

"And the 14?" Thatcher asked.

"Utah State. Cold night. We don't talk about it."

Thatcher's turn. Boise State is 7-1 and ranked 20th. The Broncos score 35.9 a game and allow 23.6. The only loss was the opener, 27-34 at Oregon, and since then it has been seven wins in a row.

"Maddux Madsen has thrown 1 interception all year," Thatcher said. "One. In eight games. He has 1,681 yards and 15 touchdowns. And Dylan Riley has 1,049 rushing yards."

Riley has 9 rushing touchdowns, Rasean Jones leads the receivers with 554 yards, and Boen Phelps has 49 tackles. Jones had a monster night against Texas State last week with 9 catches for 117 yards and 3 touchdowns.

"About that Texas State game," Ansel said gently. "46-45."

Thatcher shrugged. "A win is a win."

"Texas State put 66 on us. They put 45 on you. That's not nothing."

He has a point. Boise won that one by one at home. The defense that gave up 23.6 a game over the season gave up 45 in a single afternoon. That is the opening Colorado State needs.

I asked Ansel what Fort Collins does on a game Saturday. He said the town walks to the stadium, the tailgates go all day, and the mountains sit right there to the west watching. Thatcher said he would be the guy in blue in the middle of it, being friendly about it.

So here is how I see it. Boise State is the better team, and Riley is going to run for a lot of yards against a defense that has given up 41 or more five times. Madsen will not give the ball away. The Broncos should be in control by halftime. But Colorado State scores too much at home to get run out of its own building, and Hejny will keep hitting Vick and Brown in the second half. The Rams keep it to a little over two scores.

Ansel says he will run home either way. Thatcher says he will wave from the bus.

My call: Boise State Broncos 44, Colorado State Rams 28.

Rhett Abernathy-Coyle grew up on a horse farm a short ride from Keeneland and reads a football game like a past-performance page. "Look at the form. Homecoming week has been busy. Monica Abbott is the grand marshal. The parade steps off Friday afternoon at 4 p.m. on Volunteer Boulevard and finishes at Neyland. The Europa and the Bull fountain on campus has been dyed orange, and there is Smokey's Howl on the schedule too. If you are a Kentucky fan, you are walking into an orange wall.

I got two old hands to talk it over.

Rhett Abernathy-Coyle grew up on a horse farm outside Lexington and still talks about football like a horseman sizing up a yearling. Earl Haskew, who everyone calls Rocky Top, was a long snapper for the Vols and brings a banjo to every tailgate he can find.

"Here's the thing nobody in Knoxville wants to hear," Rhett said. "We're 7-1. We're the better team on paper."

Earl plucked a string. "Paper doesn't play in Neyland."

Kentucky has been a story all fall. The Wildcats are 7-1, scoring 32.9 points a game and allowing 24.8. The only loss was 17-45 to Alabama back in September. Since then, it has been one escape after another. They won 35-34 in overtime at South Carolina, then 35-34 in overtime against LSU the next week. Then they went to Oklahoma and won 21-13, and beat Vanderbilt 34-17.

"Kenny Minchey has thrown one interception all year," Rhett said. "One. He has 1,755 yards and 14 touchdowns. He doesn't panic."

That is the heart of the Kentucky case. CJ Baxter leads the rushers with 487 yards and 8 touchdowns, Kenny Darby is the top receiver at 507 yards, Grant Godfrey has 72 tackles and Mi'Quise Humphrey-Grace has 5 sacks.

Earl put the banjo down for this part. "Tennessee is 6-2. We give up 16.2 a game. We held Alabama to 10 points at home. We lost to Texas by three and at South Carolina by three. That's it."

He's right about that. The two Tennessee losses were 17-20 to Texas and 24-27 at South Carolina. The Vols score 32.2 a game. DeSean Bishop is the engine, with 957 rushing yards and 11 touchdowns, and he carried 32 times for 120 yards at South Carolina. Mike Matthews leads the receivers with 528. On defense, Tyree Weathersby has 7 sacks and Amare Campbell has 52 tackles.

"What about the quarterback?" Rhett asked.

George MacIntyre has taken over the throwing, with 728 yards. Faizon Brandon took the most throws in the first four games and MacIntyre has done it since.

"George doesn't need to be a hero," Earl said. "Hand it to Bishop. Let the defense work. That's how we beat Alabama 26-10."

Rhett had one more card to play. "Two overtime wins. You know what that tells me? We don't lose close games."

"You know what it tells me?" Earl said. "You're lucky."

My call: Tennessee Volunteers 30, Kentucky Wildcats 23.

display.fanatic_story:
Sam Houston vs Jacksonville State prediction for Homecoming in Jacksonville, Alabama: the theme on campus is Cocky Reigns Supreme, the parade comes first, and then the Gamecocks take Burgess-Snow Field at AmFirst Stadium against Sam Houston at 7:00 PM ET.

Jax State calls itself The Friendliest Campus in the South, and Homecoming is when it tries hardest to prove it. There are tailgates and reunions all day, including the Golden Gamecocks Reunion for the old grads. During the game, the school will recognize its 2026 Alumni of the Year winners along with the Homecoming Queen, King and Court. Cocky, the mascot, gets top billing for once.

I brought in two people who know their regions.

Lem Coxwell teaches history in Walker County, Texas, and will tell you a tall tale about Sam Houston the man before he will tell you anything about Sam Houston the football team. Burl Ashcraft-Neeley cooks barbecue in Calhoun County, Alabama, and has opinions about pork shoulder that he shares freely.

"I'll be honest with you," Lem said. "It has been a long fall in Huntsville."

It has. The Bearkats are 1-7. They score 18.0 points a game and allow 25.1. The only win was 59-0 over Nicholls in September. But it hasn't been all blowouts. They lost 21-24 at Troy to open the year, 17-23 to Tulsa and 24-30 to New Mexico State.

"Then the offense went cold," Lem said. "Three points at Liberty. Three against Western Kentucky. Three at Missouri State. I have told some tall tales in my classroom, and none of them were as hard to explain as that."

Landyn Locke leads the throwing with 1,653 yards and 12 touchdowns, though DJ Bailey took the most throws at Missouri State and went 20 of 35 for 258. Tim Burns Jr. leads the receivers with 392 yards, and Alton McCaskill leads the ground game with 232. The defense has been the steady part. Dean Ford has 47 tackles and Josh Alexander-Felton has 4 sacks.

Burl had a rib in one hand and a list in the other. "We're 6-2. We give up 19.9 a game. And we just went to Las Cruces and shut out New Mexico State, 24-0."

Jacksonville State scores 26.9 a game and wins tight. After a 7-33 loss at North Dakota State and a 49-7 win over Eastern Kentucky, the Gamecocks lost 27-29 in overtime at Ohio. Then they won five straight, by scores of 31-27, 23-13, 27-26, 27-24 and 24-0.

"Caden Creel," Burl said. "That's the show. He has 1,741 throwing yards and 713 rushing. He's like a good smoker. Steady heat."

Deondre Johnson leads the receivers at 438 yards, and Caleb Nix leads the defense with 54 tackles.

Lem pointed out the history. "We beat them 42-7 in 2021."

"And we won the last three," Burl said. "35-28, 21-11 and 29-27."

"All close."

"All ours."

That back-and-forth is the game in a nutshell. Jax State wins, but it rarely runs away from anybody. Sam Houston's defense is good enough to keep things from getting silly, but the Bearkats have to find some points from somewhere.

I asked Burl about Homecoming. He said the parade goes through campus, the families set up early, and the smell of smoke hangs over the whole place by noon. Lem said he has never been, but he figures any town that names its stadium field after two people instead of one has a story worth hearing.

Here is how I see it. Jacksonville State on Homecoming, with Creel running and throwing, should control this from the second quarter on. The Gamecocks' defense is coming off a shutout, and the Bearkats have scored 3 points in three of their last four. But this Jax State team has not blown many people out, and Sam Houston's defense will make it work for every score. Creel gets his yards, the Gamecocks pull clear in the second half, and the Bearkats get a couple of late scores to make it look respectable.

Lem says he will have a new tall tale either way. Burl says the shoulder will be ready at halftime.

My call: Jacksonville State Gamecocks 30, Sam Houston Bearkats 15.

Georgia vs Ole Miss prediction for Saturday night in Oxford: the Rebels and Bulldogs meet at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium at 7:30 PM ET, and Ole Miss has already turned the whole week into a contest. It is called Beat Week, and it runs from Monday, Nov. 2, through Saturday, Nov. 7.

Here is how it works. Ole Miss and Georgia are racing to see which school can collect the most charitable gifts before kickoff. Every gift of $5 or more counts as one point, no matter the size, so a $5 gift counts the same as a $5,000 one. Georgia has the bigger alumni base, so Ole Miss is asking every fan to make three gifts to three things they love about the place, maybe a school, a scholarship and the Pride of the South Marching Band. Three gifts, three points. The school even pointed out that the Rebels beat Georgia in the Sugar Bowl in January and would like a second win over the Bulldogs this year.

I talked it through with two people who see this game in very different light.

Thad Okafor-Brandt is a DJ on a college station who plays indie records nobody else has heard of and spends his off nights watching defensive film. Langston Fairbanks lives in Oxford, wears seersucker well past the season for it and will quote Faulkner at you whether or not you have asked.

"I already made my three gifts," Langston said. "School of Law, a scholarship and the band. That's three points."

"That's very Oxford of you," Thad said.

"Faulkner said the past is never dead. It's not even past. That is this series."

He is not wrong. The last four meetings have swung back and forth. Ole Miss won 45-14 in 2016 and 28-10 in 2024. Georgia won 52-17 in 2023 and 43-35 last year.

Georgia comes in at 7-1 and ranked second in the country. The Bulldogs score 41.0 points a game and allow just 14.9. They beat Oklahoma 41-13, won 20-17 at Alabama and beat Florida 27-8 last Saturday. The one loss was 24-27 to Auburn.

"Watch the Georgia defense on film," Thad said. "It's like a perfect record with one scratch. Auburn found the scratch. Alabama almost did."

Gunner Stockton has 1,671 yards, 16 touchdowns and 4 interceptions, though he threw for only 101 against Florida. Dwight Phillips Jr. leads the rushers with 415 yards, Craig Dandridge leads the receivers with 349, and Raylen Wilson leads the defense in both tackles, with 51, and sacks, with 4.

Ole Miss is 6-2 and ranked 12th, scoring 37.1 a game and allowing 24.0. The Rebels opened by beating Louisville 41-38, then beat LSU 32-24 at home. They lost 28-52 at Florida and 27-34 at Texas. But at home they have been very good, beating Missouri 31-3 and Auburn 45-15 last week.

"Trinidad Chambliss is the whole thing," Langston said. "He has 2,189 yards and 18 touchdowns. Deuce Alexander has 669 receiving yards. When the Grove is full and the sun goes down, this place is a different stadium."

"Chambliss also has 8 interceptions," Thad said. "Three at Texas. Georgia's defense eats that up."

That's the matchup. Ole Miss throws it all over the place, and Georgia's defense is the best it has seen. The Rebels also have a defense with some bite, with Blake Purchase at 4.5 sacks and Keaton Thomas at 52 tackles.

I asked them both how they want Saturday to feel. Thad said he wants a game he can play back like a great record. Langston said he wants the Hotty Toddy to ring out under the lights at the end of the fourth quarter, with the Beat Week scoreboard settled too.

Here is how I see it. Georgia is the better team on paper, with the better defense and more depth. But this is a night game in Oxford, and Ole Miss has been very good at home. Chambliss will make big plays and a couple of mistakes. Stockton will be careful and get it done late. It comes down to one drive, and Georgia has the last one.

Thad says he will play the deep cuts all the way home. Langston says the ending will be long and close, like a Faulkner sentence.

My call: Georgia Bulldogs 31, Ole Miss Rebels 30.

display.fanatic_story:
Colorado vs Arizona State prediction for Family Weekend in Tempe: Saturday is a double celebration at Mountain America Stadium, with Arizona State honoring its Salute to Service week and welcoming families for Family Weekend, and the Sun Devils and Buffaloes kick off at 7:30 PM ET.

The day begins with Sparky's Touchdown Tailgate at College Avenue and 6th Street, the free pregame party ASU throws before every home game. It opens 2.5 hours before kickoff, with games and live entertainment for the whole family. This week it doubles as a thank-you to service members, and it should be packed with parents in maroon and gold visiting their kids for the weekend.

I sat down with two people who could not be more different.

Moss Feldstein studies physics in Boulder, plays hacky sack between classes and does his serious thinking in a hammock below the Flatirons. Skylar Vanterpool is from Tempe, is finishing a master's in sports science and carries a stopwatch everywhere.

"I'm coming in hot," Moss said. "We just beat Kansas State in overtime. Momentum is a physical quantity. Look it up."

"I measure things for a living," Skylar said. "Your momentum is one game."

Colorado is 3-5. The Buffaloes score 21.0 points a game and allow 29.4. They won 14-13 at Georgia Tech to open the year and beat Weber State 52-21. Then came five losses in a row: 7-41 at Northwestern, 13-23 at Baylor, 7-29 to Texas Tech, 24-27 to Utah and 24-57 at Oklahoma State. Then the 27-24 overtime win over Kansas State.

"Richard Young ran 24 times for 120 yards and 2 touchdowns against K-State," Moss said. "That is a young man finding his orbit."

Isaac Wilson has handled the throwing since late September, with 1,164 yards, 7 touchdowns and 7 interceptions. Joseph Williams is the go-to target with 732 receiving yards and 5 scores. On defense, Lamont Lester Jr. has 5 sacks, and Gideon Lampron leads the team with 81 tackles.

Skylar clicked the stopwatch. "Arizona State is 4-4. We score 29.5 and allow 29.5. Perfectly balanced, which I appreciate."

The Sun Devils have been up and down. They crushed Morgan State 70-7, lost 20-48 at Texas A&M, beat Kansas 24-17, lost 19-55 to Baylor, beat Hawai'i 30-12, lost 25-53 at Texas Tech, beat Kansas State 28-17 and lost 20-27 at BYU last week.

"Win, lose, win, lose," Moss said. "You're a sine wave."

"And this is a win week," Skylar said.

Cutter Boley leads the team with 1,360 throwing yards and 13 touchdowns, though Mikey Keene and Jake Fette have taken the most throws in the last three games. Reed Harris is the headliner with 804 receiving yards and 8 touchdowns. Cardae Mack leads the ground game with 523 yards, and Owen Long has 72 tackles.

Then there is the history, which is about as even as it gets. Over the eight meetings since 2016, each side has won four. Colorado won 27-24 in 2023. Arizona State won 42-17 last year.

"Forty-two to seventeen," Skylar said. "I timed the drive home. It felt short."

"That was a different team," Moss said. "We have Joseph Williams now."

I asked both of them about the weekend. Skylar said the family is flying in for Family Weekend, and the first stop is the tailgate. Moss said Boulder fans travel well to Tempe in November because nobody wants to miss a warm night.

Here is how I see it. Both defenses give up a lot, and both teams are capable of a big play on any snap. Colorado has real momentum, and Young gives the Buffaloes a ground game they did not have a month ago. But the Sun Devils at home, on a family night with the crowd behind them, have been a different team. Harris will make a couple of big catches, Mack will grind out the tough yards, and Arizona State pulls away late by a score.

Moss says momentum is conserved. Skylar says she has the stopwatch to prove otherwise.

My call: Arizona State Sun Devils 30, Colorado Buffaloes 24.

Louisville vs Georgia Tech prediction for Dodd After Dark: Georgia Tech is turning Saturday night into an event at Bobby Dodd Stadium at Hyundai Field, with a 7:30 PM ET kickoff, a halftime fireworks show presented by Georgia Power and the school's annual Military Appreciation Day all wrapped into one.

The Jackets are pulling out the stops for this one. Remaining tickets were marked down to half price, and there is a Buy One, Give One offer so fans can send local military personnel and veterans to the game. A wide range of events is planned to thank people who served. And then, at halftime, the sky over Midtown lights up.

I found two people to give me both sides.

Bianca Thornberry hosts a Kentucky Derby party every May in Louisville that people plan their springs around. She talks about football the way she talks about seating charts. Wendell Quist has an aerospace engineering degree from Georgia Tech and spends his free time tracking punt trajectories, which he will show you on his phone if you let him.

"I love a night game," Bianca said. "And I love fireworks. Georgia Tech is throwing a party, and Louisville is bringing the guests."

"That's generous," Wendell said. "Most guests don't score 52."

Louisville is 5-3 and the offense has been a joy to watch. The Cardinals score 40.4 points a game. They beat Villanova 59-13, SMU 41-31, Florida State 44-20, Syracuse 34-26 and Stanford 52-24 last week. But all three losses were heartbreakers: 38-41 to Ole Miss, 27-30 to Wake Forest and 28-31 at NC State.

"Every one of those was a coin flip," Bianca said. "That's the part that makes me crazy. We could be 8-0."

Lincoln Kienholz has 2,094 throwing yards, 12 touchdowns and only 3 interceptions. Isaac Brown ran 9 times for 139 yards and 3 touchdowns against Stanford and has 707 rushing yards on the year. Tre Richardson leads the receivers with 633, and he caught 10 balls for 140 last week. On defense, Tyler Thompson has 5.5 sacks and T.J. Capers has 57 tackles.

Wendell pulled up his phone. "Our side of it is harder. We're 2-6."

Georgia Tech scores 24.8 a game and allows 30.8. The losses include a 13-14 heartbreaker to Colorado to open the year, 24-45 to Tennessee, 27-34 at Stanford, 24-34 at Virginia Tech, 27-49 to Boston College and 11-34 at Pitt last Saturday. The wins came over Mercer and Duke, 44-11 and 28-25.

"Alberto Mendoza threw for 81 at Pitt," Wendell said. "That's a bad trajectory. But he has 1,795 yards on the year. Justice Haynes has 548 rushing yards. Jordan Allen has 543 receiving."

Tae Harris leads the Tech defense with 50 tackles, and Noah Carter has 3 sacks.

The history is a fun one. The four meetings are split two and two. Georgia Tech won 66-31 in 2018 and 46-27 in 2020. Louisville won 39-34 in 2023 and 31-19 in 2024.

"Sixty-six," Wendell said. "I think about it often."

"I don't," Bianca said.

I asked them both about the night itself. Wendell said he has done the math on the fireworks and is pretty sure the Georgia Power folks know what they are doing. Bianca said any night with fireworks and a crowd honoring veterans is a good night, even if her team is in the other jersey. Both said they will stand for the military salute.

So here is how I see it. Louisville has the better offense, and Brown and Kienholz are going to find room against a Tech defense that has given up 34 or more in five games. But this Louisville team has not run away from many good teams, and the Cardinals defense gives up 27.0 a game. Georgia Tech at home under the lights, with a crowd that showed up for the fireworks, will make some plays. Mendoza and Haynes get the Jackets into the twenties. The Cardinals pull away late.

Bianca says every good party runs long. Wendell says he will be watching the fireworks trajectories at halftime no matter what the scoreboard says.

My call: Louisville Cardinals 38, Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets 25.

display.fanatic_story:
Miami vs Notre Dame prediction for Saturday night in South Bend: the Hurricanes, 8-0 and rolling, walk into Notre Dame Stadium at 7:30 PM ET against a 7-1 Irish team that has been waiting for this one since the summer of 2025.

Game day on campus has its rituals, and they start early. At 5:15 PM ET the team leaves the Basilica of the Sacred Heart for the Victory March, with the Band of the Fighting Irish playing along the route and the Notre Dame Bagpipe Band leading the players into the stadium. At 5:30 the Trumpets at the Dome play outside the Main Building, and the Glee Club sings on Library Quad. At 6:00 the band plays its Concert on the Steps of Bond Hall, and the gates open, 90 minutes before kickoff. Later the band marches out to the stadium from the Main Building.

I talked it over with two very different people.

Javi Castillo, who everybody calls The Breeze, played defensive back at The U and still dresses like it is always July in Coral Gables, all linen and sunglasses. He moves between English and Spanish depending on how excited he is. Declan Moriarty-Chen is a grad student at Notre Dame who wears a sweater vest every single day and can tell you the schedule from any season you name.

"Oye, I love this place," Javi said. "The bagpipes, the band. Very classy. And then we beat you."

"You beat us last year," Declan said. "27-24. In Miami. This is our house."

That 2025 game is still sitting with both of them. Miami won it 27-24, and the series before that had a 30-27 Notre Dame win in 2016 and a 41-8 Miami win in 2017. Miami has two of the last three.

Miami is unbeaten for a reason. The Canes score 47.6 points a game and allow 17.8. They won 45-6 at Stanford, 77-7 over Florida A&M, 41-13 at Clemson and 52-23 over Pitt. The last few have been closer, a 43-35 overtime win over Florida State and a 38-35 win at North Carolina last week.

"Darian Mensah," Javi said, taking off his sunglasses for emphasis. "2,425 yards. 25 touchdowns. One interception. Uno."

Malachi Toney has 1,027 receiving yards and 13 touchdowns, including 2 scores at North Carolina. Javian Mallory leads the rushers with 495. On defense, Marquise Lightfoot has 7 sacks and Mohamed Toure has 44 tackles.

Declan was ready. "Notre Dame is 7-1. We score 40.4 a game and allow 13.4. The only loss was 24-28 at BYU."

The Irish have been close to perfect otherwise. They beat Wisconsin 41-13, Rice 52-0, Purdue 49-10, Stanford 58-7 and Navy 35-13 last week. CJ Carr has 1,849 yards, 18 touchdowns and 1 interception.

"Both quarterbacks have one interception," Declan said. "Somebody has to make the second one Saturday."

Nolan James Jr. leads the Irish ground game with 519 yards and 8 touchdowns. Jordan Faison is the top receiver at 497. Boubacar Traore has 3.5 sacks and Drayk Bowen has 45 tackles. Jerome Bettis Jr. had 78 receiving yards against Navy, which made Declan very happy.

"Florida State put 35 on you," Declan said. "North Carolina put 35 on you."

"And we still won," Javi said. "Así es."

I asked them about the night. Declan said the Victory March is the best part of any game day, and that walking behind the bagpipes with the crowd along the route makes the hair on his arms stand up. Javi said he would be there too, just to see it, even in the other team's colors. Then he said he was going to need a much warmer jacket than he brought.

Here is how I see it. Miami's offense is the best Notre Dame has seen, and Mensah is going to make his plays. But the Hurricanes defense has bent in the last three weeks, and the Irish at home at night, with James running behind that front and Carr protecting the ball, are a tough out. Notre Dame grinds out a couple of long drives in the second half, Miami answers with big plays, and the Irish hang on in the fourth quarter.

Javi says the breeze always gets through. Declan says South Bend in November has its own weather.

My call: Notre Dame Fighting Irish 33, Miami Hurricanes 29.

Kickoff is 7:30 PM ET Saturday at Michigan Stadium, and Ann Arbor is calling it a Blue Out and Military Appreciation Game, with a flag for every branch on the field during the anthem.

Shay Kowalczyk has lived in East Lansing her whole life and says a 2-6 team is the most dangerous animal in the state. Gus Hartwell says the Big House is sold out and the Spartans should enjoy the view.

"Blue Out," Shay says. "Great. We'll be the only thing in green that moves."

"You'll be the only thing in green that loses," Gus says.

Why the Spartans with the points: DraftKings opened this at Michigan −18.5 and it has come all the way down to 12.5. Michigan is 5-3 and scores 21.2 a game. Michigan State lost 37-38 in overtime to Illinois and 21-24 to Northwestern. Alessio Milivojevic has 1,263 yards, 7 touchdowns and only 3 interceptions. Twelve and a half is a lot of room for a Michigan team that grinds for everything.

display.fanatic_story:
Michigan State vs Michigan prediction for Saturday night in Ann Arbor: the Spartans walk into a sold-out Michigan Stadium at 2-6, the Wolverines sit at 5-3, and Shay Kowalczyk says that just means Michigan has more to lose. Gus Hartwell says that is the kind of thing people say on the drive down from East Lansing.

Kickoff is 7:30 p.m. ET, and this is the fifth straight night game in the series. Michigan has made it a Blue Out and Military Appreciation Game. Fans are asked to wear blue. Big flags for the six military branches go on the field for the anthem, American flags fly on all 16 flag poles around the stadium, and more than 150 Michigan football alumni will stand along the field as the team runs out. The Michigan Marching Band does an extended pregame show featuring "The Cake," and the team does the Wolverine Walk a little over two hours before kickoff.

"Blue Out," Shay says. "So a hundred thousand people dressed like a bruise."

"A hundred thousand people dressed like winners," Gus says. "Wear green if you want to be easy to find."

Gus has been going to games at the Big House since he was old enough to sit still, and he still stands up for the band every single time. Shay has a green flannel she wears to every road game in this rivalry and has never washed it during the season. She says that is tradition. Gus says it is a health concern.

Now the football.

Shay goes first. Alessio Milivojevic runs the Spartan offense, and he takes care of the ball. He has 1,263 yards with 7 touchdowns and 3 interceptions. Against Illinois he went 22 of 26 for 196 yards and 2 touchdowns, and Michigan State lost that one 37-38 in overtime. Against Northwestern it was 21-24. Jaziun Patterson leads the backs with 327 yards and 5 touchdowns. Chrishon McCray leads the receivers with 289 yards. On defense, Devin Vaught has 52 tackles and Eli Coenen has 3.5 sacks.

"We are not a 2-6 team," Shay says. "We are a team that lost close games to people who got lucky."

"You lost 3-31 at Wisconsin," Gus says.

"We don't talk about Madison," Shay says.

Gus takes his turn. Michigan has had two quarterbacks this year. Bryce Underwood leads the team with 924 yards, 5 touchdowns and 6 interceptions. Tommy Carr took over the last two games, and at Rutgers he went 22 of 27 for 266 yards and a touchdown in a 28-21 win. JJ Buchanan is the big target with 38 catches for 611 yards and 5 touchdowns. Jordan Marshall leads the backs with 319 yards. The defense is the real story. Michigan gives up 16.4 points a game. Troy Bowles has 57 tackles and John Henry Daley has 4 sacks.

"Our defense held Penn State to 18," Gus says. "Iowa got 20. Indiana got 13 in overtime. Nobody runs on us."

"Nobody scores for you either," Shay says. "You beat Western Michigan 13-12. In your own house."

"A win is a win," Gus says.

"Tell that to the 16 flag poles," Shay says.

History helps Gus. In the ten meetings from 2016 to 2025, Michigan won seven and Michigan State won three. Michigan won 31-20 last year and 24-17 the year before. But Shay remembers 2021, when the Spartans won 37-33, and 2020, when they won 27-24 in Ann Arbor.

"Every few years the green shows up," Shay says. "That's the deal in this state."

"Every few years the green gets lucky," Gus says.

Here's how it plays out. Michigan rides the run early, and the Big House gets loud when the defense forces a three-and-out on the first drive. Milivojevic makes the Wolverines work, hitting McCray on a couple of quick throws and keeping the chains moving into the second quarter. Michigan State gets a field goal and later a touchdown, and Shay jumps so high in the visitors' section that she loses her hat. But the Michigan defense tightens up after halftime. Carr finds Buchanan for the big play that finally breaks it open, and Michigan grinds out the clock in the fourth quarter.

Gus sings "The Victors" all the way to the parking lot. Shay says it is two scores and not a blowout, and that the green flannel stays unwashed until next year.

My call: Michigan Wolverines 26, Michigan State Spartans 15.

Iowa vs Northwestern prediction: we're taking Northwestern Wildcats −2.5, we're on the Over 44.5, and the final we're calling is Northwestern Wildcats 24, Iowa Hawkeyes 21. Kickoff is 7:30 PM ET Saturday at the new Ryan Field in Evanston, and it is Iowa's first trip into the rebuilt place.

Orrin Kalvelage has driven to Evanston from Iowa City more times than he can count and says the Hawkeyes always travel well to the North Shore. Ezra Lindqvist says that was fine when the stadium was a construction site. Now it is a fortress.

"New stadium, same Northwestern," Orrin says.

"Same Northwestern that has not lost at home this year," Ezra says.

Why Northwestern laying the points: DraftKings opened Northwestern −2.5 and the number has not moved off it. Aidan Chiles has 1,898 yards, 13 touchdowns and 1 interception. That is a quarterback who does not hand games away. Griffin Wilde has 761 receiving yards and went for 146 at Oregon. Northwestern scores 33.6 a game. Iowa allows 12.5, which is the best number on the field, but Iowa has played a softer path to get there. Northwestern lost 26-34 at Oregon and still threw for 281 yards. At home, with a field goal of cushion, we'll take the team with the better quarterback.

On the over/under, DraftKings opened at 42.5 and it climbed to 44.5. We're on the Over 44.5. Iowa scores 28.2 a game, and Hank Brown went 20 of 24 for 222 yards and 2 touchdowns last week. Northwestern scores in bunches at home. Both teams get into the 20s.

The room splits right down the middle on this one. The Formula lands on Iowa +2.5 and has it 24-22. Next Man Up takes Northwestern −2.5 and has it 24-20. In The Trenches is split and takes no side. The Formula lands on the Over. Next Man Up lands on the Under. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick. Series history is close. In the nine regular-season meetings since 2016, Iowa won five and Northwestern won four. Iowa won 40-14 the last time, but Ezra points out Northwestern won 21-20 in 2020 and 14-10 in 2018, and those are the games that look like this one.

"Iowa wins ugly," Orrin says. "That's the whole brand."

"Ugly doesn't work against a quarterback with one interception," Ezra says. "Bring a sweater. It's cold by the lake."

Iowa vs Northwestern prediction for Saturday night in Evanston: two 6-2 teams, a brand-new stadium, and two insiders who have not agreed on anything since the first week of September.

Orrin Kalvelage has had Iowa season tickets for longer than some of these players have been alive. He brings the same thermos to every road game. Ezra Lindqvist lives a short walk from the lake and spent the last two years watching cranes swing over the old site, waiting for the new Ryan Field to open.

It finally did. The new 35,000-seat Ryan Field opened last month after 2 2/3 years of construction, and Saturday is Iowa's first look at it. It is also the first time these two have met since 2024. While the new place was being built, Northwestern played its home games at Northwestern Medicine Field at Martin Stadium, right on the lakefront. Kickoff Saturday is 7:30 p.m. ET.

"Nice building," Orrin says. "Shame about the football."

"The football is 6-2," Ezra says. "Same as yours. And we haven't lost at home."

Orrin goes first. The Iowa defense is the whole story. The Hawkeyes allow 12.5 points a game. Cam Buffington leads them with 70 tackles, and Joseph Anderson has 4 sacks. On offense, Hank Brown has been steady with 1,190 yards, 8 touchdowns and 3 interceptions, and against Wisconsin he went 20 of 24 for 222 yards and 2 touchdowns. Kamari Moulton leads the backs with 541 yards. Tony Diaz leads the receivers with 461 yards.

"We beat Michigan in their own house 20-19," Orrin says. "We'll be fine in a stadium that still smells like paint."

Ezra has heard this speech before. His turn. Aidan Chiles is having the year of his life. He has 1,898 yards, 13 touchdowns and just 1 interception. He also runs. At Oregon last week he had 93 yards on the ground to go with 281 through the air. Griffin Wilde caught 5 balls for 146 yards in that game and has 761 on the season. Caleb Komolafe leads the backs with 618 yards. Braydon Brus does everything on defense, with 67 tackles and 4 sacks.

"We scored 26 at Oregon," Ezra says. "You'd be lucky to score 26 against a high school."

"We scored 30 against Wisconsin and they scored zero," Orrin says.

"Wisconsin scores zero against everybody," Ezra says.

History is close, too. In the nine meetings since 2016, Iowa won five and Northwestern won four. Iowa won the last one 40-14 in 2024. But Northwestern won 21-20 in 2020, 14-10 in 2018 and 38-31 in 2016. Ezra lists every one of them from memory. Orrin says he has blocked those out.

"You can't block out 2020," Ezra says. "It was one point."

"I can block out anything," Orrin says. "I'm from Iowa. We're patient people."

Here's how it plays out. The new stadium is loud from the opening kick, and it gets louder when Chiles scrambles for a first down on the opening drive. Iowa answers the way Iowa always does. Moulton runs it, Brown hits Diaz on third down, and the Hawkeyes keep the ball for what feels like a full quarter. The Iowa defense gets after Chiles and forces a punt or two. It is tight at the half.

In the second half, Chiles finds Wilde deep, and the crowd by the lake finally gets the moment it has been waiting two years for. Iowa comes back with a long drive and makes it a three-point game. The Hawkeyes get the ball back one more time, but Brus gets home on a big third down, and Northwestern holds on.

Orrin pours what is left in the thermos and says the new stadium has bad karma for visitors. Ezra says that is called a home team.

My call: Northwestern Wildcats 24, Iowa Hawkeyes 21.

display.fanatic_story:
Air Force vs Army prediction for Saturday night at West Point: the Falcons come east at 6-2, the Black Knights are 5-3 at home, and the Commander-in-Chief's Trophy is sitting right in the middle of Michie Stadium.

Marissa Okonkwo-Hale is a retired lieutenant colonel who flew for the Air Force and still salutes the Falcon on the helmet. Thaddeus Rourke is a retired Army captain who has not missed a home game at Michie in years and brings the same wool blanket every November.

This one is a night game, and that is a big deal in the Hudson Valley. It is Army's first night home game against Air Force since 2006. The first night game ever played at Michie Stadium was against Air Force in 1984, and Army won it 24-12. Thaddeus was there. He mentions it every time somebody stands still long enough.

"Forty years of telling the same story," Marissa says.

"It's a good story," Thaddeus says. "It ends 24-12."

The forecast calls for about 47 degrees with wind around 9 miles per hour. Thaddeus says that is football weather. Marissa says that is a reason to stay in Colorado.

Marissa goes first. Air Force is 6-2 and scores 29.2 points a game. The quarterback spot has moved around. Liam Szarka took most of the early snaps, then Evan Medders, then Howard Fisher IV. Medders leads the team in rushing with 490 yards and 6 touchdowns. Last week against UConn, the Falcons handed the ball to Kemper Hodges and let him go. He carried it 35 times for 200 yards and 4 touchdowns in a 35-26 win. On defense, Blake Fletcher has 79 tackles and Max Mustell has 3 sacks.

"We beat Navy 14-9," Marissa says. "We beat UNLV 41-31. We won in overtime at Nevada. This team finds a way."

"You lost 14-28 at Wyoming," Thaddeus says.

"Wyoming is at altitude," Marissa says. "Nobody likes it up there."

"You live at altitude," Thaddeus says.

Thaddeus takes his turn. Army runs through Cale Hellums. He has 874 rushing yards and 17 rushing touchdowns, which is the kind of number that ends arguments. He has also thrown for 462 yards. Army scores 33.6 a game. The Black Knights put up 56 on Florida Atlantic and 38 at Tulsa. Elijah Walton leads the defense with 55 tackles, and Victor Afolabi has 3 sacks.

Then there is last week. Army lost 22-49 at Memphis. Godspower Nwawuihe ran for 100 yards, but the defense had no answers.

"Memphis was one bad night," Thaddeus says.

"Forty-nine points is a lot of bad night," Marissa says.

History belongs to Army lately. In the ten meetings since 2016, Army won seven and Air Force won three. Army won 20-17 last year and 20-3 the year before. But Marissa reminds everyone that Air Force won 31-12 in 2016 and 13-7 in 2022, and that this rivalry tends to stay close.

"Seven of ten," Thaddeus says. "Write that on the trophy."

"The trophy has two academies on it already," Marissa says. "We beat the other one."

This game is also the middle step of the trophy chase. Air Force already beat Navy. Army plays Navy in the 127th Army-Navy Game on Dec. 12. If Army wins Saturday, everything rides on Philadelphia, and Thaddeus has already booked his hotel.

Here's how it plays out. Both teams run the ball, and the clock moves fast in the first half. Air Force gets the first score when Medders breaks a long run around the corner. Hellums answers with a touchdown of his own, and the cadets in the stands go wild. It stays close into the third quarter, with each offense putting together long drives that eat up time and patience.

In the fourth quarter, Army's defense finally gets a stop on a fourth down near midfield. Hellums takes over from there, running for one more score. Air Force answers late, but it is not enough.

Marissa says the Falcons will get their revenge next time. Thaddeus says he will bring the blanket.

My call: Army Black Knights 31, Air Force Falcons 25.

display.fanatic_story:
Oklahoma vs Florida prediction for Saturday night in Gainesville: the Sooners come in at 4-4, the Gators are 5-3 and ranked No. 25, and Ben Hill Griffin Stadium will be rocking under the lights.

Savannah Redbird-Lowe has had Oklahoma season tickets since she was a student in Norman. She drives a crimson pickup with a Sooner Schooner sticker on the back window. Dax Marchetti grew up a short drive from the Swamp, owns three different orange-and-blue jerseys, and says the heat and noise in Gainesville can break anybody.

This one is the Saluting Those Who Serve game. Florida will honor members of the armed forces, veterans and local first responders, and a ticket gets donated to a local military hero. Outside the O'Connell Center at Gate 2, there's a free Fan Fest that opens three hours before kickoff. Kickoff is 7:45 p.m. ET.

"Fan Fest," Savannah says. "Do they have barbecue?"

"They have everything," Dax says. "Come early."

These two have met before, but not often. Florida won 24-14 in January 2009. Oklahoma won 55-20 in December 2020. Savannah brings up the second one. Dax brings up the first one.

"That was the big one," Dax says.

"That was seventeen years ago," Savannah says. "Ours was more recent."

Savannah goes first. John Mateer is the leader in Norman. He has 1,835 yards, 13 touchdowns and 7 interceptions. Last week he went 26 of 43 for 244 yards and 2 touchdowns, but Oklahoma lost 25-42 to South Carolina. Isaiah Sategna III is the top receiver with 591 yards. Lloyd Avant leads the backs with 347 yards. On defense, Adepoju Adebawore has 4 sacks and Owen Heinecke has 63 tackles.

"We beat Texas," Savannah says. "27-24."

"We beat Texas too," Dax says. "27-24. In Austin."

"Same score?" Savannah says.

"Same score," Dax says. "Except ours was on their field."

Dax takes his turn. Florida has a first-year head coach in Jon Sumrall, and the Gators have been fun to watch. Aaron Philo threw for 1,367 yards before Tramell Jones Jr. took over the last two games. Against Texas, Jones went 22 of 35 for 155 yards and 2 touchdowns. Against Georgia, it was tougher. Florida lost 8-27. Jadan Baugh is the workhorse with 801 rushing yards and 13 touchdowns. Dallas Wilson leads the receivers with 417 yards. On defense, Jayden Woods has 4.5 sacks and Myles Graham has 55 tackles.

"Baugh is going to run all night," Dax says.

"We'll be ready," Savannah says.

"You gave up 42 to South Carolina," Dax says.

"So did you," Savannah says. "Almost. You gave up 38."

Florida has put up big numbers at home. The Gators scored 66 on Florida Atlantic, 52 on Campbell and 52 on Ole Miss. They also lost 17-45 at Missouri and 19-38 to South Carolina at home. Oklahoma lost 13-41 at Georgia and 13-21 to Kentucky.

Here's how it plays out. The Swamp is loud from the opening kick. Florida gets the ball first and Baugh runs right at the Sooners. He breaks a long run, and the Gators score early. Mateer answers. He hits Sategna for a big gain, then runs it in himself. It is tied after the first quarter.

The game goes back and forth. Florida takes the lead at halftime on another Baugh touchdown. In the third quarter, Mateer leads a long drive, and Oklahoma kicks a field goal. Jones finds a receiver deep in the fourth quarter, and Florida pulls ahead by two scores. Oklahoma answers with a late touchdown, but the Gators recover the onside kick and run out the clock.

Dax says the Swamp is undefeated at night. Savannah says that is not true, and that she will be back.

My call: Florida Gators 28, Oklahoma Sooners 23.

Liberty vs New Mexico State prediction: we're taking New Mexico State Aggies +17.5, we're on the Under 47.5, and the final we're calling is Liberty Flames 31, New Mexico State Aggies 16. Kickoff is 8:00 PM ET Saturday at Aggie Memorial Stadium in Las Cruces, and it is Homecoming for the Aggies.

Gideon Fairweather has followed Liberty from the old days in Lynchburg and says the Flames are the class of the league. Esperanza Lujan-Tafoya grew up a few miles from the stadium and says the class of the league has never had to play in front of an Aggie Homecoming crowd that is this hungry.

"Homecoming," Gideon says. "Nice of you to throw us a party."

"The party is for us," Esperanza says. "You're the entertainment."

Why the Aggies with the points: DraftKings opened this at Liberty −12.5 and it has moved all the way to 17.5. That is five extra points, and we will take them. Liberty is 7-1 and allows only 13.5 a game, but it has not been a blowout machine everywhere. It beat Gardner-Webb 24-23 and lost 13-20 at James Madison. Last year in this series Liberty won 30-27. The year before it was 30-24. New Mexico State has James Jones, who has 889 rushing yards and ran for 112 last week, and a ground game keeps the clock moving and the margin down.

On the over/under, DraftKings opened at 47.5 and it has not moved. We're on the Under 47.5. New Mexico State scored 0 against Jacksonville State last week and Adam Damante went 6 of 19 for 29 yards. The Aggies have a quarterback problem, and Liberty has a defense that can take advantage of it. Liberty gets into the 30s, and the Aggies run the ball and keep it under control.

The room is mostly with the Aggies on this one. The Formula lands on New Mexico State +17.5 and has it 31-16. Next Man Up lands on New Mexico State +17.5 and has it 30-16. In The Trenches is split and takes no side. The Formula lands on the Under. Next Man Up lands on the Under. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick. Letdown Watch has no score this week.

Deshawn Purdie is the reason Liberty is 7-1. He has 1,453 yards, 10 touchdowns and just 1 interception. He will make plays. But a 17.5-point spread on the road in a hostile Homecoming setting asks a lot. Liberty wins this game. It just doesn't run away from the Aggies.

"Seventeen and a half," Gideon says. "We'll get that by halftime."

"You will get a chill by halftime," Esperanza says. "Bring a jacket."

display.fanatic_story:
Liberty vs New Mexico State prediction for Saturday night in Las Cruces: the Flames come in at 7-1 and rolling, the Aggies are 3-5 and limping, and it is Homecoming and Ag Day at Aggie Memorial Stadium. Gideon Fairweather says that is nice for the alumni. Esperanza Lujan-Tafoya says that is the whole point.

Gideon has followed Liberty since the program was a small school on a hill in Lynchburg. He knows the fight song by heart and sings it in the car. Esperanza grew up in the Mesilla Valley, eats green chile with every meal, and has a red-and-white Aggies scarf she has worn to every Homecoming since high school. Kickoff is 8 p.m. ET, which is 6 p.m. out in the desert.

"Homecoming," Gideon says. "Who scheduled the Flames for Homecoming?"

"Somebody who likes a challenge," Esperanza says.

This series has history. The two teams have met nine times in the previous eight seasons, which is a lot for two schools that are not close to each other. Liberty has won four straight, including the 49-35 win in the 2023 Conference USA Championship. But Esperanza remembers 2022, when the Aggies beat Liberty 49-14. And 2018, when they won 49-41. Last year it was close, a 30-27 Liberty win.

"Two of nine," Gideon says. "You got two."

"We got two big ones," Esperanza says. "We'll take a third."

Gideon goes first. Deshawn Purdie is the best player on the field, and it is not close. He has 1,453 yards, 10 touchdowns and only 1 interception. Against FIU last week he went 16 of 19 for 227 yards in a 49-10 win. Kam Davis leads the backs with 603 yards and 7 touchdowns. Makai Jackson is the deep threat with 626 receiving yards and 5 touchdowns. On defense, Liberty allows 13.5 points a game. Derrell Farrar leads the team with 43 tackles, and Brenton Williams has 4 sacks.

"Our only loss was 13-20 at James Madison," Gideon says. "In the first week."

"You beat Gardner-Webb by one," Esperanza says. "Gardner-Webb."

"A win is a win," Gideon says.

Esperanza takes her turn, and she knows the Aggies have problems. The offense has struggled. Trey Hedden leads the team with 906 throwing yards, but Adam Damante has taken most of the snaps lately. Against Jacksonville State last week, Damante went 6 of 19 for 29 yards, and New Mexico State lost 0-24.

"Zero," Gideon says. "Your team scored zero."

"James Jones ran for 112," Esperanza says. "Look at that instead."

Jones is the real deal. He has 889 rushing yards on 139 carries this season. TK King leads the receivers with 307 yards. The defense has playmakers too. Gabe Peterson has 5.5 sacks, and Nick Session has 58 tackles.

The Aggies have shown what they can do. They beat Western Kentucky 34-13 and won 30-24 at Sam Houston. They also lost 18-42 to New Mexico, which still makes Esperanza angry.

"Don't bring up the Lobos," she says.

"I didn't," Gideon says.

"You were about to," Esperanza says.

Out in Las Cruces, the radio call is on 99.5 FM KXPZ, and Esperanza's grandfather will have it on in the garage, like he does every Homecoming.

Here's how it plays out. Liberty comes out fast. Purdie hits Jackson for a big gain on the first drive, and Davis punches it in. The Homecoming crowd goes quiet for a minute. Then the Aggies do what they do best. Jones runs it, and runs it again, and the Aggies grind out a long drive that ends with a field goal. Peterson gets to Purdie on a third down, and the crowd comes back to life.

In the second half, Liberty's defense makes it tough on the Aggie quarterback. The Flames add two more scores, but Jones keeps running hard into the fourth quarter, and the Aggies find the end zone late. Liberty wins it, but nobody in the stands goes home early.

Esperanza says she will remember every word Gideon said tonight. Gideon sings his fight song the whole way to the parking lot.

My call: Liberty Flames 31, New Mexico State Aggies 16.

Kickoff is 9:30 PM ET Saturday at Galaxy Stadium in Lubbock, where Texas Tech is calling it the Celebrate America Game.

Jolene Buckhannon has never missed a road trip she could drive to, and she says Lubbock is a drive if you love your team enough. Bodie Ratliff says nobody loves anything that much, and that the Red Raiders are going to make it a long ride home.

"Seventeen and a half," Jolene says. "In Lubbock. At night. We'll take it."

"You'll take it all the way back to Morgantown," Bodie says.

West Virginia scores 35.9 a game, and Michael Hawkins Jr. threw for 464 yards against Cincinnati in a 45-42 win. Cam Cook has 923 rushing yards. A team that scores like that can keep a three-score game from happening. Texas Tech also has a quarterback question. Thomas Castellanos took the most snaps last week with 144 yards and 2 touchdowns, after Will Hammond took them all year.

display.fanatic_story:
West Virginia vs Texas Tech prediction for Saturday night in Lubbock: the Mountaineers come in at 5-3 off a win at TCU, the Red Raiders are 7-1 and ranked No. 13, and it is the Celebrate America Game at Galaxy Stadium.

Jolene Buckhannon grew up in the hills outside Morgantown and still sings "Country Roads" every time she crosses into a new state. Bodie Ratliff is a Lubbock lifer who has a tortilla in his pocket on every home Saturday and says the wind on the South Plains is just weather to him.

"Nice of you to fly out," Bodie says.

"Nice of you to have a stadium we can find," Jolene says. "There's nothing else out here."

Texas Tech calls this one the Celebrate America Game. The school will recognize each branch of the military and its campus military and veterans programs throughout the night. Before the game, fans pack Raider Alley in the Engineering Key, which is free and open to the public, with live music, food, family activities and the Goin' Band from Raiderland. Raider Alley has been part of game day in Lubbock since 1994. Kickoff is 9:30 p.m. ET.

"Raider Alley," Jolene says. "Do they have pepperoni rolls?"

"They have better," Bodie says.

"Nothing is better," Jolene says.

Jolene goes first. West Virginia can score. The Mountaineers put up 35.9 points a game. Michael Hawkins Jr. has 1,598 yards with 11 touchdowns and only 2 interceptions. Against Cincinnati, he went 25 of 33 for 464 yards and 3 touchdowns in a 45-42 win. Cam Cook is a workhorse with 923 rushing yards and 7 touchdowns. DJ Epps is the big-play receiver with 556 yards on just 22 catches. On defense, Isaiah Patterson leads the team with 48 tackles.

"We beat TCU 24-20 on the road last week," Jolene says. "We're hot."

"You lost 31-52 to Arizona at home," Bodie says.

"Arizona was a bad day," Jolene says. "Everybody has a bad day."

Bodie takes his turn. Texas Tech is 7-1, and the only loss was 24-37 at Cincinnati. Will Hammond has led the team with 1,561 throwing yards, but Thomas Castellanos took the most snaps last week against Arizona and threw for 144 yards and 2 touchdowns in a 34-26 win. J'Koby Williams ran wild in that game with 175 yards. He has 794 on the season. Kenny Johnson leads the receivers with 548 yards. The defense is the real reason Texas Tech is ranked. A.J. Holmes Jr. has 7.5 sacks, and Austin Romaine has 66 tackles.

"Holmes is going to live in your backfield," Bodie says.

"Hawkins runs," Jolene says. "Good luck catching him."

The long history is close, but lately it has been all Texas Tech. In the ten meetings since 2016, Texas Tech won six and West Virginia won four. Last year Texas Tech won 49-0. The year before that it was 52-15.

"Forty-nine to nothing," Bodie says. "Remember that one?"

"I've moved on," Jolene says. "That was a different team."

"It was last year," Bodie says.

"Different team," Jolene says.

Jolene does have some old wins to point to. West Virginia won 48-17 in 2016, 46-35 in 2017 and 42-34 in 2018. She has those scores memorized and says them like a prayer.

Here's how it plays out. Galaxy Stadium is loud and the flags are out for Celebrate America. Texas Tech gets the ball first and Williams breaks a long run to set up the opening score. West Virginia answers right away. Hawkins finds Epps deep, and Cook finishes the drive. It is a shootout in the first half, and Jolene is on her feet in the visitors' section yelling about every flag.

Then Holmes takes over. He gets to Hawkins twice in the third quarter, and Texas Tech turns those stops into points. The Red Raiders pull away in the fourth. West Virginia keeps scoring, though, and Cook gets a late touchdown that makes Jolene feel a little better on the long drive home.

Bodie says the Red Raiders are headed somewhere special. Jolene says she will be singing "Country Roads" all the way home anyway.

My call: Texas Tech Red Raiders 41, West Virginia Mountaineers 24.

Fresno State vs Utah State prediction: we're taking Utah State Aggies +2.5, we're on the Under 41.5, and the final we're calling is Fresno State Bulldogs 21, Utah State Aggies 19. Kickoff is 9:30 PM ET Saturday at Maverik Stadium in Logan, where the Aggies are honoring military members and first responders.

Roz Ayala has been yelling at Fresno State games since the Bulldogs played in front of half-empty bleachers, and she says this is the best Fresno team in years. Hyrum Tolleson lives within walking distance of the stadium and says a cold November night in Cache Valley is where good California teams go to freeze.

"It's going to be cold," Roz says. "We have jackets."

"You have jackets for Fresno cold," Hyrum says. "That's not cold."

Why the Aggies with the points: DraftKings opened Fresno State −2.5 and it has not moved. Fresno State vs Utah State prediction for Saturday night in Logan: the Bulldogs come up from the Central Valley at 5-3, the Aggies are 3-5 but just beat Colorado State, and it is going to be cold on the hill at Maverik Stadium.

Roz Ayala has been going to Fresno State games since she was a kid, back when she sat on her dad's shoulders. She wears a red hoodie to every game, no matter how hot or cold it is. Hyrum Tolleson grew up in Cache Valley and walks to the stadium. He says anyone who needs a hoodie in November has never lived in Logan.

Saturday's game is about more than football. Utah State is honoring all military members and first responders. Kickoff is 9:30 p.m. ET, which is 7:30 p.m. in Logan, on Merlin Olsen Field at Maverik Stadium. Current Utah State students can get a free ticket, so the student section should be packed.

"Free tickets," Roz says. "That's the only way you can fill the place."

"We fill it fine," Hyrum says. "Just wait until you hear it."

Roz goes first. Fresno State's offense runs through Jayden Mandal. He has 1,595 throwing yards with 10 touchdowns and only 2 interceptions. Against Sacramento State he went 23 of 26 for 316 yards. Last week against Oregon State, he went 11 of 17 for 202 yards and 2 touchdowns in a 38-22 win. Bryson Donelson ran for 108 yards in that game and has 407 on the season. Josiah Freeman leads the receivers with 533 yards and caught 2 touchdowns last week. On defense, K'vion Thunderbird leads with 66 tackles, and Dylan Hampsten has 5 sacks.

"We beat Oregon State by 16," Roz says. "Oregon State scores a ton."

"You lost 0-39 at USC," Hyrum says.

"USC is USC," Roz says. "That was the first game."

Hyrum takes his turn, and he knows the Aggies have been up and down. Utah State has used two quarterbacks this year. Grady Brosterhous leads the team with 1,120 yards, 7 touchdowns and 6 interceptions. But McCae Hillstead took over last week and looked sharp. He went 17 of 22 for 173 yards in a 31-14 win over Colorado State. He also ran for 79 yards and a touchdown. Anthony Garcia was the hero of that game with 11 catches for 121 yards. Javen Jacobs leads the backs with 491 yards. Eli Wood leads the receivers with 479 yards and 5 touchdowns. On defense, Brevin Hamblin has 62 tackles, and Jordan Pendleton has 2.5 sacks.

"We lost to Washington by two," Hyrum says. "On the road. We beat Washington State by one. We lost to Texas State by three. We play everybody close."

"You lost to Idaho State," Roz says.

"We don't talk about that," Hyrum says.

History is pretty even. In the five meetings since 2016, Utah State won three and Fresno State won two. Utah State won 28-17 last year, and Hyrum has the program from that game framed in his basement. Fresno State won 37-32 in 2023 and 35-16 in 2020.

"Three to two," Hyrum says. "We're ahead."

"Not for long," Roz says.

Here's how it plays out. It is cold and the wind is blowing off the mountains. Fresno State gets the ball first, and Mandal hits Freeman on a quick throw to get the Bulldogs moving. The drive stalls and they kick a field goal. Utah State answers with Hillstead. He runs for a first down and then finds Garcia for a big gain. The Aggies kick a field goal of their own.

The game stays tight. Neither team can run away with it. Donelson breaks a long run in the third quarter to give Fresno State the lead. Hillstead finds Wood in the end zone to get Utah State back within two. The Aggies get one more chance late, but Thunderbird makes a big stop, and Fresno State holds on.

Roz takes off her hoodie and waves it over her head in the cold. Hyrum says she will regret that in the morning.

My call: Fresno State Bulldogs 21, Utah State Aggies 19.

Hawai'i vs UTEP prediction for Saturday night in El Paso: the Rainbow Warriors fly in at 2-6, the Miners are 1-7, and Kainoa Akana-Baird and Neto Galindo both say this is the most important game of the season.

Kainoa grew up on the windward side of O'ahu and has been following the Rainbow Warriors since he could say "Warriors." He packs a cooler of spam musubi for every road trip. Neto Galindo was born a few blocks from the Sun Bowl and has had the same seats under Franklin Mountain since he was in high school. He says nothing beats a night game in the desert.

This one has history. UTEP is hosting Hawai'i for the first time since Oct. 16, 2004, when the Miners won 51-20. Neto was there. He still has the ticket stub in his wallet.

"Twenty-two years," Kainoa says. "You've been waiting a while."

"I've been waiting for a rematch," Neto says. "Now I get one."

Kickoff is 9:30 p.m. ET, which is 7:30 p.m. in El Paso.

Kainoa goes first. Hawai'i has been through a rough year, but the Warriors just had their best game. Micah Alejado threw for 323 yards and 3 touchdowns in a 56-21 win at Northern Illinois. On the season, he has 2,186 yards, 9 touchdowns and 6 interceptions. He throws it a lot. He had 51 throws at Stanford and 49 at Arizona State. DeVon Rice ran for 3 touchdowns last week and has 385 yards on the season. Kainoa Carvalho leads the receivers with 399 yards.

"Carvalho," Kainoa says. "Same first name. Same greatness."

"Different player," Neto says.

On defense, Jamih Otis leads Hawai'i with 54 tackles, and Wynden Ho'ohuli has 2 sacks.

"We lost close games," Kainoa says. "San José State by four. Stanford by ten. We're better than 2-6."

"You lost to UNLV 6-21," Neto says.

"UNLV is good," Kainoa says.

Neto takes his turn, and he is honest about the Miners. UTEP is 1-7. The only win was 51-10 over Texas Southern. The Miners have given up 36.5 points a game. They lost 7-61 at New Mexico and 0-51 at Oklahoma. Last week they lost 7-31 at North Dakota State.

"It's been tough," Neto says. "But we're home."

UTEP has used two quarterbacks. EJ Colson Jr. has 687 throwing yards with 7 touchdowns and 5 interceptions. Raymond Moore III leads the team in rushing with 481 yards and has also played quarterback. Against Nevada he went 16 of 26 for 132 yards and 2 touchdowns. Last week he ran for 67 yards on just 3 carries. Kam Thomas leads the receivers with 283 yards. On defense, Sterling Miles has 3.5 sacks and Jayden Wilson has 47 tackles.

"Moore is the guy," Neto says. "Put the ball in his hands and let him go."

"Hawai'i will be ready," Kainoa says.

"Hawai'i hasn't been ready all year," Neto says.

Kainoa throws a spam musubi at him. Neto catches it and eats it.

Here's how it plays out. The Sun Bowl is not full, but the people who come are loud. Hawai'i gets the ball first, and Alejado goes to work. He hits Carvalho on a deep throw down the right side, and Rice punches it in. UTEP answers with Moore. He runs for a big gain on the first play, and the Miners get a field goal.

Alejado keeps throwing. Hawai'i scores twice more in the first half and takes a big lead into the break. The Miners don't quit, though. In the second half, Moore runs for a touchdown and Colson finds Thomas for another. UTEP gets within one score in the fourth quarter, and the Sun Bowl gets loud. But Rice puts it away late with a long run.

Kainoa says the Warriors will finish the season strong. Neto says he will be back in the same seats for the next one. They split the last spam musubi.

My call: Hawai'i Rainbow Warriors 29, UTEP Miners 20.

Texas State vs Oregon State prediction for Saturday night in Corvallis: the Bobcats come up from San Marcos at 4-4, the Beavers are 5-3, and it is the first-ever meeting between these two programs.

Yesenia Calderwood has lived in San Marcos for most of her life and floats the river every summer. She brings a maroon foam finger to every road game and refuses to put it down. Juniper Ostrowski grew up in the Willamette Valley, has had the same seats at Reser Stadium for years, and wears a bright orange rain jacket no matter what the sky says.

"First meeting," Yesenia says. "We're making history."

"You're making a long flight home," Juniper says.

Corvallis is ready for the newcomers. Before kickoff, the OSU Alumni Association runs Tailgate Town at the CH2M HILL Alumni Center from 4:30 p.m. until kickoff at 7:30 p.m. Pacific, which is 10:30 p.m. ET. There's barbecue from Pacific Northwest pitmasters, indoor games, photo spots and appearances from OSU Cheer and the OSU Marching Band.

"Barbecue," Yesenia says. "In Oregon."

"Pacific Northwest pitmasters," Juniper says. "It's good."

"I'm from Texas," Yesenia says. "I'll be the judge."

Yesenia goes first. Texas State can score. The Bobcats put up 38.1 points a game. Brad Jackson has 1,933 yards, 18 touchdowns and 5 interceptions. Last week he threw for 327 yards and 4 touchdowns at Boise State, and Texas State lost 45-46. Torrance Burgess Jr. has 922 rushing yards. Chris Dawn Jr. leads the receivers with 467 yards. On defense, Jayden Bradley has 56 tackles, and Tymere Jackson has 3.5 sacks.

"We lost by one at Boise," Yesenia says. "One point. On the blue turf."

"You lost 7-59 at Texas," Juniper says.

"Everybody loses at Texas," Yesenia says.

"We didn't play Texas," Juniper says.

"Lucky you," Yesenia says.

Juniper takes her turn, and she has a lot to work with. Braden Atkinson is putting up huge numbers. He has 2,977 yards, 25 touchdowns and only 2 interceptions. Against Colorado State he went 31 of 34 for 427 yards and 5 touchdowns. Against San Diego State it was 409 yards and 5 more touchdowns. Jesse Legree has 1,110 receiving yards and 14 touchdowns. AJ Newberry leads the backs with 465 yards. On defense, Takari Hickle has 6 sacks and Aiden Sullivan has 60 tackles.

"Atkinson is the best quarterback nobody talks about," Juniper says.

"You lost 22-38 at Fresno State last week," Yesenia says.

"Fresno State is tough at home," Juniper says.

The Beavers scored 66 on San Diego State and 56 at Colorado State. Texas State scored 66 on Colorado State and 63 on Incarnate Word. These teams can both put up points in a hurry.

"Sixty-six," Juniper says. "We did it first."

"We did it too," Yesenia says. "So it doesn't count."

Here's how it plays out. It is a cool night at Reser. Oregon State gets the ball first, and Atkinson finds Legree deep for a touchdown on the opening drive. Texas State answers right away. Jackson hits Dawn for a big gain, and Burgess runs it in. That's how the whole first half goes. Score, answer, score, answer.

In the second half, Hickle gets to Jackson on a big third down, and Oregon State gets a field goal out of it. Atkinson finds Legree again early in the fourth quarter to stretch the lead. display.fanatic_story:
Wyoming vs UNLV prediction for Saturday night at Allegiant Stadium: both teams are 5-3, the Cowboys come down from the high plains off a win over Air Force, and the Rebels are home under the roof.

Colter Sprague runs cattle outside Laramie and drives a pickup with more than a few miles on it. He wears a brown-and-gold flannel shirt to every Wyoming game, even indoors. Monroe-Kalani grew up in the desert and has had UNLV season tickets since the Rebels moved into Allegiant Stadium. She likes her football warm, dry and loud.

The stadium is calling this one a visit from a longtime rival, and the game opens the final month of the regular season. The Rebels close at home on Nov. 28 with the in-state rivalry game against UNR, so this is the warmup for that. Kickoff is 10:30 p.m. ET.

"Indoor football," Colter says. "It's not real football."

"It's real football with air conditioning," Monroe-Kalani says.

"Football needs weather," Colter says.

"Football needs fans," Monroe-Kalani says. "We have a stadium full of them."

Colter goes first. Wyoming is all about Tyler Hughes. He leads the team in throwing and rushing. He has 1,131 throwing yards and 605 rushing yards with 6 rushing touchdowns. Against Air Force last week, he ran for 146 yards in a 28-14 win. Jake Wilson is his go-to target, a tight end with 242 yards. On defense, Esaia Bogar has 4.5 sacks and Ethan Stuhlsatz has 59 tackles.

"Hughes runs like a bull," Colter says. "You'll need three guys to bring him down."

"He also throws interceptions," Monroe-Kalani says. "Seven of them."

"He throws touchdowns too," Colter says.

"Five," Monroe-Kalani says.

Monroe-Kalani takes her turn. Jackson Arnold runs the UNLV offense, and he has been sharp. He has 1,655 yards, 13 touchdowns and 4 interceptions. Last week against Northern Illinois he went 20 of 30 for 269 yards and 3 touchdowns in a 31-24 win. Jai'Den Thomas ran for 114 yards in that game and has 657 on the season. Kayden McGee caught 5 balls for 112 yards and has 442 on the season. On defense, Jake Pope leads with 70 tackles and Tre Fulton has 3.5 sacks.

"Arnold is a gamer," Monroe-Kalani says.

"Arnold lost to Air Force," Colter says. "41-31."

"And you beat them last week," Monroe-Kalani says. "I know. You told me four times."

"Five times," Colter says.

History is close. In the five meetings since 2016, UNLV won three and Wyoming won two. UNLV won 31-17 last year and 34-14 in 2023. Wyoming won 45-14 in 2020 and 53-17 in 2019. And then there is 2016, when UNLV won 69-66 in one of the wildest games either side has ever played.

"Sixty-nine to sixty-six," Colter says. "Nobody played defense."

"Nobody had to," Monroe-Kalani says. "We won."

Here's how it plays out. Wyoming gets the ball first and grinds. Hughes runs, then runs again, and the Cowboys eat up half the first quarter before kicking a field goal. UNLV answers fast. Arnold finds McGee deep, and Thomas punches it in.

The game settles down from there. Wyoming keeps running Hughes, and Bogar gets to Arnold once in the second quarter. But UNLV's defense holds up. Pope makes a big stop on fourth down near midfield, and the Rebels turn it into a touchdown. In the second half, Thomas wears down the Wyoming defense, and UNLV pulls away. Hughes gets a late touchdown, but it is too little, too late.

Colter says the Cowboys will be ready when the Rebels come to Laramie, and that he hopes it snows. Monroe-Kalani says she will bring a jacket and win anyway.

My call: UNLV Rebels 26, Wyoming Cowboys 16.
